verses.translation: Thou, Agni gainest for the loudly-praising priest the highest wealth, the object of a man's desire. Thou art called Father, caring even for the weak, and wisest, to the simple one thou teachest lore.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Agni, the man who giveth guerdon to the priests, like well-sewn armour thou guardest on every side. He who with grateful food shows kindness in his house, an offerer to the living, is the type of heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Pardon, we pray, this sin of ours, O Agni,--the path which we have trodden, widely straying, Dear Friend and Father, caring for the pious, who speedest nigh and who inspirest mortals.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: As erst to Manus, to Yayati, Angiras, so Angiras! pure Agni! come thou to our hall Bring hither the celestial host and seat them here upon the sacred grass, and offer what they love.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: By this our prayer be thou, O Agni, strengthened, prayer made by us after our power and knowledge. Lead thou us, therefore, to increasing riches; endow us with thy strength-bestowing favour.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I will declare the manly deeds of Indra, the first that he achieved, the Thunder-wielder. He slew the Dragon, then disclosed the waters, and cleft the channels of the mountain torrents.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He slew the Dragon lying on the mountain: his heavenly bolt of thunder Tvashṭar fashioned. Like lowing kine in rapid flow descending the waters glided downward to the ocean.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Impetuous as a bull, he chose the Soma, and in three sacred beakers drank the juices. Maghavan grasped the thunder for his weapon, and smote to death this firstborn of the dragons.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When, Indra, thou hadst slain the dragons’ firstborn, and overcome the charms of the enchanters, Then, giving life to Sun and Dawn and Heaven, thou foundest not one foe to stand against thee.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Indra with his own great and deadly thunder smote into pieces Vṛitra, worst of Vṛitras. As trunks of trees, what time the axe hath felled them, low on the earth so lies the prostrate Dragon.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He, like a mad weak warrior, challenged Indra, the great impetuous many-slaying Hero. He, brooking not the clashing of the weapons, crushed—Indra’s foe—the shattered forts in falling.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Footless and handless still he challenged Indra, who smote him with his bolt between the shoulders. Emasculate yet claiming manly vigour, thus Vṛitra lay with scattered limbs dissevered.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: There as he lies like a bank-bursting river, the waters taking courage flow above him. The Dragon lies beneath the feet of torrents which Vṛitra with his greatness had encompassed.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Then humbled was the strength of Vṛitra’s mother: Indra hath cast his deadly bolt against her. The mother was above, the son was under, and like a cow beside her calf lay Dânu.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Rolled in the midst of never-ceasing currents flowing without a rest for ever onward, The waters bear off Vṛitra’s nameless body: the foe of Indra sank to during darkness.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Guarded by Ahi stood the thralls of Dâsas, the waters stayed like kine held by the robber. But he, when he had smitten Vṛitra, opened the cave wherein the floods had been imprisoned.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: A horse's tail wast thou when he, O Indra, smote on thy bolt; thou, God without a second, Thou hast won back the kine, hast won the Soma; thou hast let loose to flow the Seven Rivers.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Nothing availed him lightning, nothing thunder, hailstorm or mist which he had spread around him: When Indra and the Dragon strove in battle, Maghavan gained the victory for ever.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Whom sawest thou to avenge the Dragon, Indra, that fear possessed thy heart when thou hadst slain him; That, like a hawk affrighted through the regions, thou crossedst nine-and-ninety flowing rivers?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Indra is King of all that moves and moves not, of creatures tame and horned, the Thunder-wielder. Over all living men he rules as Sovran, containing all as spokes within the felly.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Come, fain for booty let us seek to Indra: yet more shall he increase his care that guides us. Will not the Indestructible endow us with perfect knowledge of this wealth, of cattle?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I fly to him invisible Wealth-giver as flies the falcon to his cherished eyrie, With fairest hymns of praise adoring Indra, whom those who laud him must invoke in battle.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Mid all his host, he bindeth on the quiver: he driveth cattle from what foe he pleaseth: Gathering up great store of riches, Indra. be thou no trafficker with us, most mighty.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou slewest with thy bolt the wealthy Dasyu, alone, yet going with thy helpers, Indra! Far from the floor of heaven in all directions, the ancient riteless ones fled to destruction.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Fighting with pious worshippers, the riteless turned and fled, Indra! with averted faces. When thou, fierce Lord of the Bay Steeds, the Stayer, blewest from earth and heaven and sky the godless.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: They met in fight the army of the blameless: then the Navagvas put forth all their power. They, like emasculates with men contending, fled, conscious, by steep paths from Indra, scattered.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Whether they weep or laugh, thou hast o'erthrown them, O Indra, on the sky's extremest limit. The Dasyu thou hast burned from heaven, and welcomed the prayer of him who pours the juice and lauds thee.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Adorned with their array of gold and jewels, they o'er the earth a covering veil extended. Although they hastened, they o'ercame not Indra: their spies he compassed with the Sun of morning.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: As thou enjoyest heaven and earth, O Indra, on every side surrounded with thy greatness, So thou with priests bast blown away the Dasyu, and those who worship not with those who worship.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: They who pervaded earth's extremest limit subdued not with their charms the Wealth-bestower: Indra, the Bull, made his ally the thunder, and with its light milked cows from out the darkness.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The waters flowed according to their nature; he raid the navigable streams waxed mighty. Then Indra, with his spirit concentrated, smote him for ever with his strongest weapon.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Indra broke through Ilibisa's strong castles, and Susna with his horn he cut to pieces: Thou, Maghavan, for all his might and swiftness, slewest thy fighting foeman with thy thunder
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Fierce on his enemies fell Indra's weapon: with. his sharp bull he rent their forts in pieces. He with his thunderbolt dealt blows on Vrtra; and conquered, executing all his purpose.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Indra, thou helpest Kutsa whom thou lovedst, and guardedst brave Dagadyu when he battled, The dust of trampling horses rose to heaven, and Svitra's son stood up again for conquest.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Svitra's mild steer, O Maghavan thou helpest in combat for the land, mid Tugra's houses. Long stood they there before the task was ended: thou wast the master of the foemen's treasure.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Ye who observe this day be with us even thrice: far-stretching is you bounty, Asvins and your course. To you, as to a cloak in winter, we cleave close: you are to be drawn nigh unto us by the wise.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Three are the fellies in your honey-bearing car, that travels after Soma's loved one, as all know. Three are the pillars set upon it for support: thrice journey ye by night, O Asvins, thrice by day.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thrice in the self-same day, ye Gods who banish want, sprinkle ye thrice to-day our sacrifice with meath; And thrice vouchsafe us store of food with plenteous strength, at evening, O ye Asvins, and at break of day.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thrice come ye to our home, thrice to the righteous folk, thrice triply aid the man who well deserves your help. Thrice, O ye Asvins, bring us what shall make us glad; thrice send us store of food as nevermore to fail.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thrice, O ye Asvins, bring to us abundant wealth: thrice in the Gods' assembly, thrice assist our thoughts. Thrice, grant ye us prosperity, thrice grant us fame; for the Sun's daughter hath mounted your three-wheeled car.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thrice, Asvins, grant to us the heavenly medicines, thrice those of earth and thrice those that the waters hold, Favour and health and strength bestow upon my son; triple protection, Lords of Splendour, grant to him.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thrice are ye to be worshipped day by day by us: thrice, O ye Asvins, ye travel around the earth. Car-borne from far away, O ye Nasatyas, come, like vital air to bodies, come ye to the three.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thrice, O ye Asvins, with the Seven Mother Streams; three are the jars, the triple offering is prepared. Three are the worlds, and moving on above the sky ye guard the firm-set vault of heaven through days and nights.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Where are the three wheels of your triple chariot, where are the three seats thereto firmly fastened? When will ye yoke the mighty ass that draws it, to bring you to our sacrifice. Nasatyas?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Nasatyas, come: the sacred gift is offered up; drink the sweet juice with lips that know the sweetness well. Savitar sends, before the dawn of day, your car, fraught with oil, various-coloured, to our sacrifice.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Come, O Nasatyas, with the thrice-eleven Gods; come, O ye Asvins, to the drinking of the meath. Make long our days of life, and wipe out all our sins: ward off our enemies; be with us evermore.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Borne in your triple car, O Asvins, bring us present prosperity with noble offspring. I cry to you who hear me for protection be ye our helpers where men win the booty.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: AGNI I first invoke for our prosperity; I call on Mitra, Varuna, to aid us here. I call on Night who gives rest to all moving life; I call on Savitar the God to lend us help.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Throughout the dusky firmament advancing, laying to rest the immortal and the mortal, Borne in his golden chariot he cometh, Savitar, God who looks on every creature.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The God moves by the upward path, the downward; with two bright Bays, adorable, he journeys. Savitar comes, the God from the far distance, and chases from us all distress and sorrow.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: His chariot decked with pearl, of various colours, lofty, with golden pole, the God hath mounted, The many-rayed One, Savitar the holy, bound, bearing power and might, for darksome regions.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Drawing the gold-yoked car his Bays, white-footed, have manifested light to all the peoples. Held in the lap of Savitar, divine One, all men, all beings have their place for ever.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Three heavens there are; two Savitar's, adjacent: in Yama's world is one, the home of heroes, As on a linch-pin, firm, rest things immortal: he who hath known it let him here declare it.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He, strong of wing, hath lightened up the regions, deep-quivering Asura, the gentle Leader. Where now is Surya, where is one to tell us to what celestial sphere his ray hath wandered?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The earth's eight points his brightness hath illumined, three desert regions and the Seven Rivers. God Savitar the gold-eyed hath come hither, giving choice treasures unto him who worships.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The golden-handed Savitar, far-seeing, goes on his way between the earth and heaven, Drives away sickness, bids the Sun approach us, and spreads the bright sky through the darksome region.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May he, gold-handed Asura, kind Leader, come hither to us with his help and favour. Driving off Raksasas and Yatudhanas, the God is present, praised in hymns at evening.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Savitar, thine ancient dustless pathways are well established in the air's mid-region: O God, come by those paths so fair to travel, preserve thou us from harm this day, and bless us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: WITH words sent forth in holy hymns, Agni we supplicate, the Lord Of many families who duly serve the Gods, yea, him whom others also praise.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Men have won Agni, him who makes their strength abound: we, with oblations, worship thee. Our gracious-minded Helper in our deeds of might, be thou, O Excellent, this day.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thee for our messenger we choose, thee, the Omniscient, for our Priest. The flames of thee the mighty are spread wide around: thy splendour reaches to the sky.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Gods enkindle thee their ancient messenger,--Varuna, Mitra, Aryaman. That mortal man, O Agni, gains through thee all wealth, who hath poured offerings unto thee.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou, Agni, art a cheering Priest, Lord of the House, men's messenger: All constant high decrees established by the Gods, gathered together, meet in thee.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: In thee, the auspicious One, O Agni, youthfullest, each sacred gift is offered up: This day, and after, gracious, worship thou our Gods, that we may have heroic sons.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To him in his own splendour bright draw near in worship the devout. Men kindle Agni with their sacrificial gifts, victorious o'er the enemies.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Vrtra they smote and slew, and made the earth and heaven and firmament a wide abode. The glorious Bull, invoked, hath stood at Kanva's side: loud neighed the Steed in frays for kine.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Seat thee, for thou art mighty; shine, best entertainer of the Gods. Worthy of sacred food, praised Agni! loose the smoke, ruddy and beautiful to see.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Bearer of offerings, whom, best sacrificing Priest, the Gods for Manu's sake ordained; Whom Kanva, whom Medhyatithi made the source of wealth, and Vrsan and Upastuta.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Him, Agni, whom Medhyatithi, whom Kanva kindled for his rite, Him these our songs of praise, him, Agni, we extol: his powers shine out preeminent.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Make our wealth perfect thou, O Agni, Lord divine: for thou hast kinship with the Gods. Thou rulest as a King o'er widely-famous strength: be good to us, for thou art great.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Stand up erect to lend us aid, stand up like Savitar the God: Erect as strength-bestower we call aloud, with unguents and with priests, on thee.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Erect, preserve us from sore trouble; with thy flame burn thou each ravening demon dead. Raise thou us up that we may walk and live: so thou shalt find our worship mid the Gods.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Preserve us, Agni, from the fiend, preserve us from malicious wrong. Save us from him who fain would injure us or slay, Most Youthful, thou with lofty light.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Smite down as with a club, thou who hast fire for teeth, smite thou the wicked, right and left. Let not the man who plots against us in the night, nor any foe prevail o'er us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Agni hath given heroic might to Kanva, and felicity: Agni hath helped our friends, hath helped Medhyatithi, hath helped Upastuta to win.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: We call on Ugradeva, Yadu, Turvasa, by means of Agni, from afar; Agni, bring Navavastva and Brhadratha, Turviti, to subdue the foe.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Manu hath stablished thee a light, Agni, for all the race of men: Sprung from the Law, oil-fed, for Kanva hast thou blazed, thou whom the people reverence.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The flames of Agni full of splendour and of might are fearful, not to be approached. Consume for ever all demons and sorcerers, consume thou each devouring fiend.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: SING forth, O Kanvas, to your band of Maruts unassailable, Sporting, resplendent on their car
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: They who, self-luminous, were born together, with the spotted deer, Spears, swords, and glittering ornaments.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: One hears, as though 'twere close at hand, the cracking of the whips they hold They gather glory on their way.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Now sing ye forth the God-given hymn to your exultant Marut host, The fiercely-vigorous, the strong.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Praise ye the Bull among the cows; for 'tis the Maruts' sportive band: It strengthened as it drank the rain.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Who is your mightiest, Heroes, when, O shakers of the earth and heaven, Ye shake them like a garment's hem?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: At your approach man holds him down before the fury of your wrath: The rugged-jointed mountain yields.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: They at whose racings forth the earth, like an age-weakened lord of men, Trembles in terror on their ways.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Strong is their birth: vigour have they to issue from their Mother; strength, Yea, even twice enough, is theirs.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: And these, the Sons, the Singers, in their racings have enlarged the bounds, So that the kine must walk knee-deep.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Before them, on the ways they go, they drop this offspring of the cloud, Long, broad, and inexhaustible.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Maruts, as your strength is great, so have ye cast men down on earth, So have ye made the mountains fall.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The while the Maruts pass along, they talk together on the way: Doth any hear them as they speak?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Come quick with swift steeds, for ye have worshippers among Kanva's sons May you rejoice among them well.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: All is prepared for your delight. We are their servants evermore, To live as long as life may last.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: WHAT now? When will ye take us by both hands, as a dear sire his son, Gods, for whom sacred grass is clipped?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Now whither? To what goal of yours go ye in heaven, and not on earth? Where do your cows disport themselves?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Where are your newest favours shown? Where, Maruts, your prosperity? Where all your high felicities?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: If, O ye Maruts, ye the Sons whom Prsni bore, were mortal, and Immortal he who sings your praise.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Then never were your praiser loathed like a wild beast in pasture-land, Nor should he go on Yama's path.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Let not destructive plague on plague hard to be conquered, strike its down: Let each, with drought, depart from us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Truly, they the fierce and mighty Sons of Rudra send their windless Rain e'en on the desert places.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Like a cow the lightning lows and follows, motherlike, her youngling, When their rain-flood hath been loosened.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When they inundate the earth they spread forth darkness e'en in day time, With the water-laden rain-cloud.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Maruts, at your voice's sound this earthly habitation shakes, And each man reels who dwells therein.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Maruts, with your strong-hoofed steeds, unhindered in their courses, haste Along the bright embanked streams.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Firm be the fellies of your wheels, steady your horses and your cars, And may your reins be fashioned well.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Invite thou hither with this song, for praise, Agni the Lord of Prayer, Him who is fair as Mitra is.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Form in thy mouth the hymn of praise expand thee like, a rainy cloud Sing forth the measured eulogy.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Sing glory to the Marut host, praiseworthy, tuneful, vigorous: Here let the Strong Ones dwell with us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: WHEN thus, like flame, from far away, Maruts, ye cast your measure forth, To whom go Ye, to whom, O shakers of the earth, moved by whose wisdom, whose design?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Strong let your weapons be to drive away your foes, firm for resistance let them be. Yea, passing glorious must be your warrior might, not as a guileful mortal's strength.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When what is strong ye overthrow, and whirl about each ponderous thing, Heroes, your course is through the forest trees of earth, and through the fissures of the rocks.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Consumers of your foes, no enemy of yours is found in heaven or on the earth: Ye Rudras, may the strength, held in this bond, be yours, to bid defiance even now.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: They make the mountains rock and reel, they rend the forest-kings apart. Onward, ye Maruts, drive, like creatures drunk with wine, ye, Gods with all your company.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Ye to your chariot have yoked the spotted deer: a red deer, as a leader, draws. Even the Earth herself listened as ye came near, and men were sorely terrified.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Rudras, quickly we desire your succour for this work of ours. Come to us with your aid as in the days of old, so now for frightened Kanva's sake.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Should any monstrous foe, O Maruts, sent by you or sent by mortals threaten us, Tear ye him from us with your power and with your might, and with the succours that are yours.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: For ye, the worshipful and wise, have guarded Kanva perfectly. O Maruts, come to us with full protecting help, as lightning flashes seek the rain.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Whole strength have ye, O Bounteous Ones; perfect, earth-shakers, is your might. Maruts, against the poet's wrathful enemy send ye an enemy like a dart.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O BRAMANASPATI, stand up: God-serving men we pray to thee. May they who give good gifts, the Maruts, come to us. Indra, most swift, be thou with them.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Son of Strength, each mortal calls to thee for aid when spoil of battle waits for him. O Maruts, may this man who loves you well obtain wealth of good steeds and hero might.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May Brahmanaspati draw nigh, may Sunrta the Goddess come, And Gods bring to this rite which gives the five-fold gift the Hero, lover of mankind.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He who bestows a noble guerdon on the priest wins fame that never shall decay. For him we offer sacred hero-giving food, peerless and conquering easily.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Now Brahmanaspati speaks forth aloud the solemn hymn of praise, Wherein Indra and Varuna, Mitra, Aryaman, the Gods, have made their dwelling place.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May we in holy synods, Gods! recite that hymn, peerless, that brings felicity. If you, O Heroes, graciously accept this word, may it obtain all bliss from you.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Who shall approach the pious? who the man whose sacred grass is trimmed? The offerer with his folk advances more and more: he fills his house with precious things.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He amplifies his lordly might, with kings he slays: e'en mid alarms he dwells secure In great or lesser fight none checks him, none subdues,--the wielder of the thunderbolt.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: NE'ER is he injured whom the Gods Varuna, Mitra, Aryaman, The excellently wise, protect.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He prospers ever, free from scathe, whom they, as with full hands, enrich, Whom they preserve from every foe.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Kings drive far away from him his troubles and his enemies, And lead him safely o'er distress.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thornless, Adityas, is the path, easy for him who seeks the Law: With him is naught to anger you.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: What sacrifice, Adityas, ye Heroes guide by the path direct,-- May that come nigh unto your thought.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: That mortal, ever unsubdued, gains wealth and every precious thing, And children also of his own.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: How, my friends, shall we prepare Aryaman's and Mitra's laud, Glorious food of Varuna?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I point not out to you a man who strikes the pious, or reviles: Only with hymns I call you nigh.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Let him not love to speak ill words: but fear the One who holds all four Within his hand, until they fall.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: SHORTEN our ways, O Pusan, move aside obstruction in the path: Go close before us, cloud-born God.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Drive, Pusan, from our road the wolf, the wicked inauspicious wolf, Who lies in wait to injure us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Who lurks about the path we take, the robber with a guileful heart: Far from the road chase him away.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Tread with thy foot and trample out the firebrand of the wicked one, The double-tongued, whoe'er he be.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Wise Pusan, Wonder-Worker, we claim of thee now the aid wherewith Thou furtheredst our sires of old.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: So, Lord of all prosperity, best wielder of the golden sword, Make riches easy to be won.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Past all pursuers lead us, make pleasant our path and fair to tread: O Pusan, find thou power for this.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Lead us to meadows rich in grass: send on our way no early heat: O Pusan, find thou power for this.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Be gracious to us, fill us full, give, feed us, and invigorate: O Pusan, find thou power for this.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: No blame have we for Pusan; him we magnify with songs of praise: We seek the Mighty One for wealth.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: WHAT shall we sing to Rudra, strong, most bounteous, excellently wise, That shall be dearest to his heart?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: That Aditi may grant the grace of Rudra to our folk, our kine, Our cattle and our progeny;
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: That Mitra and that Varuna, that Rudra may remember us, Yea, all the Gods with one accord.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To Rudra Lord of sacrifice, of hymns and balmy medicines, We pray for joy and health and strength.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He shines in splendour like the Sun, refulgent as bright gold is he, The good, the best among the Gods.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May he grant health into our steeds, wellbeing to our rams and ewes, To men, to women, and to kine.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Soma, set thou upon us the glory of a hundred men, The great renown of mighty chiefs.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Let not malignities, nor those who trouble Soma, hinder us. Indu, give us a share of strength.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Soma! head, central point, love these; Soma! know these as serving thee, Children of thee Immortal, at the highest place of holy law.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: IMMORTAL Jatavedas, thou many-hued fulgent gift of Dawn, Agni, this day to him who pays oblations bring the Gods who waken with the morn.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: For thou art offering-bearer and loved messenger, the charioteer of sacrifice: Accordant with the Asvins and with Dawn grant us heroic strength and lofty fame.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: As messenger we choose to-day Agni the good whom many love, Smoke-bannered spreader of the light, at break of day glory of sacrificial rites.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Him noblest and most youthful, richly worshipped guest, dear to the men who offer gifts, Him, Agni Jatavedas, I beseech at dawn that he may bring the Gods to us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thee, Agni, will I glorify, deathless nourisher of the world, Immortal, offering-bearer, meet for sacred food, preserver, best at sacrifice.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Tell good things to thy praiser, O most youthful God, as richly worshipped, honey-tongued, And, granting to Praskanva lengthened days of life, show honour to the Heavenly Host.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: For the men, Agni, kindle thee as all possessor and as Priest; So Agni, much-invoked, bring hither with all speed the Gods, the excellently wise,
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: At dawn of day, at night, Usas and Savitar, the Asvins, Bhaga, Agni's self: Skilled in fair rites, with Soma poured, the Kanvas light thee, the oblation-wafting God.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: For, Agni, Lord of sacrifice and messenger of men art thou: Bring thou the Gods who wake at dawn who see the light, this day to drink the Soma juice.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou shonest forth, O Agni, after former dawns, all visible, O rich in light. Thou art our help in battle-strife, the Friend of man, the great high priest in sacrifice.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Like Manu, we will stablish thee, Agni, performer of the rite, Invoker, ministering Priest, exceeding wise, the swift immortal messenger.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When as the Gods' High Priest, by many loved, thou dost their mission as their nearest Friend, Then, like the far-resounding billows of the flood, thy flames, O Agni, roar aloud.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Hear, Agni, who hast ears to hear, with all thy train of escort Gods; Let Mitra, Aryaman, seeking betimes our rite, seat them upon the sacred grass.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Let those who strengthen Law, who bountifully give, the life-tongued Maruts, hear our praise. May Law-supporting Varuna with the Asvins twain and Usas, drink the Soma juice.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: WORSHIP the Vasus, Agni! here, the Rudras, the Adityas, all Who spring from Manu, those who know fair rites, who pour their blessings down.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Agni, the Gods who understand give ear unto the worshipper: Lord of Red Steeds, who lovest song, bring thou those Three-and-Thirty Gods.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Jatavedas, great in act, hearken thou to Praskanva's call, As Priyamedha erst was heard, Atri, Virupa, Angiras.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The sons of Priyamedha skilled in lofty praise have called for help On Agni who with fulgent flame is Ruler of all holy rites.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Hear thou, invoked with holy oil, bountiful giver of rewards, These eulogies, whereby the sons of Kanva call thee to their aid.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Agni, loved by many, thou of fame most wondrous, in their homes Men call on thee whose hair is flame, to be the bearer of their gifts.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thee, Agni, best to find out wealth, most widely famous, quick to hear, Singers have stablished in their rites Herald and ministering Priest.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Singers with Soma pressed have made thee, Agni, hasten to the feast, Great light to mortal worshipper, what time they bring the sacred gift.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Good, bounteous, Son of Strength, this day seat here on sacred grass the Gods Who come at early morn, the host of heaven, to drink the Soma juice
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Bring with joint invocations thou, O Agni, the celestial host: Here stands the Soma, bounteous Gods drink this expressed ere yesterday.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Now Morning with her earliest light shines forth, dear Daughter of the Sky: High, Asvins, I extol your praise,
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Sons of the Sea, mighty to save discoverers of riches, ye Gods with deep thought who find out wealth.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Your giant coursers hasten on over the region all in flames, When your car flies with winged steeds.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He, liberal, lover of the flood, Lord of the House, the vigilant, Chiefs! with oblations feeds you full.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Ye have regard unto our hymns, Nasatyas, thinking of our words: Drink boldly of the Soma juice.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Vouchsafe to us, O Asvin Pair, such strength as, with attendant light, May through the darkness carry us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Come in the ship of these our hymns to bear you to the hither shore O Asvins, harness ye the car.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The heaven's wide vessel is your own on the flood's shore your chariot waits Drops, with the hymn, have been prepared.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Kanvas, the drops are in the heaven; the wealth is at the waters' place: Where will ye manifest your form?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Light came to lighten up the branch, the Sun appeared as it were gold: And with its tongue shone forth the dark.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The path of sacrifice was made to travel to the farther goal: The road of heaven was manifest.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The singer of their praise awaits whatever grace the Asvins give, who save when Soma gladdens them.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Ye dwellers with Vivasvan come, auspicious, as to Manu erst; come to the Soma and our praise.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O circumambient Asvins, Dawn follows the brightness of your way: Approve with beams our solemn rites.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Drink ye of our libations, grant protection, O ye Asvins Twain, With aids which none may interrupt.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: ASVINS, for you who strengthen Law this sweetest Soma hath been shed. Drink this expressed ere yesterday and give riches to him who offers it.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Come, O ye Asvins, mounted on your triple car three-seated, beautiful of form To you at sacrifice the Kanvas send the prayer: graciously listen to their call.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Asvins, ye who strengthen Law, drink ye this sweetest Soma juice. Borne on your wealth-fraught car come ye this day to him who offers, ye of wondrous deeds.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Omniscient Asvins, on the thrice-heaped grass bedew with the sweet juice the sacrifice. The sons of Kanva, striving heavenward, call on you with draughts of Soma juice out-poured.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Asvins, with those aids wherewith ye guarded Kanva carefully, Keep us, O Lords of Splendour: drink the Soma juice, ye strengtheners of holy law.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Mighty Ones, ye gave Sudas abundant food, brought on your treasure-laden car; So now vouchsafe to us the wealth which many crave, either from heaven or from the sea.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Nasatyas, whether ye be far away or close to Turvasa, Borne on your lightly-rolling chariot come to us, together with the sunbeams come.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: So let your coursers, ornaments of sacrifice, bring you to our libations here. Bestowing food on him who acts and gives aright, sit, Chiefs, upon the sacred grass.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Come, O Nasatyas, on your car decked with a sunbright canopy, Whereon ye ever bring wealth to the worshipper, to drink the Soma's pleasant juice.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With lauds and songs of praise we call them down to us, that they, most rich, may succour us; For ye have ever in the Kanvas' well-loved house, O Asvins, drunk the Soma juice.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: DAWN on us with prosperity, O Usas, Daughter of the Sky, Dawn with great glory, Goddess, Lady of the Light, dawn thou with riches, Bounteous One.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: They, bringing steeds and kine, boon-givers of all wealth, have oft sped forth to lighten us. O Usas, waken up for me the sounds of joy: send us the riches of the great.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Usas hath dawned, and now shall dawn, the Goddess, driver forth of cars Which, as she cometh nigh, have fixed their thought on her, like glory-seekers on the flood.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Here Kanva, chief of Kanva's race, sings forth aloud the glories of the heroes' names,-- The. princes who, O Usas, as thou comest near, direct their thoughts to liberal gifts.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Like a good matron Usas comes carefully tending everything: Rousing all life she stirs all creatures that have feet, and makes the birds of air fly up.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: She sends the busy forth, each man to his pursuit: delay she knows not as she springs. O rich in opulence, after thy dawning birds that have flown forth no longer rest.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: This Dawn hath yoked her steeds afar, beyond the rising of the Sun: Borne on a hundred chariots she, auspicious Dawn, advances on her way to Men.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To meet her glance all living creatures bend them down: Excellent One, she makes the light. Usas, the Daughter of the Sky, the opulent, shines foes and enmities away.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Shine on us with thy radiant light, O Usas, Daughter of the Sky, Bringing to us great store of high felicity, and beaming on our solemn rites.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: For in thee is each living creature's breath and life, when, Excellent! thou dawnest forth. Borne on thy lofty car, O Lady of the Light, hear, thou of wondrous wealth, our call.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Usas, win thyself the strength which among men is wonderful. Bring thou thereby the pious unto holy rites, those who as priests sing praise to thee.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Bring from the firmament, O Usas, all the Gods, that they may drink our Soma juice, And, being what thou art, vouchsafe us kine and steeds, strength meet for praise and hero might.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May Usas whose auspicious rays are seen resplendent round about, Grant us great riches, fair in form, of all good things, wealth which light labour may attain.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Mighty One, whom the Rsis of old time invoked for their protection and their help, O Usas, graciously answer our songs of praise with bounty and with brilliant light.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Usas, as thou with light to day hast opened the twin doors of heaven, So grant thou us a dwelling wide and free from foes. O Goddess, give us food with kine.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Bring us to wealth abundant, sent in every shape, to plentiful refreshing food, To all-subduing splendour, Usas, Mighty One, to strength, thou rich in spoil and wealth.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: E'EN from above the sky's bright realm come, Usas, by auspicious ways: Let red steeds bear thee to the house of him who pours the Soma, juice.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The chariot which thou mountest, fair of shape, O Usas light to move,-- Therewith, O Daughter of the Sky, aid men of noble fame today.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Bright Usas, when thy times return, all quadrupeds and bipeds stir, And round about flock winged birds from all the boundaries of heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou dawning with thy beams of light illumest all the radiant realm. Thee, as thou art, the Kanvas, fain for wealth, have called with sacred songs.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: HIS bright rays bear him up aloft, the God who knoweth all that lives, Surya, that all may look on him.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The constellations pass away, like thieves, together with their beams, Before the all-beholding Sun.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: His herald rays are seen afar refulgent o'er the world of men, Like flames of fire that burn and blaze.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Swift and all beautiful art thou, O Surya, maker of the light, Illuming all the radiant realm.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou goest to the hosts of Gods, thou comest hither to mankind, Hither all light to be beheld.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With that same eye of thine wherewith thou lookest brilliant Varuna, Upon the busy race of men,
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Traversing sky and wide mid-air, thou metest with thy beams our days, Sun, seeing all things that have birth.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Seven Bay Steeds harnessed to thy car bear thee, O thou farseeing One, God, Surya, with the radiant hair.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Surya hath yoked the pure bright Seven, the daughters of the car; with these, His own dear team, he goeth forth.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Looking upon the loftier light above the darkness we have come To Surya, God among the Gods, the light that is most excellent.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Rising this day, O rich in friends, ascending to the loftier heaven, Surya remove my heart's disease, take from me this my yellow hue.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To parrots and to starlings let us give away my yellowness, Or this my yellowness let us transfer to Haritala trees.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With all his conquering vigour this Aditya hath gone up on high, Giving my foe into mine hand: let me not be my foeman's prey.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: MAKE glad with songs that Ram whom many men invoke, worthy of songs of praise, Indra, the sea of wealth; Whose gracious deeds for men spread like the heavens abroad: sing praise to him the Sage, most liberal for our good.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: As aids the skilful Rbhus yearned to Indra strong to save, who fills mid-air, encompassed round with might, Rushing in rapture; and o'er Satakratu came the gladdening shout that urged him on to victory.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou hast disclosed the kine's stall for the Angirases, and made a way for Atri by a hundred doors. On Vimada thou hast bestowed both food and wealth, making thy bolt dance in the sacrificer's fight.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou hast unclosed the prisons of the waters; thou hast in the mountain seized the treasure rich in gifts. When thou hadst slain with might the dragon Vrtra, thou, Indra, didst raise the Sun in heaven for all to see.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With wondrous might thou blewest enchanter fiends away, with powers celestial those who called on thee in jest. Thou, hero-hearted, hast broken down Pipru's forts, and helped Rjisvan when the Dasyus were struck dead.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou savedst Kutsa when Susna was smitten down; to Atithigva gavest Sambara for a prey. E'en mighty Arbuda thou troddest under foot: thou from of old wast born to strike the Dasyus dead.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: All power and might is closely gathered up in thee; thy bounteous spirit joys in drinking Soma juice. Known is the thunderbolt that lies within thine arms: rend off therewith all manly prowess of our foe.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Discern thou well Aryas and Dasyus; punishing the lawless give them up to him whose grass is strewn. Be thou the sacrificer's strong encourager all these thy deeds are my delight at festivals.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Indra gives up the lawless to the pious man, destroying by the Strong Ones those who have no strength. Vamra when glorified destroyed the gathered piles of the still waxing great one who would reach the heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The might which Usana hath formed for thee with might rends in its greatness and with strength both worlds apart. O Hero-souled, the steeds of Vata, yoked by thought, have carried thee to fame while thou art filled with power.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When Indra hath rejoiced with Kavya Usana, he mounts his steeds who swerve wider and wider yet. The Strong hath loosed his bolt with the swift rush of rain, and he hath rent in pieces Susna's firm-built forts.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou mountest on thy car amid strong Soma draughts: Saryata brought thee those in which thou hast delight. Indra, when thou art pleased with men whose Soma flows thou risest to unchallenged glory in the sky.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To old Kaksivan, Soma-presser, skilled in song, O Indra, thou didst give the youthful Vrcaya. Thou, very wise, wast Mena, Vrsanaiva's child: those deeds of thine must all be told at Soma feasts.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The good man's refuge in his need is Indra, firm as a doorpost, praised among the Pajras. Indra alone is Lord of wealth, the Giver, lover of riches, chariots, kine, and horses.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To him the Mighty One, the self-resplendent, verily strong and great, this praise is uttered. May we and all the heroes, with the princes, be, in this fray, O Indra, in thy keeping.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I GLORIFY that Ram who finds the light of heaven, whose hundred nobly-natured ones go forth with him. With hymns may I turn hither Indra to mine aid,--the Car which like a strong steed hasteth to the call.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Like as a mountain on firm basis, unremoved, he, thousandfold protector, waxed in mighty strength, When Indra, joying in the draughts of Soma juice, forced the clouds, slaying Vrtra stayer of their flow.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: For he stays e'en the stayers, spread o'er laden cloud, rooted in light, strengthened in rapture by the wise. Indra with thought, with skilled activity, I call, most liberal giver, for he sates him with the juice.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Whom those that flow in heaven on sacred grass, his own assistants, nobly-natured, fill full like the sea,-- Beside that Indra when he smote down Vrtra stood his helpers, straight in form, mighty, invincible.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To him, as in wild joy he fought with him who stayed the rain, his helpers sped like swift streams down a slope, When Indra, thunder-armed, made bold by Soma draughts, as Trta cleaveth Vala's fences, cleft him through.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Splendour encompassed thee, forth shone thy warrior might: the rain-obstructer lay in mid-air's lowest deep, What time, O Indra, thou didst cast thy thunder down upon the jaws of Vritra hard to be restrained.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The hymns which magnify thee, Indra, reach to thee even as water-brooks flow down and fill the lake. Tvastar gave yet more force to thine appropriate strength, and forged thy thunderbolt of overpowering might.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When, Indra, thou whose power is linked with thy Bay Steeds hadst smitten Vrtra, causing floods to flow for man, Thou heldst in thine arms the metal thunderbolt, and settest in the heaven the Sun for all to see.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: In fear they raised the lofty self-resplendent hymn, praise giving and effectual, leading up to heaven, When Indra's helpers fighting for the good of men, the Maruts, faithful to mankind, joyed in the light.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Then Heaven himself, the mighty, at that Dragon's roar reeled back in terror when, Indra, thy thunderbolt In the wild joy of Soma had struck off with might the head of Vrtra, tyrant of the earth and heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Indra, were this earth extended forth tenfold, and men who dwell therein multiplied day by day, Still here thy conquering might, Maghavan, would be famed: it hath waxed vast as heaven in majesty and power.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou, bold of heart, in thine own native might, for help, upon the limit of this mid-air and of heaven, Hast made the earth to be the pattern of thy strength: embracing flood and light thou reachest to the sky.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou art the counterpart of earth, the Master of lofty heaven with all its mighty Heroes: Thou hast filled all the region with thy greatness: yea, of a truth there is none other like thee.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Whose amplitude the heaven and earth have not attained, whose bounds the waters of mid-air have never reached,-- Not, when in joy he fights the stayer of the rain: thou, and none else, hast made all things in order due.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Maruts sang thy praise in this encounter, and in thee all the Deities delighted, What time thou, Indra, with thy spiky weapon, thy deadly bolt, smotest the face of Vrtra.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I WE will present fair praise unto the Mighty One, our hymns to Indra in Vivasvan's dwelling-place; For he hath ne'er found wealth in those who seem to sleep: those who give wealth to men accept no paltry praise.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Giver of horses, Indra, giver, thou, of kine, giver of barley, thou art Lord and guard of wealth: Man's helper from of old, not disappointing hope, Friend of our friends, to thee as such we sing this praise.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Indra, most splendid, powerful, rich in mighty deeds, this treasure spread around is known to be thine own. Gather therefrom, O Conqueror, and bring to us: fail not the hope of him who loves and sings to thee.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Well pleased with these bright flames and with these Soma drops, take thou away our poverty with seeds and kine. With Indra scattering the Dasyu through these drops, freed from their hate may we obtain abundant food.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Let us obtain, O Indra, plenteous wealth and food, with strength exceeding glorious, shining to the sky: May we obtain the Goddess Providence, the strength of heroes, special source of cattle, rich in steeds.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: These our libations strength-inspiring, Soma draughts, gladdened thee in the fight with Vrtra, Hero Lord, What time thou slewest for the singer with trimmed grass ten thousand Vrtras, thou resistless in thy might.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou goest on from fight to fight intrepidly, destroying castle after castle here with strength. Thou, Indra, with thy friend who makes the foe bow down, slewest from far away the guileful Namuci.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou hast struck down in death Karañja, Parnaya, in Atithigva's very glorious going forth. Unyielding, when Rjisvan compassed them with siege, thou hast destroyed the hundred forts of Vangrida.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With all-outstripping chariot-wheel, O Indra, thou far-famed, hast overthrown the twice ten Kings of men, With sixty thousand nine-and-ninety followers, who came in arms to fight with friendless Susravas.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou hast protected Susravas with succour, and Turvayana with thine aid, O Indra. Thou madest Kutsa, Atithigva, Ayu, subject unto this King, the young, the mighty.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May we protected by the Gods hereafter remain thy very prosperous friends, O Indra. Thee we extol, enjoying through thy favour life long and joyful and with store of heroes.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: URGE us not, Maghavan, to this distressful fight, for none may comprehend the limit of thy strength. Thou with fierce shout hast made the woods and rivers roar: did not men run in crowds together in their fear?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Sing hymns of praise to Sakra, Lord of power and might; laud thou and magnify Indra who heareth thee, Who with his daring might, a Bull exceeding strong in strength, maketh him master of the heaven and earth.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Sing forth to lofty Dyaus a strength-bestowing song, the Bold, whose resolute mind hath independent sway. High glory hath the Asura, compact of strength, drawn on by two Bay Steeds: a Bull, a Car is he.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The ridges of the lofty heaven thou madest shake; thou, daring, of thyself smotest through Sambara, When bold with gladdening juice, thou warredst with thy bolt, sharp and two-edged, against the banded sorcerers.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When with a roar that fills the woods, thou forcest down on wind's head the stores which Susna kept confined, Who shall have power to stay thee firm and eager-souled from doing still this day what thou of old hast done?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou helpest Narya, Turvasa, and Yadu, and Vayya's son Turviti, Satakratu! Thou helpest horse and car in final battle thou breakest down the nine-and-ninety castles.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: A hero-lord is he, King of a mighty folk, who offers free oblations and promotes the Law, Who with a bounteous guerdon welcomes hymns of praise: for him flows down the abundant stream below the sky.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: His power is matchless, matchless is his wisdom; chief, through their work, be some who drink the Soma, Those, Indra, who increase the lordly power, the firm heroic strength of thee the Giver.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Therefore for thee are these abundant beakers Indra's drink, stone-pressed juices held in ladles. Quaff them and satisfy therewith thy longing; then fix thy mind upon bestowing treasure.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: There darkness stood, the vault that stayed the waters' flow: in Vrtra's hollow side the rain-cloud lay concealed. But Indra smote the rivers which the obstructer stayed, flood following after flood, down steep declivities.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: So give us, Indra, bliss-increasing glory give us great sway and strength that conquers people. Preserve our wealthy patrons, save our princes; vouchsafe us wealth and food with noble offspring.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: THOUGH e'en this heaven's wide space and earth have spread them out, nor heaven nor earth may be in greatness Indra's match. Awful and very mighty, causing woe to men, he whets his thunderbolt for sharpness, as a bull.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Like as the watery ocean, so doth he receive the rivers spread on all sides in their ample width. He bears him like a bull to drink of Soma juice, and will, as Warrior from of old, be praised for might.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou swayest, Indra, all kinds of great manly power, so as to bend, as't were, even that famed mountain down. Foremost among the Gods is he through hero might, set in the van, the Strong One, for each arduous deed.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He only in the wood is praised by worshippers, when he shows forth to men his own fair Indra-power. A friendly Bull is he, a Bull to be desired when Maghavan auspiciously sends forth his voice.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Yet verily the Warrior in his vigorous strength stirreth up with his might great battles for mankind; And men have faith in Indra, the resplendent One, what time he hurleth down his bolt, his dart of death.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Though, fain for glory, and with strength increased on earth, he with great might destroys the dwellings made with art, He makes the lights of heaven shine forth secure, he bids, exceeding wise, the floods flow for his worshipper.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Drinker of Soma, let thy heart incline to give; bring thy Bays hitherward, O thou who hearest praise. Those charioteers of' thine, best skilled to draw the rein, the rapid sunbeams, Indra, lead thee not astray.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou bearest in both hands treasure that never fails; the famed One in his body holds unvanquished might. O Indra, in thy members many powers abide, like wells surrounded by the ministering priests.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: FOR this man's full libations held in ladles, he hath roused him, eager, as a horse to meet the mare. He stays his golden car, yoked with Bay Horses, swift, and drinks the Soma juice which strengthens for great deeds.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To him the guidance-following songs of praise flow full, as those who seek gain go in company to the flood. To him the Lord of power, the holy synod's might, as to a hill, with speed, ascend the loving ones.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Victorious, great is he; in manly battle shines, unstained with dust, his might, as shines a mountain peak; Wherewith the iron one, fierce e'en against the strong, in rapture, fettered wily Sushna fast in bonds.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When Strength the Goddess, made more strong for help by thee, waits upon Indra as the Sun attends the Dawn, Then. he who with his might unflinching kills the gloom stirs up the dust aloft, with joy and triumphing.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When thou with might, upon the framework of the heaven, didst fix, across, air's region firmly, unremoved, In the light-winning war, Indra, in rapturous joy, thou smotest Vrtra dead and broughtest floods of rain.
