verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou with thy might didst grasp, the holder-up of heaven, thou who art mighty also in the seats of earth. Thou, gladdened by the juice, hast set the waters free, and broken Vrtra's stony fences through and through.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To him most liberal, lofty Lord of lofty wealth, verily powerful and strong, I bring my hymn,-- Whose checkless bounty, as of waters down a slope, is spread abroad for all that live, to give them strength.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Now all this world, for worship, shall come after thee--the offerer's libations like floods to the depth, When the well-loved one seems to rest upon the hill, the thunderbolt of Indra, shatterer wrought of gold.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To him the terrible, most meet for lofty praise, like bright Dawn, now bring gifts with reverence in this rite, Whose being, for renown, yea, Indra-power and light, have been created, like bay steeds, to move with speed.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thine, Indra, praised by many, excellently rich! are we who trusting in thy help draw near to thee. Lover of praise, none else but thou receives our laud: as earth loves all her creatures, love thou this our hymn.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Great is thy power, O Indra, we are thine. Fulfil, O Maghavan, the wish of this thy worshipper. After thee lofty heaven hath measured out its strength: to thee and to thy power this earth hath bowed itself.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou, who hast thunder for thy weapon, with thy bolt hast shattered into pieces this broad massive cloud. Thou hast sent down the obstructed floods that they may flow: thou hast, thine own for ever, all victorious might.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: NE'ER waxeth faint the Immortal, Son of Strength, since he, the Herald, hath become Vivasvan's messenger. On paths most excellent he measured out mid-air: he with oblation calls to service of the Gods.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Never decaying, seizing his appropriate food, rapidly, eagerly through the dry wood he spreads. His back, as he is sprinkled, glistens like a horse: loud hath he roared and shouted like the heights of heaven?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Set high in place o'er all that Vasus, Rudras do, immortal, Lord of riches, seated as High Priest; Hastening like a car to men, to those who live, the God without delay gives boons to be desired.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Urged by the wind be spreads through dry wood as he lists, armed with his tongues for sickles, with a mighty roar. Black is thy path, Agni, changeless, with glittering waves! when like a bull thou rushest eager to the trees.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With teeth of flame, wind-driven, through the wood he speeds, triumphant like a bull among the herd of cows, With bright strength roaming to the everlasting air: things fixed, things moving quake before him as he flies.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Bhrgus established thee among mankind for men, like as a treasure, beauteous, easy to invoke; Thee, Agni, as a herald and choice-worthy guest, as an auspicious Friend to the Celestial Race.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Agni, the seven tongues' deftest Sacrificer, him whom the priests elect at solemn worship, The Herald, messenger of all the Vasus, I serve with dainty food, I ask for riches.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Grant, Son of Strength, thou rich in friends, a refuge without a flaw this day to us thy praisers. O Agni, Son of Strength, with forts of iron preserve thou from distress the man who lauds thee.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Be thou a refuge, Bright One, to the singer, a shelter, Bounteous Lord, to those who worship. Preserve the singer from distress, O Agni. May he, enriched with prayer, come soon and early.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: THE other fires are, verily, thy branches; the Immortals all rejoice in thee, O Agni. Centre art thou, Vaisvanara, of the people, sustaining men like a deep-founded pillar.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The forehead of the sky, earth's centre, Agni became the messenger of earth and heaven. Vaisvanara, the Deities produced thee, a God, to be a light unto the Arya.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: As in the Sun firm rays are set for ever, treasures are in Vaisvanara, in Agni. Of all the riches in the hills, the waters, the herbs, among mankind, thou art the Sovran.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: As the great World-halves, so are their Son's praises; skilled, as a man, to act, is he the Herald. Vaisvanara, celestial, truly mighty, most manly One, hath many a youthful consort.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Even the lofty heaven, O Jatavedas Vaisvanara, hath not attained thy greatness. Thou art the King of lands where men are settled, thou hast brought comfort to the Gods in battle.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Now will I tell the greatness of the Hero whom Puru's sons follow as Vrtra's slayer: Agni Vaisvanara struck down the Dasyu, cleave Sambara through and shattered down his fences.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Vaisvanara, dwelling by his might with all men, far-shining, holy mid the Bharadvajas, Is lauded, excellent, with hundred praises by Purunitha, son of Satavani.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: As 'twere Some goodly treasure Matarisvan brought, as a gift, the glorious Priest to Bhrgu, Banner of sacrifice, the good Protector, child of two births, the swiftly moving envoy.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Both Gods and men obey this Ruler's order, Gods who are worshipped, men who yearn and worship. As Priest he takes his seat ere break of morning, House-Lord, adorable with men, Ordainer.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May our fair praise, heart-born, most recent, reach him whose tongue, e'en at his birth, is sweet as honey; Whom mortal priests, men, with their strong endeavour, supplied with dainty viands, have created.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Good to mankind, the yearning Purifier hath among men been placed as Priest choice-worthy. May Agni be our Friend, Lord of the Household, protector of the riches in the dwelling.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: As such we Gotamas with hymns extol thee, O Agni, as the guardian Lord of riches, Decking thee like a horse, the swift prizewinner. May he, enriched with prayer, come soon and early.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: EVEN to him, swift, strong and high. exalted, I bring my song of praise as dainty viands, My thought to him resistless, praise-deserving, prayers offered most especially to Indra.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Praise, like oblation, I present, and utter aloud my song, my fair hymn to the Victor. For Indra, who is Lord of old, the singers have decked their lauds with heart and mind and spirit.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To him then with my lips mine adoration, winning heaven's light, most excellent, I offer, To magnify with songs of invocation and with fair hymns the Lord, most bounteous Giver.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Even for him I frame a laud, as fashions the wright a chariot for the man who needs it,-- Praises to him who gladly hears our praises, a hymn well-formed, all-moving, to wise Indra.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: So with my tongue I deck, to please that Indra, my hymn, as 'twere a horse, through love of glory, To reverence the Hero, bounteous Giver, famed far and wide, destroyer of the castles.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Even for him hath Tvastar forged the thunder, most deftly wrought, celestial, for the battle, Wherewith he reached the vital parts of Vrtra, striking-the vast, the mighty with the striker.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: As soon as, at libations of his mother, great Visnu had drunk up the draught, he plundered. The dainty cates, the cooked mess; but One stronger transfixed the wild boar, shooting through the mountain.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To him, to Indra, when he slew the Dragon, the Dames, too, Consorts of the Gods, wove praises. The mighty heaven and earth hath he encompassed: thy greatness heaven and earth, combined, exceed not.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Yea, of a truth, his magnitude surpasseth the magnitude of earth, mid-air, and heaven. Indra, approved by all men, self-resplendent, waxed in his home, loud-voiced and strong for battle.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Through his own strength Indra with bolt of thunder cut piece-meal Vrtra, drier up of waters. He let the floods go free, like cows imprisoned, for glory, with a heart inclined to bounty.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The rivers played, through his impetuous splendour, since with his bolt he compassed them on all sides. Using his might and favouring him who worshipped, he made a ford, victorious, for Turviti.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Vast, with thine ample power, with eager movement, against this Vrtra cast thy bolt of thunder. Rend thou his joints, as of an ox, dissevered, with bolt oblique, that floods of rain may follow.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Sing with new lauds his exploits wrought aforetime, the deeds of him, yea, him who moveth swiftly, When, hurling forth his weapons in the battle, he with impetuous wrath lays low the foemen.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When he, yea, he, comes forth the firm. Set mountains and the whole heaven and earth, tremble for terror. May Nodhas, ever praising the protection of that dear Friend, gain quickly strength heroic.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Now unto him of these things hath been given what he who rules alone o'er much, electeth. Indra hath helped Etasa, Soma-presser, contending in the race of steeds with Surya.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thus to thee, Indra, yoker of Bay Coursers, the Gotamas have brought their prayers to please thee. Bestow upon them thought, decked with all beauty. May he, enriched with prayer, come soon and early.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: LIKE Angiras a gladdening laud we ponder to him who loveth song, exceeding mighty. Let us sing glory to the far-famed Hero who must be praised with fair hymns by the singer.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Unto the great bring ye great adoration, a chant with praise to him exceeding mighty, Through whom our sires, Angirases, singing praises and knowing well the places, found the cattle.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When Indra and the Angirases desired it, Sarama found provision for her offspring. Brhaspati cleft the mountain, found the cattle: the heroes shouted with the kine in triumph.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Mid shout, loud shout, and roar, with the Navagvas, seven singers, hast thou, heavenly, rent the mountain; Thou hast, with speeders, with Dasagvas, Indra, Sakra, with thunder rent obstructive Vala.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Praised by Angirases, thou, foe-destroyer, hast, with the Dawn, Sun, rays, dispelled the darkness. Thou Indra, hast spread out the earth's high ridges, and firmly fixed the region under heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: This is the deed most worthy of all honour, the fairest marvel of the Wonder-Worker, That, nigh where heaven bends down, he made four rivers flow full with waves that carry down sweet water.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Unwearied, won with lauding hymns, he parted of old the ancient Pair, united ever. In highest sky like Bhaga, he the doer of marvels set both Dames and earth and heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Still born afresh, young Dames, each in her manner, unlike in hue, the Pair in alternation Round heaven and earth from ancient time have travelled, Night with her dark limbs, Dawn with limbs of splendour.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Rich in good actions, skilled in operation, the Son with might maintains his perfect friendship. Thou in the raw cows, black of hue or ruddy, storest the ripe milk glossy white in colour.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Their paths, of old connected, rest uninjured; they with great might preserve the immortal statutes. For many thousand holy works the Sisters wait on the haughty Lord like wives and matrons.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thoughts ancient, seeking wealth, with adoration, with newest lauds have sped to thee, O Mighty. As yearning wives cleave to their yearning husband, so cleave our hymns to thee, O Lord most potent.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Strong God, the riches which thy hands have holden from days of old have perished not nor wasted. Splendid art thou, O Indra, wise, unbending: strengthen us with might, O Lord of Power.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O mighty Indra, Gotama's son Nodhas hath fashioned this new prayer to thee Eternal, Sure leader, yoker of the Tawny Coursers. May he, enriched with prayer, come soon and early.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: THOU art the Mighty One; when born, O Indra, with power thou terrifiedst earth and heaven; When, in their fear of thee, all firm-set mountains and monstrous creatures shook like dust before thee.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When thy two wandering Bays thou drawest hither, thy praiser laid within thine arms the thunder, Wherewith, O Much-invoked, in will resistless, thou smitest foemen down and many a castle.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Faithful art thou, these thou defiest, Indra; thou art the Rbhus' Lord, heroic, victor. Thou, by his side, for young and glorious Kutsa, with steed and car in battle slewest Susna,
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: That, as a friend, thou furtheredst, O Indra, when, Thunderer, strong in act, thou crushedst Vrtra; When, Hero, thou, great-souled, with easy conquest didst rend the Dasyus in their distant dwelling.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: This doest thou, and art not harmed, O Indra, e'en in the anger of the strongest mortal. Lay thou the race-course open for our horses: as with a club, slay, Thunder-armed! our foemen.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Hence men invoke thee, Indra, in the tumult of battle, in the light-bestowing conflict. This aid of thine, O Godlike One, was ever to be implored in deeds of might in combat.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Warring for Purukutsa thou, O Indra, Thunder-armed! breakest down the seven castles; Easily, for Sudas, like grass didst rend them, and out of need, King, broughtest gain to Puru.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Indra, God who movest round about us, feed us with varied food plenteous as water- Food wherewithal, O Hero, thou bestowest vigour itself to flow to us for ever.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Prayers have been made by Gotamas, O Indra, addressed to thee, with laud for thy Bay Horses. Bring us in noble shape abundant riches. May he, enriched with prayer, come soon and early.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: BRING for the manly host, wise and majestical, O Nodhas, for the Maruts bring thou a pure gift. I deck my songs as one deft-handed, wise in mind prepares the water that hath power in solemn rites.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: They spring to birth, the lofty Ones, the Bulls of Heaven, divine, the youths of Rudra, free from spot and stain; The purifiers, shining brightly even as suns, awful of form like giants, scattering rain-drops down.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Young Rudras, demon-slayers, never growing old, they have waxed, even as mountains, irresistible. They make all beings tremble with their mighty strength, even the very strongest, both of earth and heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With glittering ornaments they deck them forth for show; for beauty on their breasts they bind their chains of gold. The lances on their shoulders pound to pieces; they were born together, of themselves, the Men of Heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Loud roarers, giving strength, devourers of the foe, they make the winds, they make the lightnings with their powers. The restless shakers drain the udders of the sky, and ever wandering round fill the earth full with milk.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The bounteous Maruts with the fatness dropping milk fill full the waters which avail in solemn rites. They lead, as 'twere, the Strong Horse forth, that it may rain: they milk the thundering, the never-failing spring.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Mighty, with wondrous power and marvellously bright, selfstrong like mountains, ye glide swiftly on your way. Like the wild elephants ye eat the forests up when ye assume your strength among the bright red flames.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Exceeding wise they roar like lions mightily, they, all-possessing, are beauteous as antelopes; Stirring the darkness with lances and spotted deer, combined as priests, with serpents' fury through their might.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Heroes who march in companies, befriending man, with serpents' ire through strength, ye greet the earth and heaven. Upon the seats, O Maruts, of your chariots, upon the cars stands lightning visible as light.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Lords of all riches, dwelling in the home of wealth, endowed with mighty vigour, singers loud of voice, Heroes, of powers infinite, armed with strong men's rings, the archers, they have laid the arrow on their arms.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: They who with golden fellies make the rain increase drive forward the big clouds like wanderers on the way. Self-moving, brisk, unwearied, they o'erthrow the firm; the Maruts with bright lances make all things to reel.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The progeny of Rudra we invoke with prayer, the brisk, the bright, the worshipful, the active Ones To the strong band of Maruts cleave for happiness, the chasers of the sky, impetuous, vigorous.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Maruts, the man whom ye have guarded with your help, he verily in strength surpasseth all mankind. Spoil with his steeds he gaineth, treasure with his men; he winneth honourable strength and prospereth.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Maruts, to the worshippers give glorious strength invincible in battle, brilliant, bringing wealth, Praiseworthy, known to all men. May we foster well, during a hundred winters, son and progeny.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Will ye then, O ye Maruts, grant us riches, durable, rich in men, defying onslaught. A hundred, thousandfold, ever increasing? May he, enriched with prayer, come soon and early.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: ONE-MINDED, wise, they tracked thee like a thief lurking in dark cave with a stolen cow: Thee claiming worship, bearing it to Gods: there nigh to thee sate all the Holy Ones.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Gods approached the ways of holy Law; there was a gathering vast as heaven itself. The waters feed with praise the growing Babe, born nobly in the womb, the seat of Law.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Like grateful food, like some wide dwelling place, like a fruit-bearing hill, a wholesome stream. Like a steed urged to run in swift career, rushing like Sindhu, who may check his course?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Kin as a brother to his sister floods, he eats the woods as a King eats the rich. When through the forest, urged by wind, he spreads, verily Agni shears the hair of earth.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Like a swan sitting in the floods he pants wisest in mind mid men he wakes at morn. A Sage like Soma, sprung from Law, he grew like some young creature, mighty, shining far.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: LIKE the Sun's glance, like wealth of varied sort, like breath which is the life, like one's own son, Like a swift bird, a cow who yields her milk, pure and refulgent to the wood he speeds.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He offers safety like a pleasant home, like ripened corn, the Conqueror of men. Like a Seer lauding, famed among the folk; like a steed friendly he vouchsafes us power.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With flame insatiate, like eternal might; caring for each one like a dame at home; Bright when he shines forth, whitish mid the folk, like a car, gold-decked, thundering to the fight.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He strikes with terror like a dart shot forth, e'en like an archer's arrow tipped with flame; Master of present and of future life, the maidens' lover and the matrons' Lord.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To him lead all your ways: may we attain the kindled God as cows their home at eve. He drives the flames below as floods their swell: the rays rise up to the fair place of heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: VICTORIOUS in the wood, Friend among men, ever he claims obedience as a King. Gracious like peace, blessing like mental power, Priest was he, offering-bearer, full of thought.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He, bearing in his hand all manly might, crouched in the cavern, struck the Gods with fear. Men filled with understanding find him there, when they have sting prayers formed within their heart.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He, like the Unborn, holds the broad earth up; and with effective utterance fixed the sky. O Agni, guard the spots which cattle love: thou, life of all, hast gone from lair to lair.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Whoso hath known him dwelling in his lair, and hath approached the stream of holy Law,-- They who release him, paying sacred rites,--truly to such doth he announce great wealth.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He who grows mightily in herbs, within each fruitful mother and each babe she bears, Wise, life of all men, in the waters' home,--for him have sages built as 'twere a seat.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: COMMINGLING, restless, he ascends the sky, unveiling nights and all that stands or moves, As he the sole God is preeminent in greatness among all these other Gods.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: All men are joyful in thy power, O God, that living from the dry wood thou art born. All truly share thy Godhead while they keep, in their accustomed ways, eternal Law.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Strong is the thought of Law, the Law's behest; all works have they performed; he quickens all. Whoso will bring oblation, gifts to thee, to him, bethinking thee, vouchsafe thou wealth.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Seated as Priest with Manu's progeny, of all these treasures he alone is Lord. Men yearn for children to prolong their line, and are not disappointed in their hope.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Eagerly they who hear his word fulfil his wish as sons obey their sire's behest. He, rich in food, unbars his wealth like doors: he, the House-Friend, hath decked heaven's vault with stars.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: BRIGHT, splendid, like Dawn's lover, he hath filled the two joined worlds as with the light of heaven. When born, with might thou hast encompassed them: Father of Gods, and yet their Son wast thou.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Agni, the Sage, the humble, who discerns like the cow's udder, the sweet taste of food, Like a bliss-giver to be drawn to men, sits gracious in the middle of the house.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Born in the dwelling like a lovely son, pleased, like a strong steed, he bears on the folk. What time the men and I, with heroes, call, may Agni then gain all through Godlike power.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: None breaks these holy laws of thine when thou hast granted audience to these chieftains here. This is thy boast, thou smotest with thy peers, and joined with heroes dravest off disgrace.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Like the Dawn's lover, spreading light, well-known as hued like morn, may he remember me. They, bearing of themselves, unbar the doors: they all ascend to the fair place of heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: MAY we, the pious, win much food by prayer, may Agni with fair light pervade each act,-- He the observer of the heavenly laws of Gods, and of the race of mortal man.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He who is germ of waters, germ of woods, germ of all things that move not and that move,-- To him even in the rock and in the house: Immortal One, he cares for all mankind.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Agni is Lord of riches for the man who serves him readily with sacred songs. Protect these beings thou with careful thought, knowing the races both of Gods and men.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Whom many dawns and nights, unlike, make strong, whom, born in Law, all things that move and stand,-- He hath been won, Herald who sits in light, making effectual all our holy works.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou settest value on our cows and woods: all shall bring tribute to us to the light. Men have served thee in many and sundry spots, parting, as 'twere, an aged father's wealth.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Like a brave archer, like one skilled and bold, a fierce avenger, so he shines in fight.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: LOVING the loving One, as wives their husband, the sisters of one home have urged him forward, Bright-coloured, even, as the cows love morning, dark, breaking forth to view, and redly beaming.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Our sires with lauds burst e'en the firm-set fortress, yea, the Angirases, with roar, the mountain. They made for us a way to reach high heaven, they found us day, light, day's sign, beams of morning.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: They stablished order, made his service fruitful; then parting them among the longing faithful, Not thirsting after aught, they come, most active, while with sweet food the race of Gods they strengthen.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Since Matarisvan, far-diffused, hath stirred him, and he in every house grown bright and noble, He, Bhrgu-like I hath gone as his companion, as on commission to a greater Sovran.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When man poured juice to Heaven, the mighty Father, he knew and freed himself from close embracement. The archer boldly shot at him his arrow, and the God threw his splendour on his Daughter.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Whoso, hath flames for thee within his dwelling, or brings the worship which thou lovest daily, Do thou of double might increase his substance: may he whom thou incitest meet with riches.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: All sacrificial viands wait on Agni as the Seven mighty Rivers seek the ocean. Not by our brethren was our food discovered: find with the Gods care for us, thou who knowest.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When light hath filled the Lord of men for increase, straight from the heaven descends the limpid moisture. Agni hath brought to light and filled with spirit the youthful host blameless and well providing.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He who like thought goes swiftly on his journey, the Sun, alone is ever Lord of riches. The Kings with fair hands, Varuna and Mitra, protect the precious nectar in our cattle.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Agni, break not our ancestral friendship, Sage as thou art, endowed with deepest knowledge. Old age, like gathering cloud, impairs the body: before that evil be come nigh protect me.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: THOUGH holding many gifts for men, he humbleth the higher powers of each wise ordainer. Agni is now the treasure-lord of treasures, for ever granting all immortal bounties.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Gods infallible all searching found not him, the dear Babe who still is round about us. Worn weary, following his track, devoted, they reached the lovely highest home of Agni.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Because with holy oil the pure Ones, Agni, served thee the very pure three autumn seasons, Therefore they won them holy names for worship, and nobly born they dignified their bodies.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Making them known to spacious earth and heaven, the holy Ones revealed the powers of Rudra. The mortal band, discerning in the distance, found Agni standing in the loftiest station.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Nigh they approached, one-minded, with their spouses, kneeling to him adorable paid worship. Friend finding in his own friend's eye protection, they made their own the bodies which they chastened.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Soon as the holy beings had discovered the thrice-seven mystic things contained within thee, With these, one-minded, they preserve the Amrta: guard thou the life of all their plants and cattle.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou, Agni, knower of men's works, hast sent us good food in constant course for our subsistence: Thou deeply skilled in paths of Gods becamest an envoy never wearied, offering-bearer.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Knowing the Law, the seven strong floods from heaven, full of good thought, discerned the doors of riches. Sarama found the cattle's firm-built prison whereby the race of man is still supported.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: They who approached all noble operations making a path that leads to life immortal, To be the Bird's support, the spacious mother, Aditi, and her great Sons stood in power.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When Gods immortal made both eyes of heaven, they gave to him the gift of beauteous glory. Now they flow forth like rivers set in motion: they knew the Red Steeds coming down, O Agni.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I. HE who gives food, like patrimonial riches and guides aright like some wise man's instruction, Loved like a guest who lies in pleasant lodging,--may he, as Priest, prosper his servant's dwelling.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He who like Savitar the God, true-minded protecteth with his power. all acts of vigour, Truthful, like splendour, glorified by many, like breath joy-giving,--all must strive to win him.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He who on earth dwells like a king surrounded by faithful friends, like a God all-sustaining, Like heroes who preside, who sit in safety: like as a blameless dame dear to her husband.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thee, such, in settlements secure, O Agni, our men serve ever kindled in each dwelling. On him have they laid splendour in abundance: dear to all men, bearer be he of riches.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May thy rich worshippers win food, O Agni, and princes gain long life who bring oblation. May we get booty from our foe in battle, presenting to the Gods their share for glory.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The cows of holy law, sent us by Heaven, have swelled with laden udders, loudly lowing; Soliciting his favour, from a distance the rivers to the rock have flowed together.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Agni, with thee, soliciting thy favour, the holy Ones have gained glory in heaven. They made the Night and Dawn of different colours, and set the black and purple hues together.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May we and those who worship be the mortals whom thou, O Agni, leadest on to riches. Thou hast filled earth and heaven and air's mid-region, and followest the whole world like a shadow.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Aided by thee, O Agni, may we conquer steeds with steeds, men with men, heroes with heroes, Lords of the wealth transmitted by our fathers: and may our princes live a hundred winters.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May these our hymns of praise, Agni, Ordainer, be pleasant to thee in thy heart and spirit. May we have power to hold thy steeds of riches, laying on thee the God-sent gift of glory.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: As forth to sacrifice we go, a hymn to a hymn let us say, Who hears us even when afar;
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Who, from of old, in carnage, when the people gathered, hath preserved His household for the worshipper.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: And let men say, Agni is born, e'en he who slayeth Vrtra, he Who winneth wealth in every fight.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Him in whose house an envoy thou lovest to taste his offered gifts, And strengthenest his sacrifice,
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Him, Angiras, thou Son of Strength, all men call happy in his God, His offerings, and his sacred grass.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Hitherward shalt thou bring these Gods to our laudation and to taste. These offered gifts, fair-shining One.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When, Agni, on thine embassage thou goest not a sound is heard of steed or straining of thy car.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Aided by thee uninjured, strong, one after other, goes he forth: Agni, the offerer forward steps.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: And splendid strength, heroic, high, Agni, thou grantest from the Gods, Thou God, to him who offers gifts.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: ACCEPT our loudest-sounding hymn, food most delightful to the Gods, Pouring our offerings in thy mouth.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Now, Agni, will we say to thee, O wisest and best Angiras, Our precious, much-availing prayer.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Who, Agni, is thy kin, of men? who is thy worthy worshipper? On whom dependent? who art thou?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The kinsman, Agni, of mankind, their well beloved Friend art thou, A Friend whom friends may supplicate.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Bring to us Mitra, Varuna, bring the Gods to mighty sacrifice. Bring them, O Agni, to thine home.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: How may the mind draw nigh to please thee, Agni? What hymn of praise shall bring us greatest blessing? Or who hath gained thy power by sacrifices? or with what mind shall we bring thee oblations?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Come hither, Agni; sit thee down as Hotar; be thou who never wast deceived our leader. May Heaven and Earth, the all-pervading, love thee: worship the Gods to win for us their favour.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Burn thou up all the Raksasas, O Agni; ward thou off curses from our sacrifices. Bring hither with his Bays the Lord of Soma: here is glad welcome for the Bounteous Giver.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou Priest with lip and voice that bring us children hast been invoked. Here with the Gods be seated. Thine is the task of Cleanser and Presenter: waken us, Wealth-bestower and Producer.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: As with oblations of the priestly Manus thou worshippedst the Gods, a Sage with sages, So now, O truthfullest Invoker Agni, worship this day with joy-bestowing ladle.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: How shall we pay oblation unto Agni? What hymn, Godloved, is said to him refulgent? Who, deathless, true to Law, mid men a herald, bringeth the Gods as best of sacrificers?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Bring him with reverence hither, most propitious in sacrifices, true to Law, the herald; For Agni, when he seeks the Gods for mortals, knows them full well and worships them in spirit.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: For he is mental power, a man, and perfect; he is the bringer, friend-like, of the wondrous. The pious Aryan tribes at sacrifices address them first to him who doeth marvels.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May Agni, foe-destroyer, manliest Hero, accept with love our hymns and our devotion. So may the liberal lords whose strength is strongest, urged by their riches, stir our thoughts with vigour.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thus Agni Jatavedas, true to Order, hath by the priestly Gotamas been lauded. May he augment in them splendour and vigour: observant, as he lists, he gathers increase.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O JATAVEDAS, keen and swift, we Gotamas with sacred song exalt thee for thy glories' sake.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thee, as thou art, desiring wealth Gotama worships with his song: We laud thee for thy glories' sake.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: As such, like Angiras we call on thee best winner of the spoil: We laud thee for thy glories' sake.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thee, best of Vrtra-slayers, thee who shakest off our Dasyu foes: We laud thee for thy glories' sake.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: A pleasant song to Agni we, sons of Rahugana, have sung: We laud thee for thy glories' sake.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: HE in mid-air's expanse hath golden tresses; a raging serpent, like the rushing tempest: Purely refulgent, knowing well the morning; like honourable dames, true, active workers.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thy well-winged flashes strengthen in their manner, when the black Bull hath bellowed round about us. With drops that bless and seem to smile he cometh: the waters fall, the clouds utter their thunder.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When he comes streaming with the milk of worship, conducting by directest paths of Order Aryaman, Mitra, Varuna, Parijman fill the hide full where lies the nether press-stone.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Agni, thou who art the lord of wealth in kine, thou Son of Strength, Vouchsafe to us, O Jatavedas, high renown.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He, Agni, kindled, good and wise, must be exalted in our song: Shine, thou of many forms, shine radiantly on us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Agni, shining of thyself by night and when the morning breaks, Burn, thou whose teeth are sharp, against the Raksasas.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Adorable in all our rites, favour us, Agni, with thine aid, When the great hymn is chanted forth.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Bring to us ever-conquering wealth, wealth, Agni, worthy of our choice, In all our frays invincible.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Give us, O Agni, through thy grace wealth that supporteth all our life, Thy favour so that we may live.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Gotama, desiring bliss present thy songs composed with care To Agni of the pointed flames.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May the man fall, O Agni, who near or afar assaileth us: Do thou increase and prosper us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Keen and swift Agni, thousand-eyed, chaseth the Raksasas afar: He singeth, herald meet for lauds.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: THUS in the Soma, in wild joy the Brahman hath exalted thee: Thou, mightiest thunder-armed, hast driven by force the Dragon from the earth, lauding thine own imperial sway.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The mighty flowing Soma-draught, brought by the Hawk, hath gladdened thee, That in thy strength, O Thunderer, thou hast struck down Vrtra from the floods, lauding thine own imperial sway.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Go forward, meet the foe, be bold; thy bolt of thunder is not checked. Manliness, Indra, is thy might: stay Vrtra, make the waters thine, lauding thine own imperial sway.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou smotest Vrtra from the earth, smotest him, Indra, from the sky. Let these life-fostering waters flow attended by the Marut host, lauding thine own imperial sway.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The wrathful Indra with his bolt of thunder rushing on the foe, Smote fierce on trembling Vrtra's back, and loosed the waters free to run, lauding his own imperial sway.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With hundred-jointed thunderbolt Indra hath struck him on the back, And, while rejoicing in the juice, seeketh prosperity for friends, lauding his own imperial sway.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Indra, unconquered might is thine, Thunderer, Caster of the Stone; For thou with thy surpassing power smotest to death the guileful beast, lauding thine own imperial sway.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Far over ninety spacious floods thy thunderbolts were cast abroad: Great, Indra, is thy hero might, and strength is seated in thine arms, lauding thine own imperial sway.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Laud him a thousand all at once, shout twenty forth the hymn of praise. Hundreds have sung aloud to him, to Indra hath the prayer been raised, lauding his own imperial sway.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Indra hath smitten down the power of Vrtra,--might with stronger might. This was his manly exploit, he slew Vrtra and let loose the floods, lauding his own imperial sway.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Yea, even this great Pair of Worlds trembled in terror at thy wrath, When, Indra, Thunderer, Marut-girt, thou slewest Vrtra in thy strength, lauding thine own imperial sway.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: But Vrtra scared not Indra with his shaking or his thunder roar. On him that iron thunderbolt fell fiercely with its thousand points, lauding his own imperial sway.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When with the thunder thou didst make thy dart and Vrtra meet in war, Thy might, O Indra, fain to slay the Dragon, was set firm in heaven, lauding thine own imperial sway.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When at thy shout, O Thunder-armed, each thing both fixed and moving shook, E'en Tvastar trembled at thy wrath and quaked with fear because of thee, lauding thine own imperial sway.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: There is not, in our knowledge, one who passeth Indra in his strength: In him the Deities have stored manliness, insight, power and might, lauding his own imperial sway.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Still as of old, whatever rite Atharvan, Manus sire of all, Dadhyach performed, their prayer and praise united in that Indra meet, lauding his own imperial sway.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: THE men have lifted Indra up, the Vrtra slayer, to joy and strength: Him, verily, we invocate in battles whether great or small: be he our aid in deeds of might.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou, Hero, art a warrior, thou art giver of abundant spoil. Strengthening e'en the feeble, thou aidest the sacrificer, thou givest the offerer ample wealth.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When war and battles are on foot, booty is laid before the bold. Yoke thou thy wildly-rushing Bays. Whom wilt thou slay and whom enrich? Do thou, O Indra, make us rich.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Mighty through wisdom, as he lists, terrible, he hath waxed in strength. Lord of Bay Steeds, strong-jawed, sublime, he in joined hands for glory's sake hath grasped his iron thunderbolt.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He filled the earthly atmosphere and pressed against the lights in heaven. None like thee ever hath been born, none, Indra, will be born like thee. Thou hast waxed mighty over all.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May he who to the offerer gives the foeman's man-sustaining food, May Indra lend his aid to us. Deal forth--abundant is thy wealth--that in thy bounty I may share.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He, righteous-hearted, at each time of rapture gives us herds of kine. Gather in both thy hands for us treasures of many hundred sorts. Sharpen thou us, and bring us wealth.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Refresh thee, Hero, with the juice outpoured for bounty and for strength. We know thee Lord of ample store, to thee have sent our hearts' desires: be therefore our Protector thou.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: These people, Indra, keep for thee all that is worthy of thy choice. Discover thou, as Lord, the wealth of men who offer up no gifts: bring thou to us this wealth of theirs.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: GRACIOUSLY listen to our songs, Maghavan, be not negligent. As thou hast made us full of joy and lettest us solicit thee, now, Indra, yoke thy two Bay Steeds.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Well have they eaten and rejoiced; the friends have risen and passed away. The sages luminous in themselves have. praised thee with their latest hymn. Now, Indra, yoke thy two Bay Steeds.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Maghavan, we will reverence thee who art so fair to look upon. Thus praised, according to our wish come now with richly laden car. Now, Indra, yoke thy two Bay Steeds.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He will in very truth ascend the powerful car that finds the kine, Who thinks upon the well-filled bowl, the Tawny Coursers' harnesser. Now, Indra, yoke thy two Bay Steeds.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Let, Lord of Hundred Powers, thy Steeds be harnessed on the right and left. Therewith in rapture of the juice, draw near to thy beloved Spouse. Now, Indra, yoke thy two Bay Steeds.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With holy prayer I yoke thy long-maned pair of Bays: come hitherward; thou holdest them in both thy hands. The stirring draughts of juice outpoured have made thee glad: thou, Thunderer, hast rejoiced with Pusan and thy Spouse.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: INDRA, the mortal man well guarded by thine aid goes foremost in the wealth of horses and of kine. With amplest wealth thou fillest him, as round about the waters clearly seen afar fill Sindhu full.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The heavenly Waters come not nigh the priestly bowl: they but look down and see how far mid-air is spread: The Deities conduct the pious man to them: like suitors they delight in him who loveth prayer.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Praiseworthy blessing hast thou laid upon the pair who with uplifted ladle serve thee, man and wife. Unchecked he dwells and prospers in thy law: thy power brings blessing to the sacrificer pouring gifts.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: First the Angirases won themselves vital power, whose fires were kindled through good deeds and sacrifice. The men together found the Pani's hoarded wealth, the cattle, and the wealth in horses and in kine.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Atharvan first by sacrifices laid the paths then, guardian of the Law, sprang up the loving Sun. Usana Kavya straightway hither drove the kine. Let us with offerings honour Yama's deathless birth.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When sacred grass is trimmed to aid the auspicious work, or the hymn makes its voice of praise sound to the sky. Where the stone rings as 'twere a singer skilled in laud,--Indra in truth delights when these come near to him.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Soma hath been pressed for thee, O Indra; mightiest, bold One, come. May Indra-vigour fill thee full, as the Sun fills mid-air with rays.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: His pair of Tawny Coursers bring Indra of unresisted might Hither to Rsis' songs of praise and sacrifice performed by men.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Slayer of Vrtra, mount thy car; thy Bay Steeds have been yoked by prayer. May, with its voice, the pressing-stone draw thine attention hitherward.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: This poured libation, Indra, drink, immortal, gladdening, excellent. Streams of the bright have flowed to thee here at the seat of holy Law.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Sing glory now to Indra, say to him your solemn eulogies. The drops poured forth have made him glad: pay reverence to his might supreme.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When, Indra, thou dost yoke thy Steeds, there is no better charioteer: None hath surpassed thee in thy might, none with good steeds o'ertaken thee.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He who alone bestoweth on mortal man who offereth gifts, The ruler of resistless power, is Indra, sure.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When will he trample, like a weed, the man who hath no gift for him? When, verily, will Indra hear our songs of praise?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He who with Soma juice prepared amid the many honours thee,-- Verily Indra gains thereby tremendous might.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The juice of Soma thus diffused, sweet to the taste, the bright cows drink, Who for the sake of splendour close to mighty Indra's side rejoice, good in their own supremacy.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Craving his touch the dappled kine mingle the Soma with their milk. The milch-kine dear to Indra send forth his death-dealing thunderbolt, good in their own supremacy.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With veneration, passing wise, honouring his victorious might, They follow close his many laws to win them due preeminence, good in their own supremacy.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With bones of Dadhyac for his arms, Indra, resistless in attack, Struck nine-and-ninety Vrtras dead.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He, searching for the horse's head, removed among the mountains, found At Saryanavan what he sought.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Then verily they recognized the essential form of Tvastar's Bull, Here in the mansion of the Moon.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Who yokes to-day unto the pole of Order the strong and passionate steers of checkless spirit, With shaft-armed mouths, heart-piercing, health-bestowing? Long shall he live who richly pays their service.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Who fleeth forth? who suffereth? who feareth? Who knoweth Indra present, Indra near us? Who sendeth benediction on his offspring, his household, wealth and person, and the People?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Who with poured oil and offering honours Agni, with ladle worships at appointed seasons? To whom to the Gods bring oblation quickly? What offerer, God-favoured, knows him thoroughly?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou as a God, O Mightiest, verily blessest mortal man. O Maghavan, there is no comforter but thou: Indra, I speak my words to thee.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Let not thy bounteous gifts, let not thy saving help fail us, good Lord, at any time; And measure out to us, thou lover of mankind, all riches hitherward from men.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: THEY who are glancing forth, like women, on their way, doers of mighty deeds, swift racers, Rudra's Sons, The Maruts have made heaven and earth increase and grow: in sacrifices they delight, the strong and wild.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Grown to their perfect strength greatness have they attained; the Rudras have established their abode in heaven. Singing their song of praise and generating might, they have put glory on, the Sons whom Prsni bare.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When, Children of the Cow, they shine in bright attire, and on their fair limbs lay their golden ornaments, They drive away each adversary from their path, and, following their traces, fatness floweth down,
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When, mighty Warriors, ye who glitter with your spears, o'erthrowing with your strength e'en what is ne'er o'erthrown, When, O ye Maruts, ye the host that send the rain, had harnessed to your cars the thought-fleet spotted deer.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When ye have harnessed to your cars the spotted deer, urging the thunderbolt, O Maruts, to the fray, Forth rush the torrents of the dark red stormy cloud, and moisten, like a skin, the earth with water-floods.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Let your swift-gliding coursers bear you hitherward with their fleet pinions. Come ye forward with your arms. Sit on the grass; a wide seat hath been made for you: delight yourselves, O Maruts, in the pleasant food.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Strong in their native strength to greatness have they grown, stepped to the firmament and made their dwelling wide. When Visnu saved the Soma bringing wild delight, the Maruts sate like birds on their dear holy grass.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: In sooth like heroes fain for fight they rush about, like combatants fame-seeking have they striven in war. Before the Maruts every creature is afraid: the men are like to Kings, terrible to behold.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When Tvastar deft of hand had turned the thunderbolt, golden, with thousand edges, fashioned more skilfully, Indra received it to perform heroic deeds. Vrtra he slew, and forced the flood of water forth.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: They with their vigorous strength pushed the well up on high, and clove the cloud in twain though it was passing strong. The Maruts, bounteous Givers, sending forth their voice, in the wild joy of Soma wrought their glorious deeds.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: They drave the cloud transverse directed hitherward, and poured the fountain forth for thirsting Gotama. Shining with varied light they come to him with help: they with their might fulfilled the longing of the sage.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The shelters which ye have for him who lauds you, bestow them threefold on the man who offers. Extend the same boons unto us, ye Maruts. Give us, O Heroes, wealth with noble offspring.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: THE best of guardians hath that man within whose dwelling place ye drink, O Maruts, giants of the sky.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Honoured with sacrifice or with the worship of the sages' hymns, O Maruts, listen to the call.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Yea, the strong man to whom ye have vouchsafed to give a sage, shall move Into a stable rich in kine.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Upon this hero's sacred grass Soma is poured in daily rites: Praise and delight are sung aloud.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Let the strong Maruts hear him, him surpassing all men: strength be his That reaches even to the Sun.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: For, through the swift Gods' loving help, in many an autumn, Maruts, we Have offered up our sacrifice.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Fortunate shall that mortal be, O Maruts most adorable, Whose offerings ye bear away.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Heroes truly strong, ye know the toil of him who sings your praise, The heart's desire of him who loves.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O ye of true strength, make this thing manifest by your greatness: strike The demon with your thunderbolt.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Conceal the horrid darkness, drive far from us each devouring fiend. Create the light for which we long.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: LOUD Singers, never humbled, active, full of strength, immovable, impetuous, manliest, best-beloved, They have displayed themselves with glittering ornaments, a few in number only, like the heavens with stars.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When, Maruts, on the steeps ye pile the moving cloud, ye are like birds on whatsoever path it be. Clouds everywhere shed forth the rain upon your cars. Drop fatness, honey-hued, for him who sings your praise.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Earth at their racings trembles as if weak and worn, when on their ways they yoke their cars for victory. They, sportive, loudly roaring, armed with glittering spears, shakers of all, themselves admire their mightiness.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Self-moving is that youthful band, with spotted steeds; thus it hath lordly sway, endued with power and might. Truthful art thou, and blameless, searcher out of sin: so thou, Strong Host, wilt be protector of this prayer.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: We speak by our descent from our primeval Sire; our tongue, when we behold the Soma, stirs itself. When, shouting, they had joined Indra in toil of fight, then only they obtained their sacrificial names.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Splendours they gained for glory, they who wear bright rings; rays they obtained, and men to celebrate their praise. Armed with their swords, impetuous and fearing naught, they have possessed the Maruts' own beloved home.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: COME hither, Maruts, on your lightning laden cars, sounding with sweet songs, armed with lances, winged with steeds. Fly unto us with noblest food, like birds, O ye of mighty power.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With their red-hued or, haply, tawny coursers which speed their chariots on, they come for glory. Brilliant like gold is he who holds the thunder. Earth have they smitten with the chariot's felly.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: For beauty ye have swords upon your bodies. As they stir woods so may they stir our spirits. For your sake, O ye Maruts very mighty and well-born, have they set the stone, in motion.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The days went round you and came back O yearners, back, to this prayer and to this solemn worship. The Gotamas making their prayer with singing have pushed the well's lid up to drink the water.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: No hymn way ever known like this aforetime which Gotama sang forth for you, O Maruts, What time upon your golden wheels he saw you, wild boars rushing about with tusks of iron.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To you this freshening draught of Soma rusheth, O Maruts, like the voice of one who prayeth. It rusheth freely from our hands as these libations wont to flow.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: MAY powers auspicious come to us from every side, never deceived, unhindered, and victorious, That the Gods ever may be with us for our gain, our guardians day by day unceasing in their care.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May the auspicious favour of the Gods be ours, on us descend the bounty of the righteous Gods. The friendship of the Gods have we devoutly sought: so may the Gods extend our life that we may live.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: We call them hither with a hymn of olden time, Bhaga, the friendly Daksa, Mitra, Aditi, Aryaman, Varuna, Soma, the Asvins. May Sarasvati, auspicious, grant felicity.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May the Wind waft to us that pleasant medicine, may Earth our Mother give it, and our Father Heaven, And the joy-giving stones that press the Soma's juice. Asvins, may ye, for whom our spirits long, hear this.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Him we invoke for aid who reigns supreme, the Lord of all that stands or moves, inspirer of the soul, That Pusan may promote the increase of our wealth, our keeper and our guard infallible for our good.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Illustrious far and wide, may Indra prosper us: may Pusan prosper us, the Master of all wealth. May Tarksya with uninjured fellies prosper us: Brhaspati vouchsafe to us prosperity.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Maruts, Sons of Prsni, borne by spotted steeds, moving in glory, oft visiting holy rites, Sages whose tongue is Agni, brilliant as the Sun,--hither let all the Gods for our protection come.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Gods, may we with our ears listen to what is good, and with our eyes see what is good, ye Holy Ones. With limbs and bodies firm may we extolling you attain the term of life appointed by the Gods.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: A hundred autumns stand before us, O ye Gods, within whose space ye bring our bodies to decay; Within whose space our sons become fathers in turn. Break ye not in the midst our course of fleeting life.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Aditi is the heaven, Aditi is mid-air, Aditi is the Mother and the Sire and Son. Aditi is all Gods, Aditi five-classed men, Aditi all that hath been born and shall be born.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary
