verses.translation: MAY Varuna with guidance straight, and Mitra lead us, he who knows, And Aryaman in accord with Gods.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: For they are dealers forth of wealth, and, not deluded, with their might Guard evermore the holy laws.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Shelter may they vouchsafe to us, Immortal Gods to mortal men, Chasing our enemies away.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May they mark out our paths to bliss, Indra, the Maruts, Pusan, and Bhaga, the Gods to be adored.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Yea, Pusan, Visnu, ye who run your course, enrich our hymns with kine; Bless us with all prosperity.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The winds waft sweets, the rivers pour sweets for the man who keeps the Law So may the plants be sweet for us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Sweet be the night and sweet the dawns, sweet the terrestrial atmosphere; Sweet be our Father Heaven to us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May the tall tree be full of sweets for us, and full of sweets the Sun: May our milch-kine be sweet for us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Be Mitra gracious unto us, and Varuna and Aryaman: Indra, Brhaspati be kind, and Visnu of the mighty stride.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou, Soma, art preeminent for wisdom; along the straightest path thou art our leader. Our wise forefathers by thy guidance, Indu, dealt out among the Gods their share of treasure.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou by thine insight art most wise, O Soma, strong by thine energies and all possessing, Mighty art thou by all thy powers and greatness, by glories art thou glorious, guide of mortals.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thine are King Varuna's eternal statutes, lofty and deep, O Soma, is thy glory. All-pure art thou like Mitra the beloved, adorable, like Aryaman, O Soma.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With all thy glories on the earth, in heaven, on mountains, in the plants, and in the waters,-- With all of these, well-pleased and not in anger, accept, O royal Soma, our oblations.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou, Soma, art the Lord of heroes, King, yea, Vrtra-slayer thou: Thou art auspicious energy.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: And, Soma, let it be thy wish that we may live and may not die: Praise-loving Lord of plants art thou.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To him who keeps the law, both old and young, thou givest happiness, And energy that he may live.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Guard us, King Soma, on all sides from him who threatens us: never let The friend of one like thee be harmed.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With those delightful aids which thou hast, Soma, for the worshipper,-- Even with those protect thou us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Accepting this our sacrifice and this our praise, O Soma, come, And be thou nigh to prosper us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Well-skilled in speech we magnify thee, Soma, with our sacred songs: Come thou to us, most gracious One.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Enricher, healer of disease, wealth-finder, prospering our store, Be, Soma, a good Friend to us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Soma, be happy in our heart, as milch-kine in the grassy meads, As a young man in his own house.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Soma, God, the mortal man who in thy friendship hath delight, Him doth the mighty Sage befriend.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Save us from slanderous reproach, keep us., O Soma, from distress: Be unto us a gracious Friend.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Soma, wax great. From every side may vigorous powers unite in thee: Be in the gathering-place of strength.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Wax, O most gladdening Soma, great through all thy rays of light, and be A Friend of most illustrious fame to prosper us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: In thee be juicy nutriments united, and powers and mighty foe-subduing vigour, Waxing to immortality, O Soma: win highest glories for thyself in heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Such of thy glories as with poured oblations men honour, may they all invest our worship. Wealth-giver, furtherer with troops of heroes, sparing the brave, come, Soma, to our houses.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To him who worships Soma gives the milch-cow, a fleet steed and a man of active knowledge, Skilled in home duties, meet for holy synod, for council meet, a glory to his father.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Invincible in fight, saver in battles, guard of our camp, winner of light and water, Born amid hymns, well-housed, exceeding famous, victor, in thee will we rejoice, O Soma.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: These herbs, these milch-kine, and these running waters, all these, O Soma, thou hast generated. The spacious firmament hast thou expanded, and with the light thou hast dispelled the darkness.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Do thou, God Soma, with thy Godlike spirit, victorious, win for us a share of riches. Let none prevent thee: thou art Lord of valour. Provide for both sides in the fray for booty.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: THESE Dawns have raised their banner; in the eastern half of the mid-air they spread abroad their shining light. Like heroes who prepare their weapons for the war, onward they come bright red in hue, the Mother Cows.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Readily have the purple beams of light shot up; the Red Cows have they harnessed, easy to be yoked. The Dawns have brought distinct perception as before: red-hued, they have attained their fulgent brilliancy.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: They sing their song like women active in their tasks, along their common path hither from far away, Bringing refreshment to the liberal devotee, yea, all things to the worshipper who pours the juice.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: She, like a dancer, puts her broidered garments on: as a cow yields her udder so she bares her breast. Creating light for all the world of life, the Dawn hath laid the darkness open as the cows their stall.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: We have beheld the brightness of her shining; it spreads and drives away the darksome monster. Like tints that deck the Post at sacrifices, Heaven's Daughter hath attained her wondrous splendour.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: We have o'erpast the limit of this darkness; Dawn breaking forth again brings clear perception. She like a flatterer smiles in light for glory, and fair of face hath wakened to rejoice us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Gotamas have praised Heaven's radiant Daughter, the leader of the charm of pleasant voices. Dawn, thou conferrest on us strength with offspring and men, conspicuous with kine and horses.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O thou who shinest forth in wondrous glory, urged onward by thy strength, auspicious Lady, Dawn, may I gain that wealth, renowned and ample, in brave sons, troops of slaves, far-famed for horses.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Bending her looks on all the world, the Goddess shines, widely spreading with her bright eye westward. Waking to motion every living creature, she understands the voice of each adorer.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Ancient of days, again again born newly, decking her beauty with the self-same raiment. The Goddess wastes away the life of mortals, like a skilled hunter cutting birds in pieces.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: She hath appeared discovering heaven's borders: to the far distance she drives off her Sister. Diminishing the days of human creatures, the Lady shines with all her lover's splendour.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The bright, the blessed One shines forth extending her rays like kine, as a flood rolls his waters. Never transgressing the divine commandments, she is beheld visible with the sunbeams.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Dawn enriched with ample wealth, bestow on us the wondrous gift Wherewith we may support children and children's sons.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou radiant mover of sweet sounds, with wealth of horses and of kine Shine thou on us this day, O Dawn auspiciously.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Dawn enriched with holy rites, yoke to thy car thy purple steeds, And then bring thou unto us all felicities.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Asvins wonderful in act, do ye unanimous direct Your chariot to our home wealthy in kine and gold.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Ye who brought down the hymn from heaven, a light that giveth light to man, Do ye, O Asvins, bring strength hither unto us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Hither may they who wake at dawn bring, to drink Soma both the Gods Health-givers Wonder-Workers, borne on paths of gold.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: AGNI and Soma, mighty Pair, graciously hearken to my call, Accept in friendly wise my hymn, and prosper him who offers gifts.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The man who honours you to-day, Agni and Soma, with this hymn, Bestow on him heroic strength, increase of kine, and noble steeds.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The man who offers holy oil and burnt oblations unto you, Agni and Soma, shall enjoy great strength, with offspring, all his life.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Agni and Soma, famed is that your. prowess wherewith ye stole the kine, his food, from Pani. Ye caused the brood of Brsaya to perish; ye found the light, the single light for many.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Agni and Soma, joined in operation ye have set up the shining lights in heaven. From curse and from reproach, Agni and Soma, ye freed the rivers that were bound in fetters.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: One of you Matarisvan brought from heaven, the Falcon rent the other from the mountain. Strengthened by holy prayer Agni and Soma have made us ample room for sacrificing.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Taste, Agni, Soma, this prepared oblation; accept it, Mighty Ones, and let it please you. Vouchsafe us good protection and kind favour: grant to the sacrificer health and riches.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Whoso with oil and poured oblation honours, with God-devoted heart, Agni and Soma,-- Protect his sacrifice, preserve him from distress, grant to the sacrificer great felicity.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Invoked together, mates in wealth, Agni-Soma, accept our hymns: Together be among the Gods.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Agni and Soma, unto him who worships you with holy oil Shine forth an ample recompense.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Agni and Soma, be ye pleased with these oblations brought to you, And come, together, nigh to us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Agni and Soma, cherish well our horses, and let our cows be fat who yield oblations. Grant power to us and to our wealthy patrons, and cause our holy rites to be successful.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: FOR Jatavedas worthy of our praise will we frame with our mind this eulogy as 'twere a car. For good, in his assembly, is this care of ours. Let us not, in thy friendship, Agni, suffer harm.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The man for whom thou sacrificest prospereth, dwelleth without a foe, gaineth heroic might. He waxeth strong, distress never approacheth him. Let us not, in thy friendship, Agni, suffer harm.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May we have power to kindle thee. Fulfil our thoughts. In thee the Gods eat the presented offering, Bring hither the Adityas, for we long for them. Let us not in thy friendship, Agni, suffer harm.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: We will bring fuel and prepare burnt offerings, reminding thee at each successive festival. Fulfil our thought that so we may prolong our lives. Let us not in thy friendship, Agni, suffer harm.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: His ministers move forth, the guardians of the folk, protecting quadruped and biped with their rays. Mighty art thou, the wondrous herald of the Dawn. Let us not in thy friendship, Agni, suffer harm.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou art Presenter and the chief Invoker, thou Director, Purifier, great High Priest by birth. Knowing all priestly work thou perfectest it, Sage. Let us not in thy friendship, Agni, suffer harm.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Lovely of form art thou, alike on every side; though far, thou shinest brightly as if close at hand. O God, thou seest through even the dark of night. Let us not in thy friendship, Agni, suffer harm.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Gods, foremost be his car who pours libations out, and let our hymn prevail o'er evil-hearted men. Attend to this our speech and make it prosper well. Let us not in thy friendship, Agni, suffer harm.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Smite with thy weapons those of evil speech and thought, devouring demons, whether near or far away. Then to the singer give free way for sacrifice. Let us not in thy friendship, Agni, suffer harm.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When to thy chariot thou hadst yoked two red steeds and two ruddy steeds, wind-sped, thy roar was like a bull's. Thou with smoke-bannered flame attackest forest trees. Let us not in thy friendship, Agni, suffer harm.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Then at thy roar the very birds are terrified, when, eating-up the grass, thy sparks fly forth abroad. Then is it easy for thee and thy car to pass. Let us not in thy friendship, Agni, suffer harm.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He hath the Power to soothe Mitra and Varuna: wonderful is the Maruts' wrath when they descend. Be gracious; let their hearts he turned to us again. Let us not in thy friendship, Agni, suffer harm.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou art a God, thou art the wondrous Friend of Gods, the Vasu of the Vasus, fair in sacrifice. Under, thine own most wide protection may we dwell. Let us not in thy friendship, Agni, suffer harm.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: This is thy grace that, kindled in thine own abode, invoked with Soma thou soundest forth most benign, Thou givest wealth and treasure to the worshipper. Let us not in thy friendship, Agni, suffer harm.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To whom thou, Lord of goodly riches, grantest freedom from every sin with perfect wholeness, Whom with good strength thou quikenest, with children and wealth--may we be they, Eternal Being.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Such, Agni, thou who knowest all good fortune, God, lengthen here the days of our existence. This prayer of ours may Varuna grant, and Mitra, and Aditi and Sindhu, Earth and Heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To fair goals travel Two unlike in semblance: each in succession nourishes an infant. One bears a Godlike Babe of golden colour; bright and fair-shining, is he with the other.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Tvastar's ten daughters, vigilant and youthful, produced this Infant borne to sundry quarters. They bear around him whose long flames are pointed, fulgent among mankind with native splendour.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Three several places of his birth they honour, in mid-air, in the heaven, and in the waters. Governing in the east of earthly regions, the seasons hath he stablished in their order.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Who of you knows this secret One? The Infant by his own nature hath brought forth his Mothers. The germ of many, from the waters' bosom he goes forth, wise and great, of Godlike nature.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Visible, fair, he grows in native brightness uplifted in the lap of waving waters. When he was born both Tvastar's worlds were frightened: they turn to him and reverence the Lion.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Two auspicious Ones, like women, tend him: like lowing cows they seek him in their manner. He is the Lord of Might among the mighty; him, on the right, they balm with their oblations.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Like Savitar his arms with might he stretches; awful, he strives grasping the world's two borders. He forces out from all a brilliant vesture, yea, from his Mothers draws he forth new raiment.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He makes him a most noble form of splendour, decking him in his home with milk and waters. The Sage adorns the depths of air with wisdom: this is the meeting where the Gods are worshipped.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Wide through the firmament spreads forth triumphant the far-resplendent strength of thee the Mighty. Kindled by us do thou preserve us, Agni, with all thy self-bright undiminished succours.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: In dry spots he makes stream, and course, and torrent, and inundates the earth with floods that glisten. All ancient things within his maw he gathers, and moves among the new fresh-sprouting grasses.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Fed with our fuel, purifying Agni, so blaze to us auspiciously for glory. This prayer of ours may Varuna grant, and Mitra, and Aditi and Sindhu, Earth and Heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: HE in the ancient way by strength engendered, lo! straight hath taken to himself all wisdom. The waters and the bowl have made him friendly. The Gods possessed the wealth bestowing Agni.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: At Ayu's ancient call he by his wisdom gave all this progeny of men their being, And, by refulgent light, heaven and the waters. The Gods possessed the wealth bestowing Agni.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Praise him, ye Aryan folk, as chief performer of sacrifice adored and ever toiling, Well-tended, Son of Strength, the Constant Giver. The Gods possessed the wealth bestowing Agni.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: That Matarisvan rich in wealth and treasure, light-winner, finds a pathway for his offspring. Guard of our folk, Father of earth and heaven. The Gods possessed the wealth bestowing Agni.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Night and Dawn, changing each the other's colour, meeting together suckle one same Infant: Golden between the heaven and earth he shineth. The Gods possessed the wealth bestowing Agni.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Root of wealth, gathering-place of treasures, banner of sacrifice, who grants the suppliant's wishes: Preserving him as their own life immortal, the Gods possessed the wealth-bestowing Agni.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Now and of old the home of wealth, the mansion of what is born and what was born aforetime, Guard of what is and what will be hereafter,--the Gods possessed the wealth bestowing Agni.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May the Wealth-Giver grant us conquering riches; may the Wealth-Giver grant us wealth with heroes. May the Wealth-Giver grant us food with offspring, and length of days may the Wealth-Giver send us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Fed with our fuel, purifying Agni, so blaze to us auspiciously for glory. This prayer of ours may Varuna grant, and Mitra, and Aditi and Sindhu, Earth and Heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Chasing with light our sin away, O Agni, shine thou wealth on us. May his light chase our sin away.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: For goodly fields, for pleasant homes, for wealth we sacrifice to thee. May his light chase our sin away.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Best praiser of all these be he; foremost, our chiefs who sacrifice. May his light chase our sin away.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: So that thy worshippers and we, thine, Agni, in our sons may live. May his light chase our sin away.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: As ever-conquering Agni's beams of splendour go to every side, May his light chase our sin away.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To every side thy face is turned, thou art triumphant everywhere. May his light chase our sin away.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O thou whose face looks every way, bear us past foes as in a ship. May his light chase our sin away.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: As in a ship, convey thou us for our advantage o'er the flood. May his light chase our sin away.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Still in Vaisvanara's grace may we continue: yea, he is King supreme o'er all things living. Sprung hence to life upon this All he looketh. Vaisvanara hath rivalry with Surya.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Present in heaven, in earth, all-present Agni,--all plants that grow on ground hath he pervaded. May Agni, may Vaisvanara with vigour, present, preserve us day and night from foemen.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Be this thy truth, Vaisvanara, to us-ward: let wealth in rich abundance gather round us. This prayer of ours may Varuna grant, and Mitra, and Aditi and Sindhu, Earth and Heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: FOR Jatavedas let us press the Soma: may he consume the wealth of the malignant. May Agni carry us through all our troubles, through grief as in a boat across the river.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: MAY he who hath his home with strength, the Mighty, the King supreme of earth and spacious heaven, Lord of true power, to he invoked in battles,--may Indra, girt by Maruts, be our succour.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Whose way is unattainable like Surya's: he in each fight is the strong Vrtra-slayer, Mightiest with his Friends in his own courses. May Indra, girt by Maruts, be our succour.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Whose paths go forth in their great might resistless, forth milking, as it were, heaven's genial moisture. With manly strength triumphant, foe-subduer,--may Indra, girt by Maruts, be our succour.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Among Angirases he was the chiefest, a Friend with friends, mighty amid the mighty. Praiser mid praisers, honoured most of singers. May Indra, girt by Maruts, be our succour.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Strong with the Rudras as with his own children, in manly battle conquering his foemen ' With his close comrades doing deeds of glory,--may Indra, girt by Maruts, be our succour.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Humbler of pride, exciter of the conflict, the Lord of heroes, God invoked of many, May he this day gain with our men the sunlight. May Indra, girt by Maruts, be our succour.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: His help hath made him cheerer in the battle, the folk have made him guardian of their comfort. Sole Lord is he of every holy service. May Indra, girt by Maruts, be our succour.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To him the Hero, on high days of prowess, heroes for help and booty shall betake them. He hath found light even in the blinding darkness. May Indra, girt by Maruts, be our succour.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He with his left hand checketh even the mighty, and with his right hand gathereth up the booty. Even with the humble he acquireth riches. May Indra, girt by Maruts, be our succour.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With hosts on foot and cars he winneth treasures: well is he known this day by all the people. With manly might he conquereth those who hate him. May Indra, girt by Maruts, be our succour.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When in his ways with kinsmen or with strangers he speedeth to the fight, invoked of many, For gain of waters, and of sons and grandsons, may Indra, girt by Maruts, be our succour.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Awful and fierce, fiend-slayer, thunder-wielder, with boundless knowledge, hymned by hundreds, mighty, In strength like Soma, guard of the Five Peoples, may Indra, girt by Maruts, be our succour.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Winning the light, hitherward roars his thunder like the terrific mighty voice of Heaven. Rich gifts and treasures evermore attend him. May Indra, girt by Maruts, be our succour.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Whose home eternal through his strength surrounds him on every side, his laud, the earth and heaven, May he, delighted with our service, save us. May Indra, girt by Maruts, be our succour.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The limit of whose power not Gods by Godhead, nor mortal men have reached, nor yet the Waters. Both Earth and Heaven in vigour he surpasseth. May Indra, girt by Maruts, he our succour.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The red and tawny mare, blaze-marked, high standing, celestial who, to bring Rjrasva riches, Drew at the pole the chariot yoked with stallions, joyous, among the hosts of men was noted.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Varsagiras unto thee, O Indra, the Mighty One, sing forth this laud to please thee, Rjrasva with his fellows, Ambarisa, Suradhas, Sahadeva, Bhayamana.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He, much invoked, hath slain Dasyus and Simyus, after his wont, and laid them low with arrows. The mighty Thunderer with his fair-complexioned friends won the land, the sunlight, and the waters.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May Indra evermore be our protector, and unimperilled may we win the booty. This prayer of ours may Varuna grant, and Mitra, and Aditi and Sindhu, Earth and Heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: SING, with oblation, praise to him who maketh glad, who with Rjisvan drove the dusky brood away. Fain for help, him the strong whose right hand wields the bolt, him girt by Maruts we invoke to be our Friend.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Indra, who with triumphant wrath smote Vyamsa down, and Sambara, and Pipru the unrighteous one; Who extirpated Susna the insatiate,--him girt by Maruts we invoke to be our Friend.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He whose great work of manly might is heaven and earth, and Varuna and Surya keep his holy law; Indra, whose law the rivers follow as they flow,--him girt by Maruts we invoke to be our Friend.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He who is Lord and Master of the steeds and kine, honoured--the firm and sure--at every holy act; Stayer even of the strong who pours no offering out,--him girt by Maruts we invoke to be our Friend.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He who is Lord of all the world that moves and breathes, who for the Brahman first before all found the Cows; Indra who cast the Dasyus down beneath his feet,--him girt by Maruts we invoke to be our Friend.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Whom cowards must invoke and valiant men of war, invoked by those who conquer and by those who flee; Indra, to whom all beings turn their constant thought,--him girt by Maruts we invoke to be our Friend.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Refulgent in the Rudras' region he proceeds, and with the Rudras through the wide space speeds the Dame. The hymn of praise extols Indra the far-renowned: him girt by Maruts we invoke to be our Friend.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O girt by Maruts, whether thou delight thee in loftiest gathering-place or lowly dwelling, Come thence unto our rite, true boon-best-ower: through love of thee have we prepared oblations.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: We, fain for thee, strong Indra, have pressed Soma, and, O thou sought with prayer, have made oblations. Now at this sacrifice, with all thy Maruts, on sacred grass, O team-borne God, rejoice thee.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Rejoice thee with thine own Bay Steeds, O Indra, unclose thy jaws and let thy lips be open. Thou with the fair cheek, let thy Bay Steeds bring thee: gracious to us, he pleased with our oblation.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Guards of the camp whose praisers are the Maruts, may we through Indra, get ourselves the booty. This prayer of ours may Varuna grant, and Mitra, and Aditi and Sindhu, Earth and Heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To thee the Mighty One I bring this mighty hymn, for thy desire hath been gratified by my laud. In Indra, yea in him victorious through his strength, the Gods have joyed at feast and when the Soma flowed.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Seven Rivers bear his glory far and wide, and heaven and sky and earth display his comely form. The Sun and Moon in change alternate run their course, that we, O Indra, may behold and may have faith.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Maghavan, grant us that same car to bring us spoil, thy conquering car in which we joy in shock of fight. Thou, Indra, whom our hearts praise highly in the war, grant shelter, Maghavan, to us who love thee well.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Encourage thou our side in every fight: may we, with thee for our ally, conquer the foeman's host. Indra, bestow on us joy and felicity break down, O Maghavan, the vigour of our foes.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: For here in divers ways these men invoking thee, holder of treasures, sing hymns to win thine aid. Ascend the car that thou mayest bring spoil to us, for, Indra, thy fixt winneth the victory.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: His arms win kine, his power is boundless in each act best, with a hundred helps waker of battle's din Is Indra: none may rival him in mighty strength. Hence, eager for the spoil the people call on him.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thy glory, Maghavan, exceeds a hundred yea, more than a hundred, than a thousand mid the folk, The great bowl hath inspirited thee boundlessly: so mayst thou slay the Vrtras breaker-down of forts!
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Of thy great might there is a three counterpart, the three earths, Lord men and the three realms of light. Above this whole world, Indra, thou hast waxen great: without a foe art thou, nature, from of old.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: We invocate thee first among the Deities: thou hast become a mighty Conquer in fight. May Indra fill with spirit this our singer's heart, and make our car impetuous, foremost in attack.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou hast prevailed, and hast not kept the booty back, in trifling battles in those of great account. We make thee keen, the Mighty One, succour us: inspire us, Maghavan, when we defy the foe.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May Indra evermore be our Protector, and unimperilled may we win the booty. This prayer of ours may Varuna grant and Mitra, and Aditi and Sindhu, Earth and Heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: THAT highest Indra-power of thine is distant: that which is here sages possessed aforetime. This one is on the earth, in heaven the other, and both unite as flag with flag in battle.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He spread the wide earth out and firmly fixed it, smote with his thunderbolt and loosed the waters. Maghavan with his puissance struck down Ahi, rent Rauhina to death and slaughtered Vyamsa.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Armed with his bolt and trusting in his prowess he wandered shattering the forts of Dasas. Cast thy dart, knowing, Thunderer, at the Dasyu; increase the Arya's might and glory, Indra.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: For him who thus hath taught these human races, Maghavan, bearing a fame-worthy title, Thunderer, drawing nigh to slay the Dasyus, hath given himself the name of Son for glory.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: See this abundant wealth that he possesses, and put your trust in Indra's hero vigour. He found the cattle, and he found the horses, he found the plants, the forests and the waters.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To him the truly strong, whose deeds are many, to him the strong Bull let us pour the Soma. The Hero, watching like a thief in ambush, goes parting the possessions of the godless.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Well didst thou do that hero deed, O Indra, in waking with thy bolt the slumbering Ahi. in thee, delighted, Dames divine rejoiced them, the flying Maruts and all Gods were joyful.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: As thou hast smitten Susna, Pipru, Vrtra and Kuyava, and Sambara's forts O Indra. This prayer of ours may Varuna grant, and Mitra, and Aditi and Sindhu, Earth and Heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: THE altar hath been made for thee to rest on: come like a panting courser and be seated. Loosen thy flying Steeds, set free thy Horses who bear thee swiftly nigh at eve and morning.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: These men have come to Indra for assistance: shall he not quickly come upon these pathways? May the Gods quell the fury of the Dasa, and may they lead our folk to happy fortune.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He who hath only wish as his possession casts on himself, casts foam amid the waters. Both wives of Kuyava in milk have bathed them: may they be drowned within the depth of Sipha.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: This hath his kinship checked who lives beside us: with ancient streams forth speeds and rules the Hero, Añjasi, Kulisi, and Virapatni, delighting him, bear milk upon their waters.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Soon as this Dasyu's traces were discovered, as she who knows her home, he sought the dwelling. Now think thou of us, Maghavan, nor cast us away as doth a profligate his treasure.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Indra, as such, give us a share of sunlight, of waters, sinlessness, and reputation. Do thou no harm to our yet unborn offspring: our trust is in thy mighty Indra-power.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Now we, I think, in thee as such have trusted: lead us on, Mighty One, to ample riches. In no unready house give us, O Indra invoked of many, food and drink when hungry.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Slay us not, Indra; do not thou forsake us: steal not away the joys which we delight in. Rend not our unborn brood, strong Lord of Bounty! our vessels with the life that is within them.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Come to us; they have called thee Soma-lover: here is the pressed juice. Drink thereof for rapture. Widely-capacious, pour it down within thee, and, invocated, hear us like a Father.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: WITHIN the waters runs the Moon, he with the beauteous wings in heaven. Ye lightnings with your golden wheels, men find not your abiding-place. Mark this my woe, ye Earth and Heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Surely men crave and gain their wish. Close to her husband clings the wife. And, in embraces intertwined, both give and take the bliss of love. Mark this my woe, ye Earth and Heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O never may that light, ye Gods, fall from its station in the sky. Ne'er fail us one like Soma sweet, the spring of our felicity. Mark this my woe ye Earth and Heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I ask the last of sacrifice. As envoy he shall tell it forth. Where is the ancient law divine? Who is its new diffuser now? Mark this my woe, ye Earth and Heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Ye Gods who yonder have your home in the three lucid realms of heaven, What count ye truth and what untruth? Where is mine ancient call on you? Mark this my woe, ye Earth and Heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: What is your firm support of Law? What Varuna's observant eye? How may we pass the wicked on the path of mighty Aryaman? Mark this my woe, ye Earth and Heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I am the man who sang of old full many a laud when Soma flowed. Yet torturing cares consume me as the wolf assails the thirsty deer. Mark this my woe, ye Earth and Heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Like rival wives on every side enclosing ribs oppress me sore. O Satakratu, biting cares devour me, singer of thy praise, as rats devour the weaver's threads. Mark this my woe, ye Earth and Heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Where those seven rays are shining, thence my home and family extend. This Trta Aptya knoweth well, and speaketh out for brotherhood. Mark this my woe, ye Earth and Heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May those five Bulls which stand on high full in the midst of mighty heaven, Having together swiftly borne my praises to the Gods, return. Mark this my woe, ye Earth and Heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: High in the mid ascent of heaven those Birds of beauteous pinion sit. Back from his path they drive the wolf as he would cross the restless floods. Mark this my woe, ye Earth and Heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Firm is this new-wrought hymn of praise, and meet to be told forth, O Gods. The flowing of the floods is Law, Truth is the Sun's extended light. Mark this my woe, ye Earth and Heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Worthy of laud, O Agni, is that kinship which thou hast with Gods. Here seat thee like a man: most wise, bring thou the Gods for sacrifice. Mark this my woe, ye Earth and Heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Here seated, man-like as a priest shall wisest Agni to the Gods Speed onward our oblations, God among the Gods, intelligent. Mark this my woe, ye Earth and Heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Varuna makes the holy prayer. To him who finds the path we pray. He in the heart reveals his thought. Let sacred worship rise anew. Mark this my woe, ye Earth and Heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: That pathway of the Sun in heaven, made to be highly glorified, Is not to be transgressed, O Gods. O mortals, ye behold it not. Mark this my woe, ye Earth and Heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Trita, when buried in the well, calls on the Gods to succour him. That call of his Brhaspati heard and released him from distress. Mark this my woe, ye Earth and Heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: A ruddy wolf beheld me once, as I was faring on my path. He, like a carpenter whose back is aching crouched and slunk away. Mark this my woe, ye Earth and Heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Through this our song may we, allied with Indra, with all our heroes conquer in the battle. This prayer of ours may Varuna grant, and Mitra, and Aditi and Sindhu, Earth and Heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: CALL we for aid on Indra, Mitra, Varuna and Agni and the Marut host and Aditi. Even as a chariot from a difficult ravine, bountiful Vasus, rescue us from all distress.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Come ye Adityas for our full prosperity, in conquests of the foe, ye Gods, bring joy to us. Even as a chariot from a difficult ravine, bountiful Vasus, rescue us from all distress.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May the most glorious Fathers aid us, and the two Goddesses, Mothers of the Gods, who strengthen Law. Even as a chariot from a difficult ravine, bountiful Vasus, rescue us from all distress.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To mighty Narasamsa, strengthening his might, to Pusan, ruler over men, we pray with hymns. Even as a chariot from a difficult ravine, bountiful Vasus, rescue us from all distress.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Brhaspati, make us evermore an easy path: we crave what boon thou hast for men in rest and stir. Like as a chariot from a difficult ravine, bountiful Vasus, rescue us from all distress.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Sunk in the pit the Rsi Kutsa called, to aid, Indra the Vrtra-slayer, Lord of power and might. Even as a chariot from a difficult ravine, bountiful Vasus, rescue us from all distress.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May Aditi the Goddess guard us with the Gods: may the protecting God keep us with ceaseless care. This prayer of ours may Varuna grant, and Mitra, and Aditi and Sindhu, Earth and Heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: THE sacrifice obtains the Gods' acceptance: be graciously inclined to us, Adityas. Hitherward let your favour be directed, and be our best deliverer from trouble.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: By praise-songs of Angirases exalted, may the Gods come to us with their protection. May Indra with his powers, Maruts with Maruts, Aditi with Adityas grant us shelter.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: This laud of ours may Varuna and Indra, Aryaman Agni, Savitar find pleasant. This prayer' of ours may Varuna grant, and Mitra, and Aditi and Sindhu, Earth and Heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: ON that most wondrous car of yours, O Indra and Agni, which looks round on all things living, Take ye your stand and come to us together, and drink libations of the flowing Soma.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: As vast as all this world is in its compass, deep as it is, with its far-stretching surface, So let this Soma be, Indra and Agni, made for your drinking till your soul be sated.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: For ye have won a blessed name together: yea, with one aim ye strove, O Vrtra-slayers. So Indra-Agni, seated here together, pour in, ye Mighty Ones, the mighty Soma.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Both stand adorned, when fires are duly kindled, spreading the sacred grass, with lifted ladles. Drawn by strong Soma juice poured forth around us, come, Indra-Agni, and display your favour.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The brave deeds ye have done, Indra and Agni, the forms ye have displayed and mighty exploits, The ancient and auspicious bonds of friendship,--for sake of these drink of the flowing Soma.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: As first I said when choosing you, in battle we must contend with Asuras for this Soma. So came ye unto this my true conviction, and drank libations of the flowing Soma.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: If in your dwelling, or with prince or Brahman, ye, Indra-Agni, Holy Ones, rejoice you, Even from thence, ye mighty Lords, come hither, and drink libation of the flowing Soma.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: If with, the Yadus, Turvasas, ye sojourn, with Druhyus, Anus, Purus, Indra-Agni! Even from thence, ye mighty Lords, come hither, and drink libations of the flowing Soma.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Whether, O Indra-Agni, ye be dwelling in lowest earth, in central, or in highest. Even from thence, ye mighty Lords, come hither, and drink libations of the flowing Soma.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Whether, O Indra-Agni, ye be dwelling in highest earth, in central, or in lowest, Even from thence, ye mighty Lords, come hither, and drink libations of the flowing Soma.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Whether ye be in heaven, O Indra-Agni, on earth, on mountains, in the herbs, or waters, Even from thence, ye mighty Lords, come hither, and drink libations of the flowing Soma.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: If, when the Sun to the mid-heaven hath mounted, ye take delight in food, O Indra-Agni, Even from thence, ye mighty Lords, come hither, and drink libations of the flowing Soma.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thus having drunk your fill of our libation, win us all kinds of wealth, Indra and Agni. This prayer of ours may Varuna grant, and Mitra, and Aditi and Sindhu, Earth and Heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: LONGING for weal I looked around, in spirit, for kinsmen, Indra-Agni, or for brothers. No providence but yours alone is with me so have I wrought for you this hymn for succour.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: For I have heard that ye give wealth more freely than worthless son-in-law or spouse's brother. So offering to you this draught of Soma, I make you this new hymn, Indra and Agni,
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Let us not break the cords: with this petition we strive to gain the powers of our forefathers. For Indra-Agni the strong drops are joyful, for here in the bowl's lap are both the press-stones.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: For you the bowl divine, Indra and Agni, presses the Soma gladly to delight you. With hands auspicious and fair arms, ye Asvins, haste, sprinkle it with sweetness in the waters.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: You, I have heard, were mightiest, Indra-Agni, when Vrtra fell and when the spoil was parted. Sit at this sacrifice, ye ever active, on the strewn grass, and with the juice delight you.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Surpassing all men where they shout for battle, ye Twain exceed the earth and heaven in greatness. Greater are ye than rivers and than mountains, O Indra-Agni, and all things beside them.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Bring wealth and give it, ye whose arms wield thunder: Indra and Agni, with your powers protect us. Now of a truth these be the very sunbeams wherewith our fathers were of old united.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Give, ye who shatter forts, whose hands wield thunder: Indra and Agni, save us in our battles. This prayer of ours may Varuna grant, and Mitra, and Aditi and Sindhu, Earth and Heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: THE holy work I wrought before is wrought again: my sweetest hymn is sung to celebrate your praise. Here, O ye Rbhus, is this sea for all the Gods: sate you with Soma offered with the hallowing word.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When, seeking your enjoyment onward from afar, ye, certain of my kinsmen, wandered on your way, Sons of Sudhanvan, after your long journeying, ye came unto the home of liberal Savitar.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Savitar therefore gave you immortality, because ye came proclaiming him whom naught can hide; And this the drinking-chalice of the Asura, which till that time was one, ye made to be fourfold.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When they had served with zeal at sacrifice as priests, they, mortal as they were, gained immortality. The Rbhus, children of Sudhanvan, bright as suns, were in a year's course made associate with prayers.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Rbhus, with a rod measured, as 'twere a field, the single sacrificial chalice. wide of mouth, Lauded of all who saw, praying for what is best, desiring glorious fame among Immortal Gods.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: As oil in ladles, we through knowledge will present unto the Heroes of the firmament our hymn,-- The Rbhus who came near with this great Father's speed, and rose to heaven's high sphere to eat the strengthening food.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Rbhu to us is Indra freshest in his might, Rbhu with powers and wealth is giver of rich gifts. Gods, through your favour may we on the happy day quell the attacks of those who pour no offerings forth.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Out of a skin, O Rbhus, once ye formed a cow, and brought the mother close unto her calf again. Sons of Sudhanvan, Heroes, with surpassing skill ye made your aged Parents youthful as before.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Help us with strength where spoil is won, O Indra: joined with the Rbhus give us varied bounty. This prayer of ours may Varuna grant, and Mitra, and Aditi and Sindhu, Earth and Heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: WORKING with skill they wrought the lightly rolling car: they wrought the Bays who bear Indra and bring great gifts. The Rbhus for their Parents made life young again; and fashioned for the calf a mother by its side.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: For sacrifice make for us active vital power for skill and wisdom food with noble progeny. Grant to our company this power most excellent, that with a family all-heroic we may dwell.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Do ye, O Rbhus, make prosperity for us, prosperity for car, ye Heroes, and for steed. Grant us prosperity victorious evermore, conquering foes in battle, strangers or akin.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Indra, the Rbhus' Lord, I invocate for aid, the Rbhus, Vajas, Maruts to the Soma draught. Varuna, Mitra, both, yea, and the Asvins Twain: let them speed us to wealth, wisdom, and victory.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May Rbhu send prosperity for battle, may Vaja conquering in the fight protect us. This prayer of ours may Varuna grant, and Mitra, and Aditi and Sindhu, Earth and Heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To give first thought to them, I worship Heaven and Earth, and Agni, fair bright glow, to hasten their approach. Come hither unto us, O Asvins, with those aids wherewith in fight ye speed the war-cry to the spoil.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Ample, unfailing, they have mounted as it were an eloquent car that ye may think of us and give. Come hither unto us, O Asvins, with those aids wherewith ye help our thoughts to further holy acts.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Ye by the might which heavenly nectar giveth you are in supreme dominion Lords of all these folk. Come hither unto us, O Asvins, with those aids wherewith ye, Heroes, made the barren cow give milk.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The aids wherewith the Wanderer through his offspring's might, or the Two-Mothered Son shows swiftest mid the swift; Wherewith the sapient one acquired his triple lore,--Come hither unto us, O Asvins, with those aids.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Wherewith ye raised from waters, prisoned and fast bound, Rebha, and Vandana to look upon the light; Wherewith ye succoured Kanva as he strove to win,--Come hither unto us, O Asvins, with those aids.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Wherewith ye rescued Antaka when languishing deep in the pit, and Bhujyu with unfailing help. And comforted Karkandhu, Vayya, in their woe,--Come hither unto us, O Asvins, with those aids.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Wherewith ye gave Sucanti wealth and happy home, and made the fiery pit friendly for Atri's sake; Wherewith ye guarded Purukutsa, Prsnigu,--Come hither unto us, O Asvin;, with those aids.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Mighty Ones, with what powers ye gave Paravrj aid what time ye made the blind and lame to see and walk; Wherewith ye set at liberty the swallowed quail,--Come hither unto us, O Asvins, with those aids.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Wherewith ye quickened the most sweet exhaustless flood, and comforted Vasistha, ye who ne'er decay; And to Srutarya, Kutsa, Narya gave your help,--Come hither unto us, O Asvins, with those aids.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Wherewith ye helped, in battle of a thousand spoils, Vispala seeking booty, powerless to move. Wherewith ye guarded friendly Vasa, Asva's son,--Come hither unto us, O Asvins, with those aids.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Whereby the cloud, ye Bounteous Givers, shed sweet rain for Dirghasravas, for the merchant Ausija, Wherewith ye helped Kaksivan, singer of your praise,--Come hither unto us, O Asvins, with those aids.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Wherewith ye made Rasa swell full with water-floods, and urged to victory the car without a horse; Wherewith Trisoka drove forth his recovered cows,--Come hither unto us, O Asvins, with those aids.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Wherewith ye, compass round the Sun when far away, strengthened Mandhatar in his tasks as lord of lands, And to sage Bharadvaja gave protecting help,--Come hither unto us, O Asvins, with those aids.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Wherewith, when Sambara was slain, ye guarded well great Atithigva, Divodisa, Kasoju, And Trasadasyu when the forts were shattered down,--Come hither unto us, O Asvins, with those aids.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Wherewith ye honoured the great drinker Vamra, and Upastuta and Kali when he gained his wife, And lent to Vyasva and to Prthi favouring help,--Come hither unto us, O Asvins, with those aids.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Wherewith, O Heroes, ye vouchsafed deliverance to Sayu, Atri, and to Manu long ago; Wherewith ye shot your shafts in Syumarasmi's cause.--Come hither unto us, O Asvins, with those aids.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Wherewith Patharva, in his majesty of form, shone in his course like to a gathered kindled fire; Wherewith ye helped Saryata in the mighty fray,--Come hither unto us, O Asvins, with those aids.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Wherewith, Angirases! ye triumphed in your heart, and onward went to liberate the flood of milk; Wherewith ye helped the hero Manu with new strength,--Come hither unto us, O Asvins, with those aids.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Wherewith ye brought a wife for Vimada to wed, wherewith ye freely gave the ruddy cows away; Wherewith ye brought the host of kind Gods to Sudas--Come hither unto us, O Asvins, with those aids.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Wherewith ye bring great bliss to him who offers gifts, wherewith ye have protected Bhujyu, Adhrigu, And good and gracious Subhara and Rtastup,--Come hither unto us, O Asvins, with those aids.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Wherewith ye served Krsanu where the shafts were shot, and helped the young man's horse to swiftness in the race; Wherewith ye bring delicious honey to the bees,--Come hither unto us, O Asvins, with those aids.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Wherewith ye speed the hero as he fights for kine in hero battle, in the strife for land and sons, Wherewith ye safely guard his horses and his car,--Come hither unto us, O Asvins with those aids.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Wherewith ye, Lords of Hundred Powers, helped Kutsa, son of Arjuni, gave Turviti and Dabhiti strength, Favoured Dhvasanti and lent Purusanti help,--Come hither unto us, O Asvins, with those aids.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Make ye our speech effectual, O ye Asvins, and this our hymn, ye mighty Wonder-Workers. In luckless game I call on you for succour: strengthen us also on the field of battle.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With, undiminished blessings, O ye Asvins, for evermore both night and day protect us. This prayer of ours may Varuna grant, and Mitra, and Aditi and Sindhu, Earth and Heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: This light is come, amid all lights the fairest; born is the brilliant, far-extending brightness. Night, sent away for Savitar's uprising, hath yielded up a birth-place for the Morning.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Fair, the Bright is come with her white offspring; to her the Dark One hath resigned her dwelling. Akin, immortal, following each other, changing their colours both the heavens move onward.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Common, unending is the Sisters' pathway; taught by the Gods, alternately they travel. Fair-formed, of different hues and yet one-minded, Night and Dawn clash not, neither do they travel.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Bright leader of glad sounds, our eyes behold her; splendid in hue she hath unclosed the portals. She, stirring up the world, hath shown us riches: Dawn hath awakened every living creature.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Rich Dawn, she sets afoot the coiled-up sleeper, one for enjoyment, one for wealth or worship, Those who saw little for extended vision. All living creatures hath the Dawn awakened.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: One to high sway, one to exalted glory, one to pursue his gain, and one his labour: All to regard their different vocations, all moving creatures hath the Dawn awakened.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: We see her there, the Child of Heaven apparent, the young Maid, flushing in her shining raiment. Thou sovran Lady of all earthly treasure, flush on us here, auspicious Dawn, this morning.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: She first of endless morns to come hereafter, follows the path of morns that have departed. Dawn, at her rising, urges forth the living him who is dead she wakes not from his slumber.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: As thou, Dawn, hast caused Agni to be kindled, and with the Sun's eye hast revealed creation. And hast awakened men to offer worship, thou hast performed, for Gods, a noble service.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: How long a time, and they shall be together,--Dawns that have shone and Dawns to shine hereafter? She yearns for former Dawns with eager longing, and goes forth gladly shining with the others.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Gone are the men who in the days before us looked on the rising of the earlier Morning. We, we the living, now behold her brightness and they come nigh who shall hereafter see her.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Foe-chaser, born of Law, the Law's protectress, joy-giver, waker of all pleasant voices, Auspicious, bringing food for Gods' enjoyment, shine on us here, most bright, O Dawn, this morning.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: From days eternal hath Dawn shone, the Goddess, and shows this light to-day, endowed with riches. So will she shine on days to come immortal she moves on in her own strength, undecaying.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: In the sky's borders hath she shone in splendour: the Goddess hath thrown off the veil of darkness. Awakening the world with purple horses, on her well-harnessed chariot Dawn approaches.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Bringing all life-sustaining blessings with her, showing herself she sends forth brilliant lustre. Last of the countless mornings that have vanished, first of bright morns to come hath Dawn arisen.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Arise! the breath, the life, again hath reached us: darkness hath passed away and light approacheth. She for the Sun hath left a path to travel we have arrived where men prolong existence.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Singing the praises of refulgent Mornings with his hymn's web the priest, the poet rises. Shine then to-day, rich Maid, on him who lauds thee, shine down on us the gift of life and offspring.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Dawns giving sons all heroes, kine and horses, shining upon the man who brings oblations,-- These let the Soma-presser gain when ending his glad songs louder than the voice of Vayu.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Mother of Gods, Aditi's form of glory, ensign of sacrifice, shine forth exalted. Rise up, bestowing praise on our devotion all-bounteous, make us chief among the people.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Whatever splendid wealth the Dawns bring with them to bless the man who offers praise and worship, Even that may Mitra, Varuna vouchsafe us, and Aditi and Sindhu, Earth and Heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To the strong Rudra bring we these our songs of praise, to him the Lord of Heroes with the braided hair, That it be well with all our cattle and our men, that in this village all be healthy and well-fed.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Be gracious unto us, O Rudra, bring us joy: thee, Lord of Heroes, thee with reverence will we serve. Whatever health and strength our father Manu won by sacrifice may we, under thy guidance, gain.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: By worship of the Gods may we, O Bounteous One, O Rudra, gain thy grace, Ruler of valiant men. Come to our families, bringing them bliss: may we, whose heroes are uninjured, bring thee sacred gifts,
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Hither we call for aid the wise, the wanderer, impetuous Rudra, perfecter of sacrifice. May he repel from us the anger of the Gods: verily we desire his favourable grace.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Him with the braided hair we call with reverence down, the wild-boar of the sky, the red, the dazzling shape. May he, his hand filled full of sovran medicines, grant us protection, shelter, and a home secure.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To him the Maruts' Father is this hymn addressed, to strengthen Rudra's might, a song more sweet than sweet. Grant us, Immortal One, the food which mortals eat: be gracious unto me, my seed, my progeny.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary
