verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: STRONG Pusan's majesty is lauded evermore, the glory of his lordly might is never faint, his song of praise is never faint. Seeking felicity I laud him nigh to help, the source, of bliss, Who, Vigorous one, hath drawn to him the hearts of all, drawn them, the Vigorous One, the God.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thee, then, O Pusan, like a swift one on his way, I urge with lauds that thou mayst make the foemen flee, drive, camel-like, our foes afar. As I, a man, call thee, a God, giver of bliss, to be my Friend, So make our loudly-chanted praises glorious, in battles make them glorious.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou, Pusan, in whose friendship they who sing forth praise enjoy advantage, even in wisdom, through thy grace, in wisdom even they are advanced. So, after this most recent course, we come to thee with prayers for wealth. Not stirred to anger, O Wide-Ruler, come to us, come thou to us in every fight.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Not stirred to anger, come, Free-giver, nigh to us, to take this gift of ours, thou who hast goats for steeds, Goat-borne! their gift who long for fame. So, Wonder-Worker! may we turn thee hither with effectual lauds. I slight thee not, O Pusan, thou Resplendent One: thy friendship may not be despised.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: HEARD be our prayer! In thought I honour Agni first: now straightway we elect this heavenly company, Indra and Vayu we elect. For when our latest thought is raised and on Vivasvan centred well, Then may our holy songs go forward on their way, our songs as 'twere unto the Gods.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: As there ye, Mitra, Varuna, above the true have taken to yourselves the untrue with your mind, with wisdom's mental energy, So in the seats wherein ye dwell have we beheld the Golden One, Not with our thoughts or spirit, but with these our eyes, yea, with the eyes that Soma gives.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Asvins, the pious call you with their hymns of praise, sounding their loud song forth to you, these living men, to their oblations, living men. All glories and all nourishment, Lords of all wealth! depend on you. The fellies of your golden chariot scatter drops, Mighty Ones! of your golden car.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Well is it known, O Mighty Ones: ye open heaven; for you the chariot-steeds are yoked for morning rites, unswerving steeds for morning rites, We set you on the chariot-seat, ye Mighty, on the golden car. Ye seek mid-air as by a path that leads aright, as by a path that leads direct.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Rich in Strength, through your great power vouchsafe us blessings day and night. The offerings which we bring to you shall never fail, gifts brought by us shall never fail.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: These Soma-drops, strong Indra! drink for heroes, poured, pressed out by pressing-stones, are welling forth for thee, for thee the drops are welling forth. They shall make glad thy heart to give, to give wealth great and wonderful. Thou who acceptest praise come glorified by hymns, come thou to us benevolent.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Quickly, O Agni, hear us: magnified by us thou shalt speck for us to the Gods adorable yea, to the Kings adorable: When, O ye Deities, ye gave that Milch-cow to the Angirases, They milked her: Aryaman, joined with them, did the work: he knoweth her as well as I.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Ne'er may these manly deeds of yours for us grow old, never may your bright glories fall into decay, never before our time decay. What deed of yours, new every age, wondrous, surpassing man, rings forth, Whatever, Maruts! may be difficult to gain, grant us, whate'er is hard to gain.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Dadhyac of old, Angiras, Priyamedha these, and Kanva, Atri, Manu knew my birth, yea, those of ancient days and Manu knew. Their long line stretcheth to the Gods, our birth-connexions are with them. To these, for their high station, I bow down with song, to Indra, Agni, bow with song.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Let the Invoker bless: let offerers bring choice gifts; Brhaspati the Friend doth sacrifice with Steers, Steers that have many an excellence. Now with our ears we catch the sound of the press-stone that rings afar. The very Strong hath gained the waters by himself, the strong gained many a resting-place.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O ye Eleven Gods whose home is heaven, O ye Eleven who make earth your dwelling, Ye who with might, Eleven, live in waters, accept this sacrifice, O Gods, with pleasure.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To splendid Agni seated by the altar, loving well his home, I bring the food as 'twere his place of birth. I clothe the bright One with my hymn as with a robe, him with the car of light, bright-hued, dispelling gloom.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Child of a double birth he grasps at triple food; in the year's course what he hath swallowed grows anew. He, by another's mouth and tongue a noble Bull, with other, as an elephant, consumes the trees.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The pair who dwell together, moving in the dark bestir themselves: both parents hasten to the babe, Impetuous-tongued, destroying, springing swiftly forth, one to be watched and cherished, strengthener of his sire.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: For man, thou Friend of men, these steeds of thine are yoked, impatient, lightly running, ploughing blackened lines, Discordant-minded, fleet, gliding with easy speed, urged onward by the wind and rapid in their course.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Dispelling on their way the horror of black gloom, making a glorious show these flames of his fly forth, When o'er the spacious tract he spreads himself abroad, and rushes panting on with thunder and with roar.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Amid brown plants he stoops as if adorning them, and rushes bellowing like a bull upon his wives. Proving his might, he decks the glory of his form, and shakes his horns like one terrific, hard to stay.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Now covered, now displayed he grasps as one who knows his resting-place in those who know him well. A second time they wax and gather Godlike power, and blending both together change their Parents' form.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The maidens with long, tresses hold him in embrace; dead, they rise up again to meet the Living One. Releasing them from age with a loud roar he comes, filling them with new spirit, living, unsubdued.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Licking the mantle of the Mother, far and wide he wanders over fields with beasts that flee apace. Strengthening all that walk, licking up all around, a blackened path, forsooth, he leaves where'er he goes.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Agni, shine resplendent with our wealthy chiefs, like a loud-snorting bull, accustomed to the house. Thou casting off thine infant wrappings blazest forth as though thou hadst put on a coat of mail for war.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May this our perfect prayer be dearer unto thee than an imperfect prayer although it please thee well. With the pure brilliancy that radiates from thy form, mayest thou grant to us abundant store of wealth.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Grant to our chariot, to our house, O Agni, a boat with moving feet and constant oarage, One that may further well our wealthy princes and all the folk, and be our certain refuge.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Welcome our laud with thine approval, Agni. May earth and heaven and freely flowing rivers Yield us long life and food and corn and cattle, and may the red Dawns choose for us their choicest.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: YEA, verily, the fair effulgence of the God for glory was established, since he sprang from strength. When he inclines thereto successful is the hymn: the songs of sacrifice have brought him as they flow
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Wonderful, rich in nourishment, he dwells in food; next, in the seven auspicious Mothers is his home. Thirdly, that they might drain the treasures of the Bull, the maidens brought forth him for whom the ten provide.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: What time from out the deep, from the Steer's wondrous form, the Chiefs who had the power produced him with their strength; When Matarisvan rubbed forth him who lay concealed, for mixture of the sweet drink, in the days of old.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When from the Highest Father he is brought to us, amid the plants he rises hungry, wondrously. As both together join to expedite his birth, most youthful he is born resplendent in his light.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Then also entered he the Mothers, and in them pure and uninjured he increased in magnitude. As to the first he rose, the vigorous from of old, so now he runs among the younger lowest ones.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Therefore they choose him Herald at the morning rites, pressing to him as unto Bhaga, pouring gifts, When, much-praised, by the power and will of Gods, he goes at all times to his mortal worshipper to drink.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: What time the Holy One, wind-urged, hath risen up, serpent-like winding through the dry grass unrestrained, Dust lies upon the way of him who burneth all, black-winged and pure of birth who follows sundry paths.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Like a swift chariot made by men who know their art, he with his red limbs lifts himself aloft to heaven. Thy worshippers become by burning black of hue: their strength flies as before a hero's violence.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: By thee, O Agni, Varuna who guards the Law, Mitra and Aryaman, the Bounteous, are made strong; For, as the felly holds the spokes, thou with thy might pervading hast been born encompassing them round.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Agni, to him who toils and pours libations, thou, Most Youthful! sendest wealth and all the host of Gods. Thee, therefore, even as Bhaga, will we set anew, young Child of Strength, most wealthy! in our battle-song.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Vouchsafe us riches turned to worthy ends, good luck abiding in the house, and strong capacity, Wealth that directs both worlds as they were guiding-reins, and, very Wise, the Gods' assent in sacrifice.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May he, the Priest resplendent, joyful, hear us, he with the radiant car and rapid horses. May Agni, ever wise, with best directions to bliss and highest happiness conduct us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With hymns of might hath Agni now been lauded, advanced to height of universal kingship. Now may these wealthy chiefs and we together spread forth as spreads the Sun above the rain-clouds.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: KINDLED, bring, Agni, Gods to-day for him who lifts the ladle up. Spin out the ancient thread for him who sheds, with gifts, the Soma juice.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou dealest forth, Tanunapat, sweet sacrifice enriched with oil, Brought by a singer such as I who offers gifts and toils for thee.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He wondrous, sanctifying, bright, sprinkles the sacrifice with mead, Thrice, Narasamsa from the heavens, a God mid Gods adorable.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Agni, besought, bring hitherward Indra the Friend, the Wonderful, For this my hymn of praise, O sweet of tongue, is chanted forth to thee.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The ladle-holders strew trimmed grass at this well-ordered sacrifice; A home for Indra is adorned, wide, fittest to receive the Gods.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thrown open be the Doors Divine, unfailing, that assist the rite, High, purifying, much-desired, so that the Gods may enter in.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May Night and Morning, hymned with lauds, united, fair to look upon, Strong Mothers of the sacrifice, seat them together on the grass.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May the two Priests Divine, the sage, the sweet-voiced lovers of the hymn, Complete this sacrifice of ours, effectual, reaching heaven to-day.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Let Hotra pure, set among Gods, amid the Maruts Bharati, Ila, Sarasvati, Mahi, rest on the grass, adorable.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May Tvastar send us genial dew abundant, wondrous, rich in gifts, For increase and for growth of wealth, Tvastar our kinsman and our Friend.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Vanaspati, give forth, thyself, and call the Gods to sacrifice. May Agni, God intelligent, speed our oblation to the Gods.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To Vayu joined with Pusan, with the Maruts, and the host of Gods, To Indra who inspires the hymn cry Glory! and present the gift.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Come hither to enjoy the gifts prepared with cry of Glory! Come, O Indra, hear their calling; they invite thee to the sacrifice.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To Agni I present a newer mightier hymn, I bring my words and song unto the Son of Strength, Who, Offspring of the Waters, bearing precious things sits on the earth, in season, dear Invoking Priest.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Soon as he sprang to birth that Agni was shown forth to Matarisvan in the highest firmament. When he was kindled, through his power and majesty his fiery splendour made the heavens and earth to shine.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: His flames that wax not old, beams fair to look upon of him whose face is lovely, shine with beauteous sheen. The rays of Agni, him whose active force is light, through the nights glimmer sleepless, ageless, like the floods.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Send thou with hymns that Agni to his own abode, who rules, one Sovran Lord of wealth, like Varuna, Him, All-possessor, whom the Bhrgus with their might brought to earth's central point, the centre of the world.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He whom no force can stay, even as the Maruts' roar, like to a dart sent forth, even as the bolt from heaven, Agni with sharpened jaws chews up and eats the trees, and conquers them as when the warrior smites his foes.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: And will not Agni find enjoyment in our praise, will not the Vasu grant our wish with gifts of wealth? Will not the Inspirer speed our prayers to gain their end? Him with the radiant glance I laud with this my song.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The kindler of the flame wins Agni as a Friend, promoter of the Law, whose face is bright with oil. Inflamed and keen, refulgent in our gatherings, he lifts our hymn on high clad in his radiant hues.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Keep us incessantly with guards that cease not, Agni, with guards auspicious, very mighty. With guards that never slumber, never heedless, never beguiled. O Helper, keep our children.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: THE Priest goes forth to sacrifice, with wondrous power sending aloft the hymn of glorious brilliancy. He moves to meet the ladles turning to the right, which are the first to kiss the place where he abides.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To him sang forth the flowing streams of Holy Law, encompassed in the home and birth-place of the God. He, when he dwelt extended in the waters' lap, absorbed those Godlike powers for which he is adored.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Seeking in course altern to reach the selfsame end the two copartners strive to win this beauteous form. Like Bhaga must he be duly invoked by us, as he who drives the car holds fast the horse's reins.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He whom the two copartners with observance tend, the pair who dwell together in the same abode, By night as in the day the grey one was born young, passing untouched by eld through many an age of man.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Him the ten fingers, the devotions, animate: we mortals call on him a God to give us help. He speeds over the sloping surface of the land: new deeds hath he performed with those who gird him round.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: For, Agni, like a herdsman, thou by thine own might rulest o'er all that is in heaven and on the earth; And these two Mighty Ones, bright, golden closely joined, rolling them round are come unto thy sacred grass.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Agni, accept with joy, be glad in this our prayer, joy-giver, self-sustained, strong, born of Holy Law! For fair to see art thou turning to every side, pleasant to look on as a dwelling filled with food.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Ask ye of him for he is come, he knoweth it; he, full of wisdom, is implored, is now implored. With him are admonitions and with him commands: he is the Lord of Strength, the Lord of Power and Might.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: They ask of him: not all learn by their questioning what he, the Sage, hath grasped, as 'twere, with his own mind. Forgetting not the former nor the later word, he goeth on, not careless, in his mental power.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To him these ladles go, to him these racing mares: he only will give ear to all the words I speak. All-speeding, victor, perfecter of sacrifice, the Babe with flawless help hath mustered vigorous might.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Whate'er he meets he grasps and then runs farther on, and straightway, newly born, creeps forward with his kin. He stirs the wearied man to pleasure and great joy what time the longing gifts approach him as he comes.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He is a wild thing of the flood and forest: he hath been laid upon the highest surface. He hath declared the lore of works to mortals, Agni the Wise, for he knows Law, the Truthful.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I LAUD the seven-rayed, the triple-headed, Agni all-perfect in his Parents' bosom, Sunk in the lap of all that moves and moves not, him who hath filled all luminous realms of heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: As a great Steer he grew to these his Parents; sublime he stands, untouched by eld, far-reaching. He plants his footsteps on the lofty ridges of the broad earth: his red flames lick the udder.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Coming together to their common youngling both Cows, fairshaped, spread forth in all directions, Measuring out the paths that must be travelled, entrusting all desires to him the Mighty.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The prudent sages lead him to his dwelling, guarding with varied skill the Ever-Youthful. Longing, they turned their eyes unto the River: to these the Sun of men was manifested.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Born noble in the regions, aim of all mens' eyes to be implored for life by great and small alike, Far as the Wealthy One hath spread himself abroad, he is the Sire all-visible of this progeny.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: How, Agni, have the radiant ones, aspiring, endued thee with the vigour of the living, So that on both sides fostering seed and offspring, the Gods may joy in Holy Law's fulfilment?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Mark this my speech, Divine One, thou, Most Youthful! offered to thee by him who gives most freely. One hates thee, and another sings thy praises: I thine adorer laud thy form, O Agni.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thy guardian rays, O Agni, when they saw him, preserved blind Mamateya from affliction. Lord of all riches, he preserved the pious the foes who fain would harm them did no mischief.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The sinful man who worships not, O Agni, who, offering not, harms us with double-dealing,-- Be this in turn to him a heavy sentence may he distress himself by his revilings.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Yea, when a mortal knowingly, O Victor, injures with double tongue a fellow-mortal, From him, praised Agni! save thou him that lauds thee: bring us not into trouble and affliction.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: WHAT Matarisvan, piercing, formed by friction, Herald of all the Gods. in varied figure, Is he whom they have set mid human houses, gay-hued as light and shining forth for beauty.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: They shall not harm the man who brings thee praises: such as I am, Agni my help approves me. All acts of mine shall they accept with pleasure, laudation from the singer who presents it.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Him in his constant seat men skilled in worship have taken and with praises have established. As, harnessed to a chariot fleet-foot horses, at his command let bearers lead him forward.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Wondrous, full many a thing he chews and crunches: he shines amid the wood with spreading brightness. Upon his glowing flames the wind blows daily, driving them like the keen shaft of an archer.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Him, whom while yet in embryo the hostile, both skilled and fain to harm, may never injure, Men blind and sightless through his splendour hurt not: his never-failing lovers have preserved him.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: HITHER he hastens to give, Lord of great riches, King of the mighty, to the place of treasure. The pressing-stones shall serve him speeding near us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: As Steer of men so Steer of earth and heaven by glory, he whose streams all life hath drunken, Who hasting forward rests upon the altar.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He who hath lighted up the joyous castle, wise Courser like the Steed of cloudy heaven, Bright like the Sun, with hundredfold existence.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He, doubly born, hath spread in his effulgence through the three luminous realms, through all the regions, Best sacrificing Priest where waters gather.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Priest doubly born, he through his love of glory hath in his keeping all things worth the choosing, The man who brings him gifts hath noble offspring.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: AGNI, thy faithful servant I call upon thee with many a gift, As in the keeping of the great inciting God;
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou who ne'er movest thee to aid the indolent, the godless man, Him who though wealthy never brings an offering.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Splendid, O Singer, is that man, mightiest of the great in heaven. Agni, may we be foremost, we thy worshippers.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: HEAVEN and earth trembled at the might and voice of him, whom, loved and Holy One, helper of all mankind, The wise who longed for spoil in fight for kine brought forth with power, a Friend, mid waters, at the sacrifice.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: As these, like friends, have done this work for you, these prompt servants of Purumilha Soma-offerer, Give mental power to him who sings the sacred song, and hearken, Strong Ones, to the master of the house.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The folk have glorified your birth from Earth and Heaven, to be extolled, ye Strong Ones, for your mighty power. Ye, when ye bring to singer and the rite, enjoy the sacrifice performed with holy praise and strength.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The people prospers, Asuras! whom ye dearly love: ye, Righteous Ones, proclaim aloud the Holy Law. That efficacious power that comes from lofty heaven, ye bind unto the work, as to the pole an ox.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: On this great earth ye send your treasure down with might: unstained by dust, the crowding kine are in the stalls. Here in the neighbourhood they cry unto the Sun at morning and at evening, like swift birds of prey.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The flames with curling tresses serve your sacrifice, whereto ye sing the song, Mitra and Varuna. Send down of your free will, prosper our holy songs: ye are sole Masters of the singer's hymn of praise.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Whoso with sacrifices toiling brings you gifts, and worships, sage and priest, fulfilling your desire,-- To him do ye draw nigh and taste his sacrifice. Come well-inclined to us unto our songs and prayer.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With sacrifices and with milk they deck you first, ye Righteous Ones, as if through stirrings of the mind. To you they bring their hymns with their collected thought, while ye with earnest soul come to us gloriously.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Rich strength of life is yours: ye, Heroes, have obtained through your surpassing powers rich far-extending might. Not the past days conjoined with nights, not rivers, not the Panis have attained your Godhead and your wealth.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: THE robes which ye put on abound with fatness: uninterrupted courses are your counsels. All falsehood, Mitra-Varuna! ye conquer, and closely cleave unto the Law Eternal.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: This might of theirs hath no one comprehended. True is the crushing word the sage hath uttered, The fearful four-edged bolt smites down the three-edged, and those who hate the Gods first fall and perish.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Footless Maid precedeth footed creatures. Who marketh, Mitra-Varuna, this your doing? The Babe Unborn supporteth this world's burthen, fulfilleth Law and overcometh falsehood.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: We look on him the darling of the Maidens, always advancing, never falling downward, Wearing inseparable, wide-spread raiment, Mitra's and Varuna's delightful glory.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Unbridled Courser, born but not of horses, neighing he flieth on with back uplifted. The youthful love mystery thought-surpassing, praising in Mitra-Varuna, its glory.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May the milch-kine who favour Mamateya prosper in this world him who loves devotion. May he, well skilled in rites, be food, and calling Aditi with his lips give us assistance.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Gods, Mitra-Varuna, with love and worship, let me make you delight in this oblation. May our prayer be victorious in battles, may we have rain from heaven to make us prosper.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: WE worship with our reverence and oblations you, Mitra Varuna, accordant, mighty, So that with us, ye Twain whose backs are sprinkled with oil, the priests with oil and hymns support you.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Your praise is like a mighty power, an impulse: to you, Twain Gods, a well-formed hymn is offered, As the priest decks yon, Strong Ones, in assemblies, and the prince fain to worship you for blessings.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Mitra-Varuna, Aditi the Milch-cow streams for the rite, for folk who bring oblation, When in the assembly he who worships moves you, like to a human priest, with gifts presented.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: So may the kine and heavenly Waters pour you sweet drink in families that make you joyful. Of this may he, the ancient House-Lord, give us. Enjoy, drink of the milk the cow provideth.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I WILL declare the mighty deeds of Visnu, of him who measured out the earthly regions, Who propped the highest place of congregation, thrice setting down his footstep, widely striding.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: For this his mighty deed is Visnu lauded, like some wild beast, dread, prowling, mountain-roaming; He within whose three wide-extended paces all living creatures have their habitation.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Let the hymn lift itself as strength to Visnu, the Bull far-striding, dwelling on the mountains, Him who alone with triple step hath measured this common dwelling-place, long, far extended.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Him whose three places that are filled with sweetness, imperishable, joy as it may list them, Who verily alone upholds the threefold, the earth, the heaven, and all living creatures.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May I attain to that his well-loved mansion where men devoted to the Gods are happy. For there springs, close akin to the Wide-Strider, the well of meath in Visnu's highest footstep.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Fain would we go unto your dwelling-places where there are many-horned and nimble oxen, For mightily, there, shineth down upon us the widely-striding Bull's sublimest mansion.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To the great Hero, him who sets his mind thereon, and Visnu, praise aloud in song your draught of juice,-- Gods ne'er beguiled, who borne as 'twere by noble steed, have stood upon the lofty ridges of the hills.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Your Soma-drinker keeps afar your furious rush, Indra and Visnu, when ye come with all your might. That which hath been directed well at mortal man, bow-armed Krsanu's arrow, ye turn far aside.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: These offerings increase his mighty manly strength: he brings both Parents down to share the genial flow. He lowers, though a son, the Father's highest name; the third is that which is high in the light of heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: We laud this manly power of him the Mighty One, preserver, inoffensive, bounteous and benign; His who strode, widely pacing, with three steppings forth over the realms of earth for freedom and for life.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: A mortal man, when he beholds two steps of him who looks upon the light, is restless with amaze. But his third step doth no one venture to approach, no, nor the feathered birds of air who fly with wings.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He, like a rounded wheel, hath in swift motion set his ninety racing steeds together with the four. Developed, vast in form, with those who sing forth praise, a youth, no more a child, he cometh to our call.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: FAR-SHINING, widely famed, going thy wonted way, fed with the oil, be helpful. Mitra-like, to us. So, Visnu, e'en the wise must swell thy song of praise, and he who hath oblations pay thee solemn rites.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He who brings gifts to him the Ancient and the Last, to Visnu who ordains, together with his Spouse, Who tells the lofty birth of him the Lofty One, shall verily surpass in glory e'en his peer.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Him have ye satisfied, singers, as well as ye know, primeval gem of Order even from his birth. Ye, knowing e'en his name, have told it forth: may we, Visnu, enjoy the grace of thee the Mighty One.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Sovran Varuna and both the Asvins wait on this the will of him who guides the Marut host. Visnu hath power supreme and might that finds the day, and with his Friend unbars the stable of the kine.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Even he the Heavenly One who came for fellowship, Visnu to Indra, godly to the godlier, Who Maker, throned in three worlds, helps the Aryan man, and gives the worshipper his share of Holy Law.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: AGNI is wakened: Surya riseth from the earth. Mighty, refulgent Dawn hath shone with all her light. The Asvins have equipped their chariot for the course. God Savitar hath moved the folk in sundry ways.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When, Asvins, ye equip your very mighty car, bedew, ye Twain, our power with honey and with oil. To our devotion give victorious strength in war: may we win riches in the heroes' strife for spoil.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Nigh to us come the Asvins' lauded three-wheeled car, the car laden with meath and drawn by fleet-foot steeds, Three-seated, opulent, bestowing all delight. may it bring weal to us, to cattle and to men.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Bring hither nourishment for us, ye Asvins Twain; sprinkle us with your whip that drops with honey-dew. Prolong our days of life, wipe out our trespasses; destroy our foes, be our companions and our Friends.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Ye store the germ of life in female creatures, ye lay it up within all living beings. Ye have sent forth, O Asvins passing mighty, the fire, the sovrans of the wood, the waters,
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Leeches are ye with medicines to heal us, and charioteers are ye with skill in driving. Ye Strong, give sway to him who brings oblation and with his heart pours out his gift before you.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: YE Vasus Twain, ye Rudras full of counsel, grant us, Strong Strengtheners, when ye stand beside us, What wealth Aucathya craves of you, great Helpers when ye come forward with no niggard succour.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Who may give you aught, Vasus, for your favour, for what, at the Cow's place, ye grant through worship? Wake for us understanding full of riches, come with a heart that will fulfil our longing.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: As erst for Tugra's son your car, sea-crossing, strong, was equipped and set amid the waters, So may I gain your shelter and protection as with winged course a hero seeks his army.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May this my praise preserve Ucathya's offspring: let not these Twain who fly with wings exhaust me. Let not the wood ten times up-piled consume me, when fixed for you it bites the ground it stands on.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The most maternal streams, wherein the Dasas cast me securely bound, have not devoured me. When Traitana would cleave my head asunder, the Dasa wounded his own breast and shoulders.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Dirghatamas the son of Mamata hath come to length of days in the tenth age of human kind. He is the Brahman of the waters as they strive to reach their end and aim: their charioteer is he.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I PRAISE with sacrifices mighty Heaven and Earth at festivals, the wise, the Strengtheners of Law. Who, having Gods for progeny, conjoined with Gods, through wonder-working wisdom bring forth choicest boons.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With invocations, on the gracious Father's mind, and on the Mother's great inherent power I muse. Prolific Parents, they have made the world of life, and for their brood all round wide immortality.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: These Sons of yours well skilled in work, of wondrous power, brought forth to life the two great Mothers first of all. To keep the truth of all that stands and all that moves, ye guard the station of your Son who knows no guile.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: They with surpassing skill, most wise, have measured out the Twins united in their birth and in their home. They, the refulgent Sages, weave within the sky, yea, in the depths of sea, a web for ever new.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: This is to-day the goodliest gift of Savitar: this thought we have when now the God is furthering us. On us with loving-kindness Heaven and Earth bestow riches and various wealth and treasure hundredfold!
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: THESE, Heaven and Earth, bestow prosperity on all, sustainers of the region, Holy Ones and wise, Two Bowls of noble kind: between these Goddesses the God, the fulgent Sun, travels by fixed decree.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Widely-capacious Pair, mighty, that never fail, the Father and the Mother keep all creatures safe: The two world-halves, the spirited, the beautiful, because the Father hath clothed them in goodly forms.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Son of these Parents, he the Priest with power to cleanse, Sage, sanctifies the worlds with his surpassing power. Thereto for his bright milk he milked through all the days the party-coloured Cow and the prolific Bull.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Among the skilful Gods most skilled is he, who made the two world-halves which bring prosperity to all; Who with great wisdom measured both the regions out, and stablished them with pillars that shall ne'er decay.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Extolled in song, O Heaven and Earth, bestow on us, ye mighty Pair, great glory and high lordly sway, Whereby we may extend ourselves ever over the folk; and send us strength that shall deserve the praise of men.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: WHY hath the Best, why hath the Youngest come to us? Upon what embassy comes he? What have we said? We have not blamed the chalice of illustrious birth. We, Brother Agni, praised the goodness of the wood.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The chalice that is single make ye into four: thus have the Gods commanded; therefore am I come. If, O Sudhanvan's Children, ye will do this thing ye shall participate in sacrifice with Gods.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: What to the envoy Agni in reply ye spake, A courser must be made, a chariot fashioned here, A cow must be created, and the Twain made young. When we have done these things, Brother, we turn to you.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When thus, O Rbhus, ye had done ye questioned thus, Whither went he who came to us a messenger? Then Tvastar, when he viewed the four wrought chalices, concealed himself among the Consorts of the Gods.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: As Tvastar thus had spoken, Let us slay these men who have reviled the chalice, drinking-cup of Gods, They gave themselves new names when Soma juice was shed, and under these new names the Maiden welcomed them.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Indra hath yoked his Bays, the Asvins' car is horsed, Brhaspati hath brought the Cow of every hue. Ye went as Rbhus, Vibhvan, Vaja to the Gods, and skilled in war, obtained your share in sacrifice.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Ye by your wisdom brought a cow from out a hide; unto that ancient Pair ye gave again their youth. Out of a horse, Sudhanvan's Sons, ye formed a horse: a chariot ye equipped, and went unto the Gods.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Drink ye this water, were the words ye spake to them; or drink ye this, the rinsing of the Muñja-grass. If ye approve not even this, Sudhanvan's Sons, then at the third libation gladden ye yourselves.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Most excellent are waters, thus said one of you; most excellent is Agni, thus another said. Another praised to many a one the lightning cloud. Then did ye shape the cups, speaking the words of truth.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: One downward to the water drives the crippled cow, another trims the flesh brought on the carving-board. One carries off the refuse at the set of sun. How did the Parents aid their children in their task!
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: On the high places ye have made the grass for man, and water in the valleys, by your skill, O Men. Rbhus, ye iterate not to-day that act of yours, your sleeping in the house of him whom naught can hide.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: As, compassing them round, ye glided through the worlds, where had the venerable Parents their abode? Ye laid a curse on him who raised his arm at you: to him who spake aloud to you ye spake again.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When ye had slept your fill, ye Rbhus, thus ye asked, O thou whom naught may hide, who now hath wakened us? The goat declared the hound to be your wakener. That day, in a full year, ye first unclosed our eyes.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Maruts move in heaven, on earth this Agni; through the mid-firmament the Wind approaches. Varuna comes in the sea's gathered waters, O Sons of Strength, desirous of your presence.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: SLIGHT us not Varuna, Aryaman, or Mitra, Rbhuksan, Indra, Ayu, or the Maruts, When we declare amid the congregation the virtues of the strong Steed, God-descended.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: What time they bear before the Courser, covered with trappings and with wealth, the grasped oblation, The dappled goat goeth straightforward, bleating, to the place dear to Indra and to Pusan.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Dear to all Gods, this goat, the share of Pusan, is first led forward with the vigorous Courser, While Tvastar sends him forward with the Charger, acceptable for sacrifice, to glory.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When thrice the men lead round the Steed, in order, who goeth to the Gods as meet oblation, The goat precedeth him, the share of Pusan, and to the Gods the sacrifice announceth.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Invoker, ministering priest, atoner, fire-kindler Soma-presser, sage, reciter, With this well ordered sacrifice, well finished, do ye fill full the channels of the rivers.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The hewers of the post and those who carry it, and those who carve the knob to deck the Horse's stake; Those who prepare the cooking-vessels for the Steed,--may the approving help of these promote our work.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Forth, for the regions of the Gods, the Charger with his smooth back is come my prayer attends him. In him rejoice the singers and the sages. A good friend have we won for the Gods' banquet.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May the fleet Courser's halter and his heel-ropes, the head-stall and the girths and cords about him. And the grass put within his mouth to bait him,--among the Gods, too, let all these be with thee.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: What part of the Steed's flesh the fly hath eaten, or is left sticking to the post or hatchet, Or to the slayer's hands and nails adhereth,--among the Gods, too, may all this be with thee.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Food undigested steaming from his belly, and any odour of raw flesh remaining, This let the immolators set in order and dress the sacrifice with perfect cooking.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: What from thy body which with fire is roasted, when thou art set upon the spit, distilleth, Let not that lie on earth or grass neglected, but to the longing Gods let all be offered.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: They who observing that the Horse is ready call out and say, the smell is good; remove it; And, craving meat, await the distribution,--may their approving help promote labour.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The trial-fork of the flesh-cooking caldron, the vessels out of which the broth is sprinkled, The warming-pots, the covers of the dishes, hooks, carving-boards,--all these attend the Charger.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The starting-place, his place of rest and rolling, the ropes wherewith the Charger's feet were fastened, The water that he drank, the food he tasted,--among the Gods, too, may all these attend thee.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Let not the fire, smoke-scented, make thee crackle, nor glowing caldron smell and break to pieces. Offered, beloved, approved, and consecrated,--such Charger do the Gods accept with favour.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The robe they spread upon the Horse to clothe him, the upper covering and the golden trappings, The halters which restrain the Steed, the heel-ropes,--all these, as grateful to the Gods, they offer.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: If one, when seated, with excessive urging hath with his heel or with his whip distressed thee, All these thy woes, as with the oblations' ladle at sacrifices, with my prayer I banish.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The four-and-thirty ribs of the. Swift Charger, kin to the Gods, the slayer's hatchet pierces. Cut ye with skill, so that the parts be flawless, and piece by piece declaring them dissect them.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Of Tvastar's Charger there is one dissector,--this is the custom-two there are who guide him. Such of his limbs as I divide in order, these, amid the balls, in fire I offer.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Let not thy dear soul burn thee as thou comest, let not the hatchet linger in thy body. Let not a greedy clumsy immolator, missing the joints, mangle thy limbs unduly.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: No, here thou diest not, thou art not injured: by easy paths unto the Gods thou goest. Both Bays, both spotted mares are now thy fellows, and to the ass's pole is yoked the Charger.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May this Steed bring us all-sustaining riches, wealth in good kine, good horses, manly offspring. Freedom from sin may Aditi vouchsafe us: the Steed with our oblations gain us lordship!
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: WHAT time, first springing into life, thou neighedst, proceeding from the sea or upper waters, Limbs of the deer hadst thou, and eagle pinions. O Steed, thy birth is nigh and must be lauded.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: This Steed which Yama gave hath Trita harnessed, and him, the first of all, hath Indra mounted. His bridle the Gandharva grasped. O Vasus, from out the Sun ye fashioned forth the Courser.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Yama art thou, O Horse; thou art Aditya; Trita art thou by secret operation. Thou art divided thoroughly from Soma. They say thou hast three bonds in heaven that hold thee.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Three bonds, they say, thou hast in heaven that bind thee, three in the waters, three within the ocean. To me thou seemest Varuna, O Courser, there where they say is thy sublimest birth-place.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Here-, Courser, are the places where they groomed thee, here are the traces of thy hoofs as winner. Here have I seen the auspicious reins that guide thee, which those who guard the holy Law keep safely.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thyself from far I recognized in spirit,--a Bird that from below flew through the heaven. I saw thy head still soaring, striving upward by paths unsoiled by dust, pleasant to travel.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Here I beheld thy form, matchless in glory, eager to win thee food at the Cow's station. Whene'er a man brings thee to thine enjoyment, thou swallowest the plants most greedy eater.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: After thee, Courser, come the car, the bridegroom, the kine come after, and the charm of maidens. Full companies have followed for thy friendship: the pattern of thy vigour Gods have copied.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Horns made of gold hath he: his feet are iron: less fleet than he, though swift as thought, is Indra. The Gods have come that they may taste the oblation of him who mounted, first of all, the Courser.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Symmetrical in flank, with rounded haunches, mettled like heroes, the Celestial Coursers Put forth their strength, like swans in lengthened order, when they, the Steeds, have reached the heavenly causeway.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: A body formed for flight hast thou, O Charger; swift as the wind in motion is thy spirit. Thy horns are spread abroad in all directions: they move with restless beat in wildernesses.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The strong Steed hath come forward to the slaughter, pondering with a mind directed God-ward. The goat who is his kin is led before him the sages and the singers follow after.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Steed is come unto the noblest mansion, is come unto his Father and his Mother. This day shall he approach the Gods, most welcome: then he declares good gifts to him who offers.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: OF this benignant Priest, with eld grey-coloured, the brother midmost of the three is lightning. The third is he whose back with oil is sprinkled. Here I behold the Chief with seven male children.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Seven to the one-wheeled chariot yoke the Courser; bearing seven names the single Courser draws it. Three-naved the wheel is, sound and undecaying, whereon are resting all these worlds of being.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The seven who on the seven-wheeled car are mounted have horses, seven in tale, who draw them onward. Seven Sisters utter songs of praise together, in whom the names of the seven Cows are treasured.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Who hath beheld him as he sprang to being, seen how the boneless One supports the bony? Where is the blood of earth, the life, the spirit? Who may approach the man who knows, to ask it?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Unripe in mind, in spirit undiscerning, I ask of these the Gods' established places; For up above the yearling Calf the sages, to form a web, their own seven threads have woven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I ask, unknowing, those who know, the sages, as one all ignorant for sake of knowledge, What was that ONE who in the Unborn's image hath stablished and fixed firm these worlds' six regions.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Let him who knoweth presently declare it, this lovely Bird's securely founded station. Forth from his head the Cows draw milk, and, wearing his vesture, with their foot have drunk the water.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Mother gave the Sire his share of Order: with thought, at first, she wedded him in spirit. She, the coy Dame, was filled with dew prolific: with adoration men approached to praise her.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Yoked was the Mother to the boon Cow's car-pole: in the dank rows of cloud the Infant rested. Then the Calf lowed, and looked upon the Mother, the Cow who wears all shapes in three directions.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Bearing three Mothers and three Fathers, single he stood erect: they never make him weary. There on the pitch of heaven they speak together in speech all-knowing but not all-impelling.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Formed with twelve spokes, by length of time, unweakened, rolls round the heaven this wheel of during Order. Herein established, joined in pairs together, seven hundred Sons and twenty stand, O Agni.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: They call him in the farther half of heaven the Sire five-footed, of twelve forms, wealthy in watery store. These others say that he, God with far-seeing eyes, is mounted on the lower seven-wheeled, six-spoked car.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Upon this five-spoked wheel revolving ever all living creatures rest and are dependent. Its axle, heavy-laden, is not heated: the nave from ancient time remains unbroken.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The wheel revolves, unwasting, with its felly: ten draw it, yoked to the far-stretching car-pole. The Sun's eye moves encompassed by the region: on him dependent rest all living creatures.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Of the co-born they call the seventh single-born; the six twin pairs are called Rsis, Children of Gods. Their good gifts sought of men are ranged in order due, and various in their form move for the Lord who guides.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: They told me these were males, though truly females: he who hath eyes sees this, the blind discerns not. The son who is a sage hath comprehended: who knows this rightly is his father's father.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Beneath the upper realm, above this lower, bearing her calf at foot the Cow hath risen. Witherward, to what place hath she departed? Where calves she? Not amid this herd of cattle.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Who, that the father of this Calf discerneth beneath the upper realm, above the lower, Showing himself a sage, may here declare it? Whence hath the Godlike spirit had its rising?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Those that come hitherward they call departing, those that depart they call directed hither. And what so ye have made, Indra and Soma, steeds bear as 'twere yoked to the region's car-pole.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Two Birds with fair wings, knit with bonds of friendship, in the same sheltering tree have found a refuge. One of the twain eats the sweet Fig-tree's fruitage; the other eating not regardeth only.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Where those fine Birds hymn ceaselessly their portion of life eternal, and the sacred synods, There is the Universe's mighty Keeper, who, wise, hath entered into me the simple.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The, tree whereon the fine Birds eat the sweetness, where they all rest and procreate their offspring,-- Upon its top they say the fig is luscious none gaineth it who knoweth not the Father.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: How on the Gayatri the Gayatri was based, how from the Tristup they fashioned the Tristup forth, How on the Jagati was based the Jagati,--they who know this have won themselves immortal life.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With Gayatri he measures out the praise-song, Sama with praise-song, triplet with the Tristup. The triplet with the two or four-foot measure, and with the syllable they form seven metres.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With Jagati the flood in heaven he stablished, and saw the Sun in the Rathantara Saman. Gayatri hath, they say, three brands for kindling: hence it excels in majesty and vigour.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I invocate the milch-cow good for milking so that the milker, deft of hand, may drain her. May Savitar give goodliest stimulation. The caldron is made hot; I will proclaim it.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: She, lady of all treasure, is come hither yearning in spirit for her calf and lowing. May this cow yield her milk for both the Asvins, and may she prosper to our high advantage.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The cow hath lowed after her blinking youngling; she licks his forehead, as she lows, to form it. His mouth she fondly calls to her warm udder, and suckles him with milk while gently lowing.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He also snorts, by whom encompassed round the Cow laws as she clings unto the shedder of the rain. She with her shrilling cries hath humbled mortal man, and, turned to lightning, hath stripped off her covering robe.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: That which hath breath and speed and life and motion lies firmly stablished in the midst of houses. Living, by offerings to the Dead he moveth Immortal One, the brother of the mortal.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I saw the Herdsman, him who never stumbles, approaching by his pathways and departing. He, clothed with gathered and diffusive splendour, within the worlds continually travels.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He who hath made him cloth not comprehend him: from him who saw him surely is he hidden. He, yet enveloped in his Mother's bosom, source of much life, hath sunk into destruction.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Dyaus is my Father, my begetter: kinship is here. This great earth is my kin and Mother. Between the wide-spread world-halves is the birth-place: the Father laid the Daughter's germ within it.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I ask thee of the earth's extremest limit, where is the centre of the world, I ask thee. I ask thee of the Stallion's seed prolific, I ask of highest heaven where Speech abideth.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: This altar is the earth's extremest limit; this sacrifice of ours is the world's centre. The Stallion's seed prolific is the Soma; this Brahman highest heaven where Speech abideth.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Seven germs unripened yet are heaven's prolific seed: their functions they maintain by Visnu's ordinance. Endued with wisdom through intelligence and thought, they compass us about present on every side.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: What thing I truly am I know not clearly: mysterious, fettered in my mind I wander. When the first-born of holy Law approached me, then of this speech I first obtain a portion.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Back, forward goes he, grasped by strength inherent, the Immortal born the brother of the mortal Ceaseless they move in opposite directions: men mark the one, and fail to mark the other.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Upon what syllable of holy praise-song, as twere their highest heaven, the Gods repose them,-- Who knows not this, what will he do with praise-song? But they who know it well sit here assembled.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Fortunate mayst thou be with goodly pasture, and may we also be exceeding wealthy. Feed on the grass, O Cow, at every season, and coming hitherward drink limpid water.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Forming the water-floods, the buffalo hath lowed, one-footed or two-footed or four-footed, she, Who hath become eight-footed or hath got nine feet, the thousand-syllabled in the sublimest heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: From her descend in streams the seas of water; thereby the world's four regions have their being, Thence flows the imperishable flood and thence the universe hath life.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I saw from far away the smoke of fuel with spires that rose on high o'er that beneath it. The Mighty Men have dressed the spotted bullock. These were the customs in the days aforetime,
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Three with long tresses show in ordered season. One of them sheareth when the year is ended. One with his powers the universe regardeth: Of one, the sweep is seen, but his figure.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Speech hath been measured out in four divisions, the Brahmans who have understanding know them. Three kept in close concealment cause no motion; of speech, men speak only the fourth division.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: They call him Indra, Mitra, Varuna, Agni, and he is heavenly nobly-winged Garutman. To what is One, sages give many a title they call it Agni, Yama, Matarisvan.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Dark the descent: the birds are golden-coloured; up to the heaven they fly robed in the waters. Again descend they from the seat of Order, and all the earth is moistened with their fatness.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Twelve are the fellies, and the wheel is single; three are the naves. What man hath understood it? Therein are set together spokes three hundred and sixty, which in nowise can be loosened.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: That breast of thine exhaustless, spring of pleasure, wherewith thou feedest all things that are choicest, Wealth-giver, treasure. finder, free bestower,--bring that, Sarasvati, that we may drain it.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: By means of sacrifice the Gods accomplished their sacrifice: these were the earliest ordinances. These Mighty Ones attained the height of heaven, there where the Sadhyas, Gods of old, are dwelling.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Uniform, with the passing days, this water mounts and fails again. The tempest-clouds give life to earth, and fires re-animate the heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Bird Celestial, vast with noble pinion, the lovely germ of plants, the germ of waters, Him who delighteth us with rain in season, Sarasvan I invoke that he may help us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: WITH what bright beauty are the Maruts jointly invested, peers in age, who dwell together? From what place have they come? With what intention? Sing they their strength through love of wealth, these Heroes?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Whose prayers have they, the Youthful Ones, accepted? Who to his sacrifice hath turned the Maruts? We will delay them on their journey sweeping--with what high spirit!--through the air like eagles.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Whence comest thou alone, thou who art mighty, Indra, Lord of the Brave? What is thy purpose? Thou greetest us when meeting us the Bright Ones. Lord of Bay Steeds, say what thou hast against us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Mine are devotions, hymns; sweet are libations. Strength stirs, and hurled forth is my bolt of thunder. They call for me, their lauds are longing for me. These my Bay Steeds bear me to these oblations.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Therefore together with our strong companions, having adorned our bodies, now we harness, Our spotted deer with might, for thou, O Indra, hast learnt and understood our Godlike nature.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Where was that nature then of yours, O Maruts, that ye charged me alone to slay the Dragon? For I in truth am fierce and strong and mighty. I bent away from every foeman's weapons.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Yea, much hast thou achieved with us for comrades, with manly valour like thine own, thou Hero. Much may we too achieve, O mightiest Indra, with our great power, we Maruts, when we will it.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Vrtra I slew by mine own strength, O Maruts, having waxed mighty in mine indignation. I with the thunder in my hand created for man these lucid softly flowing waters.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary
