verses.translation: Nothing, O Maghavan, stands firm before thee; among the Gods not one is found thine equal. None born or springing into life comes nigh thee. Do what thou hast to do, exceeding mighty?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Mine only be transcendent power, whatever I, daring in my spirit, may accomplish. For I am known as terrible, O Maruts I, Indra, am the Lord of what I ruined.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Now, O ye Maruts, hath your praise rejoiced me, the glorious hymn which ye have made me, Heroes! For me, for Indra, champion strong in battle, for me, yourselves, as lovers for a lover.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Here, truly, they send forth their sheen to meet me, wearing their blameless glory and their vigour. When I have seen you, Maruts, in gay splendour, ye have delighted me, so now delight me.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Who here hath magnified you, O ye Maruts? speed forward, O ye lovers, to your lovers. Ye Radiant Ones, assisting their devotions, of these my holy rites he ye regardful.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To this hath Manya's wisdom brought us, so as to aid, as aids the poet him who worships. Bring hither quick! On to the sage, ye Maruts! These prayers for you the singer hath recited.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May this your praise, may this your song, O Maruts, sung by the poet, Mana's son, Mandarya, Bring offspring for ourselves with food to feed us. May we find strengthening food in full abundance!
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Now let us publish, for the vigorous company the herald of the Strong One, their primeval might. With fire upon your way, O Maruts loud of voice, with battle, Mighty Ones, achieve your deeds of strength.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Bringing the pleasant meath as 'twere their own dear son, they sport in sportive wise gay at their gatherings. The Rudras come with succour to the worshipper; self-strong they fail not him who offers sacrifice.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To whomsoever, bringer of oblations, they immortal guardians, have given plenteous wealth, For him, like loving friends, the Maruts bringing bliss bedew the regions round with milk abundantly.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Ye who with mighty powers have stirred the regions up, your coursers have sped forth directed by themselves. All creatures of the earth, all dwellings are afraid, for brilliant is your coming with your spears advanced.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When they in dazzling rush have made the mountains roar, and shaken heaven's high back in their heroic strength, Each sovran of the forest fears as ye drive near, aid the shrubs fly before you swift as whirling wheels.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Terrible Maruts, ye with ne'er-diminished host, with great benevolence fulfil our heart's desire. Where'er your lightning bites armed with its gory teeth it crunches up the cattle like a well-aimed dart.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Givers of during gifts whose bounties never fail, free from ill-will, at sacrifices glorified, They sing their song aloud that they may drink sweet juice: well do they know the Hero's first heroic deeds.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With castles hundredfold, O Maruts, guard ye well the man whom ye have loved from ruin and from sin,-- The man whom ye the fierce, the Mighty ones who roar, preserve from calumny by cherishing his seed.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Maruts, in your cars are all things that are good: great powers are set as 'twere in rivalry therein. Rings are upon your shoulders when ye journey forth: your axle turns together both the chariot wheels.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Held in your manly arms are many goodly things, gold chains are on your chests, and glistering ornaments, Deer-skins are on their shoulders, on their fellies knives: they spread their glory out as birds spread out their wings.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Mighty in mightiness, pervading, passing strong, visible from afar as 'twere with stars of heaven, Lovely with pleasant tongues, sweet singers with their mouths, the Maruts, joined with Indra, shout forth all around.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: This is your majesty, ye Maruts nobly born, far as the sway of Aditi your bounty spreads. Even Indra by desertion never disannuls the boon bestowed by you upon the pious man.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: This is your kinship, Maruts, that, Immortals, ye were oft in olden time regardful of our call, Having vouchsafed to man a hearing through this prayer, by wondrous deeds the Heroes have displayed their might.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: That, O ye Maruts, we may long time flourish through your abundant riches, O swift movers, And that our men may spread in the encampment, let me complete the rite with these oblations.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May this your laud, may this your song, O Maruts, sung by the poet, Mana's son, Mandarya, Bring offspring for ourselves with food to feed us. May we find strengthening food in full abundance.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: A THOUSAND are thy helps for us, O Indra: a thousand, Lord of Bays, thy choice refreshments. Wealth of a thousand sorts hast thou to cheer us: may precious goods come nigh to us in thousands.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May the most sapient Maruts, with protection, with best boons brought from lofty heaven, approach us, Now when their team of the most noble horses speeds even on the sea's extremest limit.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Close to them clings one moving in seclusion, like a man's wife, like a spear carried rearward, Well grasped, bright, decked with gold there is Vak also, like to a courtly, eloquent dame, among them.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Far off the brilliant, never-weary Maruts cling to the young Maid as a joint possession. The fierce Gods drave not Rodasi before them, but wished for her to grow their friend and fellow.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When chose immortal Rodasi to follow--she with loose tresses and heroic spirit-- She climbed her servant's chariot, she like Surya with cloud-like motion and refulgent aspect.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Upon their car the young men set the Maiden wedded to glory, mighty in assemblies, When your song, Maruts, rose, and, with oblation, the Soma-pourer sang his hymn in worship.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I will declare the greatness of these Maruts, their real greatness, worthy to be lauded, How, with them, she though firm, strong-minded, haughty, travels to women happy in their fortune.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Mitra and Varuna they guard from censure: Aryaman too, discovers worthless sinners Firm things are overthrown that ne'er were shaken: he prospers, Maruts, who gives choice oblations.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: None of us, Maruts, near or at a distance, hath ever reached the limit of your vigour. They in courageous might still waxing boldly have compassed round their foemen like an ocean.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May we this day be dearest friends of Indra, and let us call on him in fight to-morrow. So were we erst. New might attend us daily! So be with us! Rbhuksan of the Heroes!
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May this your laud, may this your song, O Maruts, sung by the poet, Mana's son, Mandarya, Bring offspring for ourselves with. food to feed us. May we find strengthening food in full abundance.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: SWIFT gain is his who hath you near at every rite: ye welcome every song of him who serves the Gods. So may I turn you hither with fair hymns of praise to give great succour for the weal of both the worlds.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Surrounding, as it were, self-born, self-powerful, they spring to life the shakers-down of food and light; Like as the countess undulations of the floods, worthy of praise when near, like bullocks and like kine.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: They who, like Somas with their well-grown stalks pressed out, imbibed within the heart, dwell there in friendly wise. Upon their shoulders rests as 'twere a warrior's spear and in their hand they hold a dagger and a ring.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Self-yoked they have descended lightly from the sky. With your own lash, Immortals, urge yourselves to speed. Unstained by dust the Maruts, mighty in their strength, have cast down e'en firm things, armed with their shining spears.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Who among you, O Maruts armed with lightning-spears, moveth you by himself, as with the tongue his jaws? Ye rush from heaven's floor as though ye sought for food, on many errands like the Sun's diurnal Steed.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Say where, then, is this mighty region's farthest bound, where, Maruts, is the lowest depth that ye have reached, When ye cast down like chaff the firmly stablished pile, and from the mountain send the glittering water-flood?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Your winning is with strength, dazzling, with heavenly light, with fruit mature, O Maruts, fall of plenteousness. Auspicious is your gift like a free giver's meed, victorious, spreading far, as of immortal Gods.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The rivers roar before your chariot fellies when they are uttering the voice of rain-clouds. The lightnings laugh upon the earth beneath them, what time the Maruts scatter forth their fatness.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Prsni brought forth, to fight the mighty battle, the glittering army of the restless Maruts. Nurtured together they begat the monster, and then looked round them for the food that strengthens.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May this your laud, may this your song O Maruts, sung by the poet Mana's son, Mandarya, Bring offspring for ourselves with food to feed us. May we find strengthening food in full abundance.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: As, Indra, from great treason thou protectest, yea, from great treachery these who approach us, So, marking well, Controller of the Maruts grant us their blessings, for they are thy dearest.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The various doings of all mortal people by thee are ordered, in thy wisdom, Indra. The host of Maruts goeth forth exulting to win the light-bestowing spoil of battle.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: That spear of thine sat firm for us, O Indra: the Maruts set their whole dread power in motion. E'en Agni shines resplendent in the brush-wood: the viands hold him as floods hold an island.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Vouchsafe us now that opulence, O Indra, as guerdon won by mightiest donation. May hymns that please thee cause the breast of Vayu to swell as with the mead's refreshing sweetness.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With thee, O Indra, are most bounteous riches that further every one who lives uprightly. Now may these Maruts show us loving-kindness, Gods who of old were ever prompt to help us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Bring forth the Men who rain down boons, O Indra: exert thee in the great terrestrial region; For their broad-chested speckled deer are standing like a King's armies on the field of battle.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Heard is the roar of the advancing Maruts, terrific, glittering, and swiftly moving, Who with their rush o'erthrow as 'twere a sinner the mortal who would fight with those who love him
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Give to the Manas, Indra with Maruts, gifts universal, gifts of cattle foremost. Thou, God, art praised with Gods who must be lauded. May we find strengthening food in full abundance.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: NAUGHT is to-day, to-morrow naught. Who comprehends the mystery? We must address ourselves unto another's thought, and lost is then the hope we formed.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Maruts are thy brothers. Why, O Indra, wouldst thou take our lives? Agree with them in friendly wise, and do not slay us in the fight.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Agastya, brother, why dost thou neglect us, thou who art our friend? We know the nature of thy mind. Verity thou wilt give us naught.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Let them prepare the altar, let them kindle fire in front: we two Here will spread sacrifice for thee, that the Immortal may observe.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou, Lord of Wealth, art Master of all treasures, thou, Lord of friends, art thy friends' best supporter. O Indra, speak thou kindly with the Maruts, and taste oblations in their proper season.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To you I come with this mine adoration, and with a hymn I crave the Strong Ones' favour A hymn that truly makes you joyful, Maruts. Suppress your anger and unyoke your horses.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Maruts, to you this laud with prayer and worship, formed in the mind and heart, ye Gods, is offered. Come ye to us, rejoicing in your spirit, for ye are they who make our prayer effective.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Maruts, praised by us, shall show us favour; Maghavan, lauded, shall be most propitious. Maruts,, may all our days that are to follow be very pleasant, lovely and triumphant.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I fled in terror from this mighty Indra, my body trembling in alarm, O Maruts. Oblations meant for you had been made ready; these have we set aside: for this forgive us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: By whom the Manas recognize the day-springs, by whose strength at the dawn of endless mornings, Give us, thou Mighty, glory with Maruts. fierce with the fierce, the Strong who givest triumph.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Do thou, O Indra, guard the conquering Heroes, and rid thee of thy wrath against the Maruts, With them, the wise, victorious and bestowing. May we find strengthening food in full abundance.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: WONDERFUL let your coming be, wondrous with help, ye Bounteous Ones, Maruts, who gleam as serpents gleam.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Far be from us, O Maruts, ye free givers, your impetuous shaft; Far from us be the stone ye hurl.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Bounteous Givers, touch ye not, O Maruts, Trnskanda's folk; Lift ye us up that we may live.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: THE praise-song let him sing forth bursting bird-like: sing we that hymn which like heaven's light expandeth, That the milk-giving cows may, unimpeded call to the sacred grass the Gods' assembly.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Let the Bull sing with Bulls whose toil is worship, with a loud roar like some wild beast that hungers. Praised God! the glad priest brings his heart's devotion; the holy youth presents twofold oblation.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May the Priest come circling the measured stations, and with him bring the earth's autumnal fruitage. Let the Horse neigh led near, let the Steer bellow: let the Voice go between both worlds as herald,
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To him we offer welcomest oblations, the pious bring their strength-inspiring praises. May Indra, wondrous in his might, accept them, car-borne and swift to move like the Nasatyas.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Praise thou that Indra who is truly mighty, the car-borne Warrior, Maghavan the Hero; Stronger in war than those who fight against him, borne by strong steeds, who kills enclosing darkness;
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Him who surpasses heroes in his greatness: the earth and heavens suffice not for his girdles. Indra endues the earth to be his garment, and, God-like, wears the heaven as 'twere a frontlet,
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thee, Hero, guardian of the brave in battles, who roamest in the van,--to draw thee hither, Indra, the hosts agree beside the Soma, and joy, for his great actions, in the Chieftain.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Libations in the sea to thee are pleasant, when thy divine Floods come to cheer these people. To thee the Cow is sum of all things grateful when with the wish thou seekest men and princes.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: So may we in this One be well befriended, well aided as it were through praise of chieftains, That Indra still may linger at our worship, as one led swift to work, to hear our praises.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Like men in rivalry extolling princes, our Friend be Indra, wielder of the thunder. Like true friends of some city's lord within them held in good rule with sacrifice they help him.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: For every sacrifice makes Indra stronger, yea, when he goes around angry in spirit; As pleasure at the ford invites the thirsty, as the long way brings him who gains his object.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Let us not here contend with Gods, O Indra, for here, O Mighty One, is thine own portion, The Great, whose Friends the bounteous Maruts honour, as with a stream, his song who pours oblations.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Addressed to thee is this our praise, O Indra: Lord of Bay Steeds, find us hereby advancement. So mayst thou lead us on, O God, to comfort. May we find strengthening food in full abundance.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: THOU art the King of all the Gods, O Indra: protect the men, O Asura, preserve us. Thou Lord of Heroes, Maghavan, our saver, art faithful, very rich, the victory-giver.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Indra, thou humbledst tribes that spake with insult by breaking down seven autumn forts, their refuge. Thou stirredst, Blameless! billowy floods, and gavest his foe a prey to youthful Purukutsa.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With whom thou drivest troops whose lords are heroes, and bringest daylight now, much worshipped Indra, With them guard lion-like wasting active Agni to dwell in our tilled fields and in our homestead.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: They through the greatness of thy spear, O Indra, shall, to thy praise, rest in this earthly station. To loose the floods, to seek, for kine, the battle, his Bays he mounted boldly seized the booty.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Indra, bear Kutsa, him in whom thou joyest: the dark-red horses of the Wind are docile. Let the Sun roll his chariot wheel anear us, and let the Thunderer go to meet the foemen.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou Indra, Lord of Bays, made strong by impulse, hast slain the vexers of thy friends, who give not. They who beheld the Friend beside the living were cast aside by thee as they rode onward.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Indra, the bard sang forth in inspiration: thou madest earth a covering for the Dasa. Maghavan made the three that gleam with moisture, and to his home brought Kuyavac to slay him.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: These thine old deeds new bards have sung, O Indra. Thou conqueredst, boundest many tribes for ever. Like castles thou hast crushed the godless races, and bowed the godless scorner's deadly weapon.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: A Stormer thou hast made the stormy waters flow down, O Indra, like the running rivers. When o'er the flood thou broughtest them, O Hero, thou keptest Turvasa and Yadu safely.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Indra, mayst thou be ours in all occasions, protector of the men, most gentle-hearted, Giving us victory over all our rivals. May we find strengthening food in full abundance.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: GLAD thee: thy glory hath been quaffed, Lord of Bay Steeds, as 'twere the bowl's enlivening mead. For thee the Strong there is strong drink, mighty, omnipotent to win.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Let our strong drink, most excellent, exhilarating, come to thee, Victorious, Indra! bringing gain, immortal conquering in fight,
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou, Hero, winner of the spoil, urgest to speed the car of man. Burn, like a vessel with the flame, the lawless Dasyu, Conqueror!
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Empowered by thine own might, O Sage, thou stolest Surya's chariot wheel. Thou barest Kutsa with the steeds of Wind to Susna as his death.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Most mighty is thy rapturous joy, most splendid is thine active power, Wherewith, foe-slaying, sending bliss, thou art supreme in gaining steeds.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: As thou, O Indra, to the ancient singers wast ever joy, as water to the thirsty, So unto thee I sing this invocation. May we find strengthening food in full abundance.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: CHEER thee with draughts to win us bliss: Soma, pierce Indra in thy strength. Thou stormest trembling in thy rage, and findest not a foeman nigh.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Make our songs penetrate to him who is the Only One of men; For whom the sacred food is spread, as the steer ploughs the barley in.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Within whose hands deposited all the Five Peoples' treasures rest. Mark thou the man who injures us and kill him like the heavenly bolt.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Slay everyone who pours no gift, who, hard to reach, delights thee not. Bestow on us what wealth he hath: this even the worshipper awaits.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou helpest him the doubly strong whose hymns were sung unceasingly. When Indra fought, O Soma, thou helpest the mighty in the fray.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: As thou, O Indra, to the ancient singers wast ever joy, like water to the thirsty, So unto thee I sing this invocation. May we find strengthening food in full abundance.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: THE Bull of men, who cherishes all people, King of the Races, Indra, called of many, Fame-loving, praised, hither to me with succour turn having yoked both vigorous Bay Horses!
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thy mighty Stallions, yoked by prayer, O Indra, thy. Coursers to thy mighty chariot harnessed,-- Ascend thou these, and borne by them come hither: with Soma juice out. poured, Indra, we call thee.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Ascend thy mighty car: the mighty Soma is poured for thee and sweets are sprinkled round us. Come down to us-ward, Bull of human races, come, having harnessed them, with strong Bay Horses.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Here is God-reaching sacrifice, here the victim; here, Indra, are the prayers, here is the Soma. Strewn is the sacred grass: come hither, Sakra; seat thee and drink: unyoke thy two Bay Coursers.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Come to us, Indra, come thou highly lauded to the devotions of the singer Mana. Singing, may we find early through thy succour, may we find strengthening food in full abundance.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: IF, Indra, thou hast given that gracious hearing where with thou helpest those who sang thy praises. Blast not the wish that would exalt us may I gain all from thee, and pay all man's devotions.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Let not the Sovran Indra disappoint us in what shall bring both Sisters to our dwelling. To him have run the quickly flowing waters. May Indra come to us with life and friendship.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Victorious with the men, Hero in battles, Indra, who hears the singer's supplication, Will bring his car nigh to the man who offers, if he himself upholds the songs that praise him.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Yea, Indra, with the men, through love of glory consumes the sacred food which friends have offered. The ever-strengthening song of him who worships is sung in fight amid the clash of voices.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Aided by thee, O Maghavan, O Indra, may we subdue our foes who count them mighty. Be our protector, strengthen and increase us. May we find strengthening food in full abundance.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: LIGHTLY your coursers travel through the regions when round the sea of air your car is flying. Your golden fellies scatter drops of moisture: drinking the sweetness ye attend the Mornings.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Ye as ye travel overtake the Courser who flies apart, the Friend of man, most holy. The prayer is that the Sister may convey you, all praised, meath-drinkers! to support and strengthen.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Ye have deposited, matured within her, in the raw cow the first milk of the milch-cow, Which the bright offerer, shining like a serpent mid trees, presents to you whose form is perfect.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Ye made the fierce heat to be full of sweetness for Atri at his wish, like streaming water. Fire-offering thence is yours, O Asvins, Heroes: your car-wheels speed to us like springs of honey.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Like Tugra's ancient son may I, ye Mighty, bring you to give your gifts with milk-oblations. Your greatness compasseth Earth, Heaven, and Waters: decayed for you is sorrow's net, ye Holy.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When, Bounteous Ones, ye drive your yoked team downward, ye send, by your own natures, understanding. Swift as the wind let the prince please and feast you: he, like a pious man, gains strength for increase.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: For verily we truthful singers praise you the niggard trafficker is here excluded. Now, even now do ye O blameless Asvins, ye Mighty, guard the man whose God is near him.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: You of a truth day after day, O Asvins, that he might win the very plenteous torrent, Agastya, famous among mortal heroes, roused with a thousand lauds like sounds of music.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When with the glory of your car ye travel, when we go speeding like the priest of mortals, And give good horses to sacrificers, may we, Nasatyas! gain our share of riches.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With songs of praise we call to-day, O Asvins, that your new chariot, for our own well-being, That circles heaven with never-injured fellies. May we find strengthening food in full abundance.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: WHAT, dearest Pair, is this in strength and riches that ye as Priests are bring from the waters? This sacrifice is your glorification, ye who protect mankind and give them treasures.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May your pure steeds, rain-drinkers, bring you hither, swift as the tempest, your celestial coursers, Rapid as thought, with fair backs, full of vigour, resplendent in their native light, O Asvins.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Your car is like a torrent rushing downward: may it come nigh, broad-seated, for our welfare,-- Car holy, strong, that ever would be foremost, thought-swift, which ye, for whom we long, have mounted.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Here sprung to life, they both have sung together, with bodies free from stain, with signs that mark them; One of you Prince of Sacrifice, the Victor, the other counts as Heaven's auspicious offspring.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May your car-seat, down-gliding, golden-coloured, according to your wish approach our dwellings. Men shall feed full the bay steeds of the other, and, Asvins they with roars shall stir the regions.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Forth comes your strong Bull like a cloud of autumn, sending abundant food of liquid sweetness. Let them feed with the other's ways and vigour: the upper streams have come and do us service.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Your constant song hath been sent forth, Disposers! that flows threefold in mighty strength, O Asvins. Thus lauded, give the suppliant protection moving or resting hear mine invocation.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: This song of bright contents for you is swelling in the men's hall where three-fold grass is ready. Your strong rain-cloud, ye Mighty Ones, hath swollen, honouring men as 'twere with milk's outpouring.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The prudent worshipper, like Pusan, Asvins! praises you as he praises Dawn and Agni, When, singing with devotion, he invokes you. May we find strengthening food in full abundance.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: THIS was the task. Appear promptly, ye prudent Ones. Here is the chariot drawn by strong steeds: be ye glad. Heart-stirring, longed for, succourers of Vispala, here are Heaven's Sons whose sway blesses the pious man.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Longed for, most Indra-like, mighty, most Marut-like, most wonderful in deed, car-borne, best charioteers, Bring your full chariot hither heaped with liquid sweet: thereon, ye Asvins, come to him who offers gifts.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: What make ye there, ye Mighty? Wherefore linger ye with folk who, offering not, are held in high esteem? Pass over them; make ye the niggard's life decay: give light unto the singer eloquent in praise.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Crunch up on. every side the dogs who bark at us: slay ye our foes, O Asvins this ye understand. Make wealthy every word of him who praises you: accept with favour, both Nasatyas, this my laud.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Ye made for Tugra's son amid the water-floods that animated ship with wings to fly withal, Whereon with God-devoted mind ye brought him forth, and fled with easy flight from out the mighty surge.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Four ships most welcome in the midst of ocean, urged by the Asvins, save the son of Tugra, Him who was cast down headlong in the waters, plunged in the thick inevitable darkness.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: What tree was that which stood fixed in surrounding sea to which the son of Tugra supplicating clung? Like twigs, of which some winged creature may take hold, ye, Asvins, bore him off safely to your renown.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Welcome to you be this the hymn of praises uttered by Manas, O Nasatyas, Heroes, From this our gathering where we offer Soma. May we find strengthening food in full abundance.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: MAKE ready that which passes thought in swiftness, that hath three wheels and triple seat, ye Mighty, Whereon ye seek the dwelling of the pious, whereon, threefold, ye fly like birds with pinions.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Light rolls your easy chariot faring earthward, what time, for food, ye, full of wisdom, mount it. May this song, wondrous fair, attend your glory: ye, as ye travel, wait on Dawn Heaven's Daughter.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Ascend your lightly rolling car, approaching the worshipper who turns him to his duties,-- Whereon ye come unto the house to quicken man and his offspring, O Nasatyas, Heroes.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Let not the wolf, let not the she-wolf harm you. Forsake me not, nor pass me by or others. Here stands your share, here is your hymn, ye Mighty: yours are these vessels, full of pleasant juices.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Gotama, Purumilha, Atri bringing oblations all invoke you for protection. Like one who goes straight to the point directed, ye Nasatyas, to mine invocation.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: We have passed o'er the limit of this darkness: our praise hath been bestowed on you, O Asvins. Come hitherward by paths which Gods have travelled. May we find strengthening food in full abundance.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: LET us invoke you both this day and after the priest is here with lauds when morn is breaking: Nasatyas, wheresoe'er ye be, Heaven's Children, for him who is more liberal than the godless.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With us, ye Mighty, let yourselves be joyful, glad in our stream of Soma slay the niggards. Graciously hear my hymns and invitations, marking, O Heroes, with your cars my longing.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Nasatyas, Pusans, ye as Gods for glory arranged and set in order Surya's bridal. Your giant steeds move on, sprung from the waters, like ancient times of Varuna the Mighty.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Your grace be with us, ye who love sweet juices: further the hymn sung by the poet Mana, When men are joyful in your glorious actions, to win heroic strength, ye Bounteous Givers.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: This praise was made, O liberal Lords, O Asvins, for you with fair adornment by the Manas. Come to our house for us and for our children, rejoicing, O Nasatyas, in Agastya.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: We have passed o'er the limit of this darkness: our praise hath been bestowed on you, O Asvins. Come hitherward by paths which Gods have travelled. may we find strengthening food in full abundance.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: WHETHER of these is elder, whether later? How were they born? Who knoweth it, ye sages? These of themselves support all things existing: as on a car the Day and Night roll onward.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Twain uphold, though motionless and footless, a widespread offspring having feet and moving. Like your own son upon his parents' bosom, protect us, Heaven and earth, from fearful danger.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I call for Aditi's unrivalled bounty, perfect, celestial, deathless, meet for worship. Produce this, ye Twain Worlds, for him who lauds you. Protect us, Heaven and Earth, from fearful danger.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May we be close to both the Worlds who suffer no pain, Parents of Gods, who aid with favour, Both mid the Gods, with Day and Night alternate. Protect us, Heaven and Earth, from fearful danger.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Faring together, young, with meeting limits, Twin Sisters lying in their Parents' bosom, Kissing the centre of the world together. Protect us, Heaven and Earth, from fearful danger.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Duly I call the two wide seats, the mighty, the general Parents, with the God's protection. Who, beautiful to look on, make the nectar. Protect us, Heaven and Earth, from fearful danger.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Wide, vast, and manifold, whose bounds are distant,--these, reverent, I address at this our worship, The blessed Pair, victorious, all-sustaining. Protect us, Heaven and Earth, from fearful danger.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: What sin we have at any time committed against the Gods, our friend, our house's chieftain, Thereof may this our hymn be expiation. Protect us, Heaven and Earth, from fearful danger.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May both these Friends of man, who bless, preserve me, may they attend me with their help and favour. Enrich the man more liberal than the godless. May we, ye Gods, be strong with food rejoicing.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Endowed with understanding, I have uttered this truth, for all to hear, to Earth and Heaven. Be near us, keep us from reproach and trouble. Father and Mother, with your help preserve us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Be this my prayer fulfilled, O Earth and Heaven, wherewith, Father and Mother, I address you. Nearest of Gods be ye with your protection. May we find strengthening food in full abundance.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: LOVED of all men, may Savitar, through praises offered as sacred food, come to our synod, That you too, through-our hymn, ye ever-youthful, may gladden, at your visit, all our people.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To us may all the Gods come trooped together, Aryaman, Mitra, Varuna concordant, That all may be promoters of our welfare, and with great might preserve our strength from slackness.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Agni I sing, the guest you love most dearly: the Conqueror through our lauds is friendly-minded. That he may be our Varuna rich in glory and send food like a prince praised by the godly.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To you I seek with reverence, Night and Morning, like a cow good to milk, with hope to conquer, Preparing on a common day the praise. song with milk of various hues within this udder.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May the great Dragon of the Deep rejoice us: as one who nourishes her young comes Sindhu, With whom we will incite the Child of Waters whom vigorous course swift as thought bring hither.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Moreover Tvastar also shall approach us, one-minded with the princes at his visit. Hither shall come the Vrtra-slayer Indra, Ruler of men, as strongest of the Heroes.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Him too our hymns delight, that yoke swift horses, like mother cows who lick their tender youngling. To him our songs shall yield themselves like spouses, to him the most delightful of the Heroes.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: So may the Maruts, armed with mighty weapons, rest here on heaven and earth with hearts in concord, As Gods whose cars have dappled steeds like torrents, destroyers of the foe allies of Mitra.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: They hasten on to happy termination their orders when they are made known by glory. As on a fair bright day the arrow flieth o'er all the barren soil their missiles sparkle.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Incline the Asvins to show grace, and Pusan, for power and might have they, their own possession. Friendly are Visnu, Vata, and Rbhuksan so may I bring the Gods to make us happy.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: This is my reverent thought of you, ye Holy; may it inspire you, make you dwell among us,-- Thought, toiling for the Gods and seeking treasure. May we find strengthening food in full abundance.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Now will I glorify Food that upholds great strength, By whose invigorating power Trita rent Vrtra limb from limb.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O pleasant Food, O Food of meath, thee have we chosen for our own, So be our kind protector thou.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Come hitherward to us, O Food, auspicious with auspicious help, Health-bringing, not unkind, a dear and guileless friend.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: These juices which, O Food, are thine throughout the regions are diffused. like winds they have their place in heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: These gifts of thine, O Food, O Food most sweet to taste, These savours of thy juices work like creatures that have mighty necks.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: In thee, O Food, is set the spirit of great Gods. Under thy flag brave deeds were done he slew the Dragon with thy help.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: If thou be gone unto the splendour of the clouds, Even from thence, O Food of meath, prepared for our enjoyment, come.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Whatever morsel we consume from waters or from plants of earth, O Soma, wax thou fat thereby.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: What Soma, we enjoy from thee in milky food or barley-brew, Vatapi, grow thou fat thereby.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Vegetable, Cake of meal, he wholesome, firm, and strengthening: Vatapi, grow thou fat thereby.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Food, from thee as such have we drawn forth with lauds, like cows, our sacrificial gifts, From thee who banquetest with Gods, from thee who banquetest with us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: WINNER of thousands, kindled, thou shinest a God with Gods to-day. Bear out oblations, envoy, Sage.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Child of Thyself the sacrifice is for the righteous blent with meath, Presenting viands thousandfold.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Invoked and worthy of our praise bring Gods whose due is sacrifice: Thou, Agni, givest countless gifts.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To seat a thousand Heroes they eastward have strewn the grass with might, Whereon, Adityas, ye shine forth.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The sovran all-imperial Doors, wide, good, many and manifold, Have poured their streams of holy oil.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With gay adornment, fair to see, in glorious beauty shine they forth: Let Night and Morning rest them here.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Let these two Sages first of all, heralds divine and eloquent, Perform for us this sacrifice.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: You I address, Sarasvati, and Bharati, and Ila, all: Urge ye us on to glorious fame.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Tvastar the Lord hath made all forms and all the cattle of the field Cause them to multiply for us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Send to the Gods, Vanaspati, thyself, the sacrificial draught: Let Agni make the oblations sweet.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Agni, preceder of the Gods, is honoured with the sacred song: He glows at offerings blest with Hail!
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: BY goodly paths lead us to riches, Agni, God who knowest every sacred duty. Remove the sin that makes us stray and wander. most ample adoration will we bring thee.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Lead us anew to happiness, O Agni; lead us beyond all danger and affliction. Be unto us a wide broad ample castle bless, prosper on their way our sons and offspring.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Far from us, Agni, put thou all diseases let them strike lauds that have no saving Agni. God, make our home again to be a blessing, with all the Immortal Deities, O Holy.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Preserve us, Agni, with perpetual succour, refulgent in the dwelling which thou lovest. O Conqueror, most youthful, let no danger touch him who praises thee to-day or after.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Give not us up a prey to sin, O Agni, the greedy enemy that brings us trouble; Not to the fanged that bites, not to the toothless: give not us up, thou Conqueror, to the spoiler.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Such as thou art, born after Law, O Agni when lauded give protection to our bodies, From whosoever would reproach or injure: for thou, God, rescuest from all oppression.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou, well discerning both these classes, comest to men at early morn, O holy Agni. Be thou obedient unto man at evening, to be adorned, as keen, by eager suitors.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To him have we addressed our pious speeches, I, Mana's son, to him victorious Agni. May we gain countless riches with the sages. May we find strengthening food in full abundance.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: GLORIFY thou Brhaspati, the scatheless, who must be praised with hymns, sweet-tongued and mighty, To whom as leader of the song, resplendent, worthy of lauds, both Gods and mortals listen.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: On him wait songs according to the season even as a stream of pious men set moving. Brhaspati--for he laid out the expanses--was, at the sacrifice, vast Matarisvan.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The praise, the verse that offers adoration, may he bring forth, as the Sun sends his arms out, He who gives daily light through this God's wisdom, strong as a dread wild beast, and inoffensive.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: His song of praise pervades the earth and heaven: let the wise worshipper draw it, like a courser. These of Brhaspati, like hunters' arrows, go to the skies that change their hue like serpents.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Those, God, who count thee as a worthless bullock, and, wealthy sinners, live on thee the Bounteous,-- On fools like these no blessing thou bestowest: Brhaspati, thou punishest the spiteful.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Like a fair path is he, where grass is pleasant, though hard to win, a Friend beloved most early. Those who unharmed by enemies behold us, while they would make them bare, stood closely compassed.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He to whom songs of praise go forth like torrents, as rivers eddying under banks flow sea-ward-- Brhaspati the wise, the eager, closely looks upon both, the waters and the vessel.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: So hath Brhaspati, great, strong and mighty, the God exceeding powerful, been brought hither. May he thus lauded give us kine and horses. May we find strengthening food in full abundance.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: VENOMOUS, slightly venomous, or venomous aquatic worm,-- Both creatures, stinging, unobserved, with poison have infected me.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Coming, it kills the unobserved; it kills them as it goes away, It kills them as it drives them off, and bruising bruises them to death.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Sara grass, Darbha, Kusara, and Sairya, Muñja, Virana, Where all these creatures dwell unseen, with poison have infected me.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The cows had settled in their stalls, the beasts of prey had sought their lairs, Extinguished were the lights of men, when things unseen infected me.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Or these, these reptiles, are observed, like lurking thieves at evening time. Seers of all, themselves unseen: be therefore very vigilant.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Heaven is your Sire, your Mother Earth, Soma your Brother, Aditi Your Sister: seeing all, unseen, keep still and dwell ye happily.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Biters of shoulder or of limb, with needle-stings, most venomous, Unseen, whatever ye may be, vanish together and be gone.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Slayer of things unseen, the Sun, beheld of all, mounts, eastward, up, Consuming all that are not seen, and evil spirits of the night.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: There hath the Sun-God mounted up, who scorches much and everything. Even the Aditya from the hills, all-seen, destroying things unseen.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I hang the poison in the Sun, a wine-skin in a vintner's house, He will not die, nor shall we die: his path is far: he whom Bay Horses bear hath turned thee to sweet meath.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: This little bird, so very small, hath swallowed all thy poison up. She will not die, nor shall we die: his path is far: he whom Bay Horses bear hath turned thee to sweet meath.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The three-times-seven bright sparks of fire have swallowed up the poison's strength. They will not die, nor shall we die: his path is far: he whom Bay Horses bear hath turned thee to sweet meath.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Of ninety rivers and of nine with power to stay the venom's course,-- The names of all I have secured: his path is far: he whom Bay Horses bear hath turned thee to sweet meath.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: So have the peahens three-times-seven, so have the maiden Sisters Seven Carried thy venom far away, as girls bear water in their jars.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The poison-insect is so small; I crush the creature with a stone. I turn the poison hence away, departed unto distant lands.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Forth issuing from the mountain's side the poison-insect spake and said: Scorpion, they venom is but weak.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: THOU, Agni, shining in thy glory through the days, art brought to life from out the waters, from the stone: From out the forest trees and herbs that grow on ground, thou, Sovran Lord of men art generatad [sic] pure.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thine is the Herald's task and Cleanser's duly timed; Leader art thou, and Kindler for the pious man. Thou art Director, thou the ministering Priest: thou art the Brahman, Lord and Master in our home.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Hero of Heroes, Agni! Thou art Indra, thou art Visnu of the Mighty Stride, adorable: Thou, Brahmanaspati, the Brahman finding wealth: thou, O Sustainer, with thy wisdom tendest us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Agni, thou art King Varuna whose laws stand fast; as Mitra, Wonder-Worker, thou must be implored. Aryaman, heroes' Lord, art thou, enrich ing all, and liberal Amsa in the synod, O thou God.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou givest strength, as Tvastar, to the worshipper: thou wielding Mitra's power hast kinship with the Dames. Thou, urging thy fleet coursers, givest noble steeds: a host of heroes art thou with great store of wealth.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Rudra art thou, the Asura of mighty heaven: thou art the Maruts' host, thou art the Lord of food, Thou goest with red winds: bliss hast thou in thine home. As Pusan thou thyself protectest worshippers.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Giver of wealth art thou to him who honours thee; thou art God Savitar, granter of precious things. As Bhaga, Lord of men! thou rulest over wealth, and guardest in his house him who hath served thee well.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To thee, the people's Lord within the house, the folk press forward to their King most graciously inclined. Lord of the lovely look, all things belong to thee: ten, hundred, yea, a thousand are outweighed by thee.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Agni, men seek thee as a Father with their prayers, win thee, bright-formed, to brotherhood with holy act. Thou art a Son to him who duly worships thee, and as a trusty Friend thou guardest from attack.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: A Rbhu art thou, Agni, near to be adored thou art the Sovran Lord of foodful spoil and wealth. Thou shinest brightly forth, thou burnest to bestow: pervading sacrifice, thou lendest us thine help.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou, God, art Aditi to him who offers gifts: thou, Hotri, Bharati, art strengthened by the song. Thou art the hundred-wintered Ila to give strength, Lord of Wealth! Vrtra-slayer and Sarasvati.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou, Agni, cherished well, art highest vital power; in thy delightful hue are glories visible. Thou art the lofty might that furthers each design: thou art wealth manifold, diffused on every side.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thee, Agni, have the Adityas taken as their mouth; the Bright Ones have made thee, O Sage, to be their tongue. They who love offerings cling to thee at solemn rites: by thee the Gods devour the duly offered food.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: By thee, O Agni, all the Immortal guileless Gods eat with thy mouth the oblation that is offered them. By thee do mortal men give sweetness to their drink. Bright art thou born, the embryo of the plants of earth.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With these thou art united, Agni; yea thou, God of noble birth, surpassest them in majesty, Which, through the power of good, here spreads abroad from thee, diffused through both the worlds, throughout the earth and heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The princely worshippers who send to those who sing thy praise, O Agni, guerdon graced with kine and steeds,- Lead thou both these and us forward to higher bliss. With brave men in the assembly may we speak aloud.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: WITH sacrifice exalt Agni who knows all life; worship him 'with oblation and the song of praise, Well kindled, nobly fed; heaven's Lord, Celestial Priest, who labours at the pole where deeds of might are done.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: At night and morning, Agni, have they called to thee, like milch-kine in their stalls lowing to meet their young. As messenger of heaven thou lightest all night long the families of men. Thou Lord of precious boons.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Him have the Gods established at the region's base, doer of wondrous deeds, Herald of heaven and earth; Like a most famous car, Agni the purely bright, like Mitra. to be glorified among the folk.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Him have they set in his own dwelling, in the vault, like the Moon waxing, fulgent, in the realm of air. Bird of the firmament, observant with his eyes, guard of the place as 'twere, looking to Gods and men.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May he as Priest encompass all the sacrifice. men throng to him with offerings and with hymns of praise. Raging with jaws of gold among the growing plants, like heaven with all the stars, he quickens earth and sky.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Such as thou art, brilliantly kindled for our weal, a liberal giver, send us riches in thy shine, For our advantage, Agni, God, bring Heaven and Earth hither that they may taste oblation brought by man.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Agni, give us great wealth, give riches thousandfold. unclose to us, like doors, strength that shall bring renown. Make Heaven and Earth propitious through the power of prayer, and like the sky's bright sheen let mornings beam on us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Enkindled night by night at every morning's dawn, may he shine forth with red flame like the realm of light,- Agni adored in beauteous rites with lauds of men, fair guest of living man and King of all our folk.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Song chanted by us men, O Agni, Ancient One, has swelled unto the deathless Gods in lofty heaven- A milch-cow yielding to the singer in the rites wealth manifold, in hundreds, even as he wills.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Agni, may we show forth our valour with the steed or with the power of prayer beyond all other men; And over the Five Races let our glory shine high like the realm of light and unsurpassable.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Such, Conqueror! be to us, be worthy of our praise, thou for whom princes nobly born exert themselves; Whose sacrifice the strong seek, Agni, when it shines for never-failing offspring in thine own abode.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Knower of all that lives, O Agni may we both, singers of praise and chiefs, be in thy keeping still. Help us to wealth exceeding good and glorious, abundant, rich in children and their progeny.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The princely worshippers who send to those who sing thy praise, O Agni, guerdon, graced with kine and steeds,- Lead thou both these and us forward to higher bliss. With brave men in the assembly may we speak aloud.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: AGNI is set upon the earth well kindled; he standeth in the presence of all beings. Wise, ancient, God, the Priest and Purifier, let Agni serve the Gods for he is worthy.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May Narasamsa lighting up the chambers, bright in his majesty through threefold heaven, Steeping the gift with oil diffusing purpose, bedew the Gods at chiefest time of worship.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Adored in heart, as is thy right, O Agni, serve the Gods first to-day before the mortal. Bring thou the Marut host. Ye men do worship to Indra seated on the grass, eternal.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Grass divine, increasing, rich in heroes, strewn for wealth' sake, well laid upon this altar,- On this bedewed with oil sit ye, O Vasus, sit all ye Gods, ye Holy, ye Adityas.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Wide be the Doors, the Goddesses, thrown open, easy to pass, invoked, through adorations, Let them unfold, expansive, everlasting, that sanctify the class famed, rich in heroes.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Good work for us, the glorious Night and Morning, like female weavers, waxen from aforetime, Yielders of rich milk, interweave in concert the long-extended thread, the web of worship.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Let the two heavenly Heralds, first, most wise, most fair, present oblation duly with the sacred verse, Worshipping God at ordered seasons decking them at three high places at the centre of the earth.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Sarasvati who perfects our devotion, Ila divine, Bharati all surpassing,- Three Goddesses, with power inherent, seated, protect this holy Grass, our flawless refuge!
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Born is the pious hero swift of hearing, like gold in hue, well formed, and full of vigour. May Tvastar lengthen our line and kindred, and may they reach the place which Gods inhabit.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Vanaspati shall stand anear and start us, and Agni with his arts prepare oblation. Let the skilled heavenly Immolator forward unto the Gods the offering thrice anointed.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Oil has been mixt: oil is his habitation. In oil he rests: oil is his proper province. Come as thy wont is: O thou Steer, rejoice thee; bear off the oblation duly consecrated.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: FOR you I call the glorious refulgent Agni, the guest of men, rich in oblations Whom all must strive to win even as a lover, God among godly people, Jatavedas.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Bhrgus who served him in the home of waters set him of old in houses of the living. Over all worlds let Agni be the Sovran, the messenger of Gods with rapid coursers.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Among the tribes of men the Gods placed Agni as a dear Friend when they would dwell among them. Against the longing nights may he shine brightly, and show the offerer in the house his vigour.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Sweet is his growth as of one's own possessions; his look when rushing fain to burn is lovely. He darts his tongue forth, like a harnessed courser who shakes his flowing tail, among the bushes.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Since they who honour me have praised my greatness,-he gave, as 'twere, his hue to those who love him. Known is he by his bright delightful splendour, and waxing old renews his youth for ever.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Like one athirst, he lighteth up the forests; like water down the chariot ways he roareth. On his black path he shines in burning beauty, marked as it were the heaven that smiles through vapour.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Around, consuming the broad earth, he wanders, free roaming like an ox without a herdsman,- Agni refulgent, burning up the bushes, with blackened lines, as though the earth he seasoned.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I, in remembrance of thine ancient favour have sung my hymn in this our third assembly. O Agni, give us wealth with store of heroes and mighty strength in food and noble offspring.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May the Grtsamadas, serving in secret, through thee, O Agni, overcome their neighbours, Rich in good heroes and subduing foemen. That vital power give thou to chiefs and singers.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: HERALD and teacher was he born, a guardian for our patrons' help, Earner by rites of noble wealth. That Strong One may we grasp and guide;
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: In whom, Leader of sacrifice, the seven reins, far extended, meet; Who furthers, man-like, eighth in place, as Cleanser, all the work divine.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When swift he follows this behest, bird-like he chants the holy prayers. He holds all knowledge in his grasp even as the felly rounds the wheel.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Together with pure mental power, pure, as Director, was he born. Skilled in his own unchanging laws he waxes like the growing boughs.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Clothing them in his hues, the kine of him the Leader wait on him. Is he not better than the Three, the Sisters who have come to us?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When, laden with the holy oil, the Sister [sic] by the Mother stands, The Priest delights in their approach, as corn at coming of the rain.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: For his support let him perform as ministrant his priestly task; Yea, song of praise and sacrifice: we have bestowed, let us obtain.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary
