verses.translation: That so this man well skilled, may pay worship to all the Holy Ones. And, Agni, this our sacrifice which we have here prepared, to thee.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: AGNI, accept this flaming brand, this waiting with my prayer on thee: Hear graciously these songs of praise.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With this hymn let us honour thee, seeker of horses, Son of Strength, With this fair hymn, thou nobly born.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: As such, lover of song, with songs, wealth-lover, giver of our wealth! With reverence let us worship thee.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Be thou for us a liberal Prince, giver and Lord of precious things. Drive those who hate us far away.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Such as thou art, give rain from heaven, give strength which no man may resist: Give food exceeding plentiful.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To him who lauds thee, craving help, most youthful envoy! through our song, Most holy Herald! come thou nigh.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Between both races, Agni, Sage, well skilled thou passest to and fro, As envoy friendly to mankind.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Befriend us thou as knowing all. Sage, duly worship thou the Gods, And seat thee on this sacred grass.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: VASU, thou most youthful God, Bharata, Agni, bring us wealth, Excellent, splendid, much-desired.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Let no malignity prevail against us, either God's or man's. Save us from this and enmity.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: So through thy favour may we force through all our enemies a way, As 'twere through streaming water-floods.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou, Purifier Agni, high shinest forth, bright, adorable, When worshipped with the sacred oil.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Ours art thou, Agni, Bharata, honoured by us with barren cows, With bullocks and with kine in calf
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Wood-fed, bedewed with sacred oil, ancient, Invoker, excellent, The Son of Strength, the Wonderful.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Now praise, as one who strives for strength, the harnessing of Agni's car, The liberal, the most splendid One;
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Who, guiding worshippers aright, withers, untouched by age, the foe: When worshipped fair to look upon;
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Who for his glory is extolled at eve and morning in our homes, Whose statute is inviolate;
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Who shines refulgent like the Sun, with brilliance and with fiery flame, Decked with imperishable sheen.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Him Atri, Agni, have our songs Strengthened according to his sway: All glories hath he made his own.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May we with Agni's, Indra's help, with Soma's, yea, of all the Gods, Uninjured dwell together still, and conquer those who fight with us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: ACCUSTOMED to the Herald's place, the Herald hath seated him, bright, splendid, passing mighty, Whose foresight keeps the Law from violation, excellent, pure-tongued, bringing thousands, Agni.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Envoy art thou, protector from the foeman, strong God, thou leadest us to higher blessings. Refulgent, be an ever-heedful keeper, Agni, for us and for our seed offspring.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May we adore thee in thy loftiest birthplace, and, with our praises, in thy lower station. The place whence thou issued forth I worship: to thee well kindled have they paid oblations.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Agni, best Priest, pay worship with oblation; quickly commend the gift to be presented; For thou art Lord of gathered wealth and treasure. of the bright song of praise thou art inventor.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The twofold opulence, O Wonder-Worker, of thee new-born each day never decreases. Enrich with food the man who lauds thee, Agni: make him the lord of wealth with noble offspring.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May he, benevolent with this fair aspect, best sacrificer, bring the Gods to bless us. Sure guardian, our protector from the foemen, shine, Agni, with thine affluence and splendour.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: 1.AGNI, first, loudly calling, like a Father, kindled by man upon the seat of worship. Clothed in his glory, deathless, keen of insight, must be adorned by all, the Strong, the Famous.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May Agni the resplendent hear my calling through all my songs, Immortal, keen of insight. Dark steeds or ruddy draw his car, or carried in sundry ways he makes them red of colour.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: On wood supine they got the well-formed Infant: a germ in various-fashioned plants was Agni; And in the night, not compassed round by darkness, he dwells exceeding wise, with rays of splendour.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With oil and sacred gifts I sprinkle Agni who makes his home in front of all things living, Broad, vast, through vital power o'er all expanded, conspicuous, strong with all the food that feeds him.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I pour to him who looks in all directions: may he accept it with a friendly spirit. Agni with bridegroom's grace and lovely colour may not be touched when all his form is fury.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: By choice victorious, recognize thy portion: with thee for envoy may we speak like Manu. Obtaining wealth, I call on perfect Agni who with an eloquent tongue dispenses sweetness.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: HEAR thou my call, O Indra; be not heedless: thine may we be for thee to give us treasures; For these presented viands, seeking riches, increase thy strength like streams of water flowing.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Floods great and many, compassed by the Dragon, thou badest swell and settest free, O Hero. Strengthened by songs of praise thou rentest piecemeal the Dasa, him who deemed himself immortal.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: For, Hero, in the lauds wherein thou joyedst, in hymns of praise, O Indra, songs of Rudras, These streams in which is thy delight approach thee, even as the brilliant ones draw near to Vayu.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: We who add strength to thine own splendid vigour, laying within thine arms the splendid thunder- With us mayst thou, O Indra, waxen splendid, with Surya overcome the Dasa races.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Hero, thou slewest in thy valour Ahi concealed in depths, mysterious, great enchanter, Dwelling enveloped deep within the waters, him who checked heaven and stayed the floods from flowing.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Indra, we laud thy great deeds wrought aforetime, we laud thine exploits later of achievement; We laud the bolt that in thine arms lies eager; we laud thy two Bay Steeds, heralds of Surya.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Indra, thy Bay Steeds showing forth their vigour have sent a loud cry out that droppeth fatness. The earth hath spread herself in all her fulness: the cloud that was about to move hath rested.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Down, never ceasing, hath the rain-cloud settled: bellowing, it hath wandered with the Mothers. Swelling the roar in the far distant limits, they have spread wide the blast sent forth by Indra.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Indra hath hurled down the magician Vrtra who lay beleaguering the mighty river. Then both the heaven and earth trembled in terror at the strong Hero's thunder when he bellowed.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Loud roared the mighty Hero's bolt of thunder, when he, the Friend of man, burnt up the monster, And, having drunk his fill of flowing Soma, baffled the guileful Danava's devices.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Drink thou, O Hero Indra, drink the Soma; let the joy-giving juices make thee joyful. They, filling both thy flanks, shall swell thy vigour. The juice that satisfies hath helped Indra.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Singers have we become with thee, O Indra: may we serve duly and prepare devotion. Seeking thy help we meditate thy praises: may we at once enjoy thy gift of riches.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May we be thine, such by thy help, O Indra, as swell thy vigour while they seek thy favour. Give us, thou God, the riches that we long for, most powerful, with stare of noble children.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Give us a friend, give us an habitation; Indra, give us the company of Maruts, And those whose minds accord with theirs, the Vayus, who drink the first libation of the Soma.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Let those enjoy in whom thou art delighted. Indra, drink Soma for thy strength and gladness. Thou hast exalted us to heaven, Preserver, in battles, through the lofty hymns that praise thee.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Great, verily, are they, O thou Protector, who by their songs of praise have won the blessing. They who strew sacred grass to be thy dwelling, helped by thee have got them strength, O Indra.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Upon the great Trikadruka days, Hero, rejoicing thee, O Indra, drink the Soma. Come with Bay Steeds to drink of libation, shaking the drops from out thy beard, contented.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Hero, assume the might wherewith thou clavest Vrtra piecemeal, the Danava Aurnavabha. Thou hast disclosed the light to light the Arya: on thy left hand, O Indra, sank the Dasyu.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May we gain wealth, subduing with thy succour and with the Arya, all our foes, the Dasyus. Our gain was that to Trta of our party thou gavest up Tvastar's son Visvarupa.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He cast down Arbuda what time his vigour was strengthened by libations poured by Trta. Indra sent forth his whirling wheel like Surya, and aided by the Angirases rent Vala.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Now let that wealthy Cow of thine, O Indra, yield in return a boon to him who lauds thee. Give to thy praisers: let not fortune fail us. Loud may we speak, with brave men, in the assembly.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: HE who, just born, chief God of lofty spirit by power and might became the Gods' protector, Before whose breath through greatness of his valour the two worlds trembled, He, O men, is Indra.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He who fixed fast and firm the earth that staggered, and set at rest the agitated mountains, Who measured out the air's wide middle region and gave the heaven support, He, men, is Indra.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Who slew the Dragon, freed the Seven Rivers, and drove the kine forth from the cave of Vala, Begat the fire between two stones, the spoiler in warriors' battle, He, O men, is Indra.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: By whom this universe was made to tremble, who chased away the humbled brood of demons, Who, like a gambler gathering his winnings seized the foe's riches, He, O men, is Indra.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Of whom, the Terrible, they ask, Where is He? or verily they say of him, He is not. He sweeps away, like birds, the foe's possessions. Have faith in him, for He, O men, is Indra.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Stirrer to action of the poor and lowly, of priest, of suppliant who sings his praises; Who, fair-faced, favours him who presses Soma with stones made ready, He, O men, is Indra.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He under whose supreme control are horses, all chariots, and the villages, and cattle; He who gave being to the Sun and Morning, who leads the waters, He, O men, is Indra.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To whom two armies cry in close encounter, both enemies, the stronger and the weaker; Whom two invoke upon one chariot mounted, each for himself, He, O ye men, is Indra.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Without whose help our people never conquer; whom, battling, they invoke to give them succour; He of whom all this world is but the copy, who shakes things moveless, He, O men, is Indra.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He who hath smitten, ere they knew their danger, with his hurled weapon many grievous sinners; Who pardons not his boldness who provokes him, who slays the Dasyti, He, O men, is Indra.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He who discovered in the fortieth autumn Sambara as he dwelt among the mountains; Who slew the Dragon putting forth his vigour, the demon lying there, He, men, is Indra.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Who with seven guiding reins, the Bull, the Mighty, set free the Seven great Floods to flow at pleasure; Who, thunder-armed, rent Rauhina in pieces when scaling heaven, He, O ye men, is Indra.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Even the Heaven and Earth bow down before him, before his very breath the mountains tremble. Known as the Soma-drinker, armed with thunder, who wields the bolt, He, O ye men, is Indra.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Who aids with favour him who pours the Soma and him who brews it, sacrificer, singer. Whom prayer exalts, and pouring forth of Soma, and this our gift, He, O ye men, Is Indra.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou verily art fierce and true who sendest strength to the man who brews and pours libation. So may we evermore, thy friends, O Indra, speak loudly to the synod with our heroes.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: THE Season was the parent, and when born therefrom it entered rapidly the floods wherein it grows. Thence was it full of sap, streaming with milky juice: the milk of the plant's stalk is chief and meet for lauds.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: They come trooping together bearing milk to him, and bring him sustenance who gives support to all. The way is common for the downward streams to flow. Thou who didst these things first art worthy of our lauds.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: One priest announces what the institutor gives: one, altering the forms, zealously plies his task, The third corrects the imperfections left by each. Thou who didst these things first art worthy of our lauds.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Dealing out food unto their people there they sit, like wealth to him who comes, more than the back can bear. Greedily with his teeth he eats the master's food. Thou who didst these things first art worthy of our lauds.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou hast created earth to look upon the sky: thou, slaying Ahi, settest free the river's paths. Thee, such, a God, the Gods have quickened with their lauds, even as a steed with waters: meet for praise art thou.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou givest increase, thou dealest to us our food: thou milkest from the moist the dry, the rich in sweets. Thou by the worshipper layest thy precious store: thou art sole Lord of all. Meet for our praise art thou.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou who hast spread abroad the streams by stablished law, and in the field the plants that blossom and bear seed; Thou who hast made the matchless lightnings of the sky,-vast, compassing vast realms, meet for our praise art thou.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Who broughtest Narmara with all his wealth, for sake of food, to slay him that the fiends might be destroyed, Broughtest the face unclouded of the strengthening one, performing much even now, worthy art thou of praise.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou boundest up the Dasa's hundred friends and ten, when, at one's hearing, thou belpest thy worshipper. Thou for Dabhiti boundest Dasyus not with cords; Thou wast a mighty help. Worthy of lauds art thou.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: All banks of rivers yielded to his manly might; to him they gave, to him, the Strong, gave up their wealth. The six directions hast thou fixed, a five-fold view: thy victories reached afar. Worthy of lauds art thou.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Meet for high praise, O Hero, is thy power, that with thy single wisdom thou obtainest wealth, The life-support of conquering Jatusthira. Indra, for all thy deeds, worthy of lauds art thou.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou for Turviti heldest still the flowing floods, the river-stream for Vayya easily to pass Didst raise the outcast from the depths, and gavest fame unto the halt and blind. Worthy of lauds art thou.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Prepare thyself to grant us that great bounty, O Vasu, for abundant is thy treasure. Snatch up the wonderful, O Indra, daily. Loud may we speak, with heroes, in assembly.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: MINISTERS, bring the Soma juice for Indra, pour forth the gladdening liquor with the beakers. To drink of this the Hero longeth ever; offer it to the Bull, for this he willeth.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Ye ministers, to him who with the lightning smote, like a tree, the rain-withholding Vṛitra— Bring it to him, him who is fain to taste it, a draught of this which Indra here deserveth.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Ye ministers, to him who smote Dṛibhîka, who drove the kine forth, and discovered Vala, Offer this draught, like Vâta in the region: clothe him with Soma even as steeds with trappings.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Him who did Uraṇa to death, Adhvaryus! though showing arms ninety-and-nine in number; Who cast down headlong Arbuda and slew him,—speed ye that Indra to our offered Soma.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Ye ministers, to him who struck down Svaṣna, and did to death Vyansa and greedy Ṣushṇa, And Rudhikrâs and Namuchi and Pipru,—to him, to Indra, pour ye forth libation.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Ye ministers, to him who, as with thunder, demolished Ṣambara's hundred ancient castles; Who cast down Varchin's sons, a hundred thousand,—to him, to Indra, offer ye the Soma.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Ye ministers, to him who slew a hundred thousand, and cast them down upon earth's bosom; Who quelled the valiant men of Atithigva, Kutsa, and Âyu,—bring to him the Soma.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Ministers, men, whatever thing ye long for obtain ye quickly bringing gifts to Indra. Bring to the Glorious One what hands have cleansèd; to Indra bring, ye pious ones, the Soma.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Do ye, O ministers, obey his order: that, purified in wood, in wood uplift ye. Well pleased he longs for what your hands have tended: offer the gladdening Soma juice to Indra.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: As the cow's udder teems with milk, Adhvaryus, so fill with Soma Indra, liberal giver. I know him: I am sure of this, the Holy knows that I fain would give to him more largely.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Him, ministers, the Lord of heavenly treasure and all terrestrial wealth that earth possesses, Him, Indra, fill with Soma as a garner is filled with barley full: be this your labour.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Prepare thyself to grant us that great booty, O Vasu, for abundant is thy treasure. Gather up wondrous wealth, O Indra, daily. Loud may we speak, with heroes, in assembly.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Now, verily, will I declare the exploits, mighty and true, of him the True and Mighty. In the Trikadrukas he drank the Soma then in its rapture Indra slew the Dragon.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: High heaven unsupported in space he stablished: he filled the two worlds and the air's mid-region. Earth he upheld, and gave it wide expansion. These things did Indra in the Soma's rapture.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: From front, as 'twere a house, he ruled and measured; pierced with his bolt the fountains of the rivers, And made them flow at ease by paths far-reaching, These things did Indra in the Soma's rapture.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Compassing those who bore away Dabhiti, in kindled fire he burnt up all their weapons. And made him rich with kine and cars and horses. These things did Indra in the Soma's rapture.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The mighty roaring flood he stayed from flowing, and carried those who swam not safely over. They having crossed the stream attained to riches. These things did Indra in the Soma's rapture.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With mighty power he made the stream flow upward, crushed with his thunderbolt the car of Usas, Rending her slow steeds with his rapid coursers. These things did Indra in the Soma's rapture.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Knowing the place wherein the maids were hiding, the outcast showed himself and stood before them. The cripple stood erect, the blind beheld them. These things did Indra in the Soma's rapture.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Praised by the Angirases he slaughtered Vala, and burst apart the bulwarks of the mountain. He tore away their deftly-built defences. These things did Indra in the Soma's rapture.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou, with sleep whelming Cumuri and Dhuni, slewest the Dasyu, keptest safe Dabhiti. There the staff-bearer found the golden treasure. These things did Indra in the Soma's rapture.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Now let that wealthy Cow of thine, O Indra , yield in return a boon to him who lauds thee. Give to thy praisers: let not fortune fail us. Loud may we speak, with brave men, in assembly.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To him, your own, the best among the good, I bring eulogy, like oblation in the kindled fire. We invocate for help Indra untouched by eld, who maketh all decay, strengthened, for ever young.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Without whom naught exists, Indra the Lofty One; in whom alone all powers heroic are combined. The Soma is within him, in his frame vast strength, the thunder in his hand and wisdom in his head.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Not by both worlds is thine own power to be surpassed, nor may thy car be stayed by mountains or by seas. None cometh near, O Indra, to thy thunderbolt, when with swift steeds thou fliest over many a league.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: For all men bring their will to him the Resolute, to him the Holy One, to him the Strong they cleave. Pay worship with oblation, strong and passing wise. Drink thou the Soma, Indra, through the mighty blaze.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The vessel of the strong flows forth, the flood of meath, unto the Strong who feeds upon the strong, for drink, Strong are the two Adhvaryus, strong are both the stones. They press the Soma that is strong for him the Strong.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Strong is thy thunderbolt, yea, and thy car is strong; strong are thy Bay Steeds and thy weapons powerful. Thou, Indra, Bull, art Lord of the strong gladdening drink. with the strong Soma, Indra, satisfy thyself.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I, bold by prayer, come near thee in thy sacred rites, thee like a saving ship, thee shouting in the war. Verily he will hear and mark this word of ours: we will pour Indra forth as 'twere a spring of wealth.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Turn thee unto us ere calamity come nigh, as a cow full of pasture turns her to her calf. Lord of a Hundred Powers, may we once firmly cling to thy fair favours even as husbands to their wives.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Now let that wealthy Cow of thine, O Indra, yield in return a boon to him who lauds thee. Give to thy praisers: let not fortune fail us. Loud may we speak, with heroes, in assembly.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: LIKE the Angirases, sing this new song forth to him, for, as in ancient days, his mighty powers are shown, When in the rapture of the Soma he unclosed with strength the solid firm-shut stables of the kine.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Let him be even that God who, for the earliest draught measuring out his power, increased his majesty; Hero who fortified his body in the wars, and through his greatness set the heaven upon his head.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou didst perform thy first great deed of hero might what time thou showedst power, through prayer, before this folk. Hurled down by thee the car-borne Lord of Tawny Steeds, the congregated swift ones fled in sundry ways.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He made himself by might Lord of all living things, and strong in vital power waxed great above them all. He, borne on high, o'erspread with light the heaven and earth, and, sewing up the turbid darkness, closed it in.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He with his might made firm the forward-bending hills, the downward rushing of the waters he ordained. Fast he upheld the earth that nourisheth all life, and stayed the heaven from falling by his wondrous skill.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Fit for the grasping of his arms is what the Sire hath fabricated from all kind of precious wealth. The thunderbolt, wherewith, loud-roaring, he smote down, and striking him to death laid Krivi on the earth.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: As she who in her parents' house is growing old, I pray to thee as Bhaga from the seat of all. Grant knowledge, mete it out and bring it to us here: give us the share wherewith thou makest people glad.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May we invoke thee as a liberal giver thou givest us, O Indra, strength and labours. Help us with manifold assistance, Indra: Migthy One, Indra, make us yet more wealthy.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Now may that wealthy Cow of thine, O Indra, give in return a boon to him who lauds thee. Give to thy praisers: let not fortune fail us. Loud may we speak, with heroes, in assembly.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: THE rich new car hath been equipped at morning; four yokes it hath, three whips, seven reins to guide it: Ten-sided, friendly to mankind, light-winner, that must be urged to speed with prayers and wishes.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: This is prepared for him the first, the second, and the third time: he is man's Priest and Herald. Others get offspring of another parent he goeth, as a noble Bull, with others.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To Indra's car the Bay Steeds have I harnessed, that new well-spoken words may bring him hither. Here let not other worshippers detain thee, for among us are many holy singers.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Indra, come hitherward with two Bay Coursers, come thou with four, with six when invocated. Come thou with eight, with ten, to drink the Soma. Here is the juice, brave Warrior: do not scorn it.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Indra, come thou hither having harnessed thy car with twenty, thirty, forty horses. Come thou with fifty well trained coursers, Indra, sixty or seventy, to drink the Soma.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Come to us hitherward, O Indra, carried by eighty, ninety, or an hundred horses. This Soma juice among the Sunahotras hath been poured out, in love, to glad thee, Indra.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To this my prayer, O Indra, come thou hither: bind to thy car's pole all thy two Bay Coursers. Thou art to be invoked in many places Hero, rejoice thyself in this libation.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Ne'er be my love from Indra disunited still may his liberal Milch-cow yield us treasure. So may we under his supreme protection, safe in his arms, succeed in each forth-going.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Now may that wealthy Cow Of thine, O Indra, give in return a boon to him who lauds thee. Give to thy praisers: let not fortune fail us. Loud may we speak, with heroes, in assembly.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: DRAUGHTS of this sweet juice have been drunk for rapture, of the wise Soma-presser's offered dainty, Wherein, grown mighty in the days aforetime, Indra hath found delight, and men who worship.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Cheered by this meath Indra, whose hand wields thunder, rent piecemeal Ahi who barred up the waters, So that the quickening currents of the rivers flowed forth like birds unto their resting-places.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Indra, this Mighty One, the Dragon's slayer, sent forth the flood of waters to the ocean. He gave the Sun his life, he found the cattle, and with the night the works of days completed.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To him who worshippeth hath Indra given many and matchless gifts. He slayeth Vrtra. Straight was he to be sought with supplications by men who struggled to obtain the sunlight.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To him who poured him gifts he gave up Surya,-Indra, the God, the Mighty, to the mortal; For Etasa with worship brought him riches that keep distress afar, as 'twere his portion.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Once to the driver of his chariot, Kutsa, he gave up greedy Surya, plague of harvest; And Indra, for the sake of Divodasa demolished Sambara's nine-and-ninety castles.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: So have we brought our hymn to thee, O Indra, strengthening thee and fain ourselves for glory. May we with best endeavours gain this friendship, and mayst thou bend the godless scorner's weapons.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thus the Grtsamadas for thee, O Hero, have wrought their hymn and task as seeking favour. May they who worship thee afresh, O Indra, gain food and strength, bliss, and a happy dwelling.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Now may that wealthy Cow of thine, O Indra, give in return a boon to him who lauds thee, Give to thy praisers: let not fortune fail us. Loud may we speak, with heroes, in assembly.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: As one brings forth his car when fain for combat, so bring we power to thee- regard us, Indra- Well skilled in song, thoughtful in spirit, seeking great bliss from one like thee amid the Heroes.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Indra, thou art our own with thy protection, a guardian near to men who love thee truly, Active art thou, the liberal man's defender, his who draws near to thee with right devotion.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May Indra, called with solemn invocations. the young, the Friend, be men's auspicious keeper, One who will further with his aid the singer, the toiler, praiser, dresser of oblations.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With laud and song let me extol that Indra in whom of old men prospered and were mighty. May he, implored, fulfil the prayer for plenty of him who worships, of the living mortal.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He, Indra whom the Angirases' praise delighted, strengthened their prayer and made their goings prosper. Stealing away the mornings with the sunlight, he, lauded, crushed even Asna's ancient powers.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He verily, the God, the glorious Indra, hath raised him up for man, best Wonder-Worker. He, self-reliant, mighty and triumphant, brought low the dear head of the wicked Dasa.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Indra the Vrtra-slayer, Fort-destroyer, scattered the Dasa hosts who dwelt in darkness. For men hath he created earth and waters, and ever helped the prayer of him who worships.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To him in might the Gods have ever yielded, to Indra in the tumult of the battle. When in his arms they laid the bolt, he slaughtered the Dasyus and cast down their forts of iron.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Now may that wealthy Cow of thine, O Indra, give in return a boon to him who lauds thee. Give to thy praisers: let not fortune fail us. Loud may we speak, with heroes, in assembly.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To him the Lord of all, the Lord of wealth, of light; him who is Lord for ever, Lord of men and tilth, Him who is Lord of horses, Lord of kine,of floods, to Indra, to the Holy bring sweet Soma juice.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To him the potent One, who conquers and breaks down, the Victor never vanquished who disposes all, The migbty-voiced, the rider, unassailable, to Indra everconquering speak your reverent prayer.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Still Victor, loved by mortals, ruler over men, o'erthrower, warrior, he hath waxen as he would; Host-gatherer, triumphant, honoured mid the folk. Indra's heroic deeds will I tell forth to all.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The strong who never yields, who slew the furious fiend, the deep, the vast, of wisdom unattainable; Who speeds the good, the breaker-down, the firm, the vast,-Indra whose rites bring joy hath made the light of Dawn.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: By sacrifice the yearning sages sending forth their songs found furtherance from him who speeds the flood. In Indra seeking help with worship and with hymn, they drew him to themselves and won them kine and wealth.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Indra, bestow on us the best of treasures, the spirit of ability and fortune; Increase of riches, safety of our bodies, charm of sweet speech, and days of pleasant weather.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: At the Trikadrukas the Great and Strong hath drunk drink blent with meal. With Visnu hath he quaffed the poured out Soma juice, all that he would. That hath so heightened him the Great, the Wide, to do his mighty work. So may the God attain the God, true Indu Indra who is true.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: So he resplendent in the battle overcame Krivi by might. He with his majesty hath filled the earth and heaven, and waxen strong. One share of the libation hath he swallowed down: one share he left. So may the God attend the God, true Indu Indra who is true.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Brought forth together with wisdom and mighty power thou grewest great; with hero deeds subduing the malevolent, most swift in act; Giving prosperity, and lovely wealth to him who praiseth thee. So may the God attend the God, true Indu Indra who is true.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: This, Indra, was thy hero deed, Dancer, thy first and ancient work, worthy to be told forth in heaven, What time thou sentest down life with a God's own power, freeing the floods. All that is godless may he conquer with his might, and, Lord of Hundred Powers, find for us strength and food.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: WE call thee, Lord and Leader of the heavenly hosts, the wise among the wise, the famousest of all, The King supreme of prayers, O Brahmanaspati: hear us with help; sit down in place of sacrifice.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Brhaspati, God immortal! verily the Gods have gained from thee, the wise, a share in holy rites. As with great light the Sun brings forth the rays of morn, so thou alone art Father of all sacred prayer.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When thou hast chased away revilers and the gloom, thou mountest the refulgent car of sacrifice; The awful car, Brhaspati, that quells the foe, slays demons, cleaves the stall of kine, and finds the light.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou leadest with good guidance and preservest men; distress o'ertakes not him who offers gifts to thee. Him who hates prayer thou punishest, Brhaspati, quelling his wrath: herein is thy great mightiness.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: No sorrow, no distress from any side, no foes, no creatures double-tongued have overcome the man,- Thou drivest all seductive fiends away from him whom, careful guard, thou keepest Brahmanaspati.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou art our keeper, wise, preparer of our paths: we, for thy service, sing to thee with hymns of praise. Brhaspati, whoever lays a snare for us, him may his evil fate, precipitate, destroy.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Him, too, who threatens us without offence of ours, the evil minded, arrogant, rapacious man,- Him turn thou from our path away, Brhaspati: give us fair access to this banquet of the Gods.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thee as protector of our bodies we invoke, thee, saviour, as the comforter who loveth us. Strike, O Brhaspati, the Gods' revilers down, and let not the unrighteous come to highest bliss.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Through thee, kind -prosperer, O Brahmanaspati, may we obtain the wealth of Men which all desire: And all our enemies, who near or far away prevail against us, crush, and leave them destitute.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With thee as our own rich and liberal ally may we, Brhaspati, gain highest power of life. Let not the guileful wicked man be lord of us:-still may we prosper, singing goodly hymns of praise.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Strong, never yielding, hastening to the battle-cry, consumer of the foe, victorious in the strife, Thou art sin's true avenger, Brahmanaspati, who tamest e'en the fierce, the wildly passionate.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Whoso with mind ungodly seeks to do us harm, who, deeming him a man of might mid lords, would slay,- Let not his deadly blow reach us, Brhaspati; may we humiliate the strong ill-doer's wrath.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The mover mid the spoil, the winner of all wealth, to be invoked in fight and reverently adored, Brhaspati hath overthrown like cars of war all wicked enemies who fain would injure us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Burn up the demons with thy fiercest flaming brand, those who have scorned thee in thy manifested might. Show forth that power that shall deserve the hymn of praise: destroy the evil speakers, O Brhaspati.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Brhaspati, that which the foe deserves not which shines among the folk effectual, splendid, That, Son of Law I which is with might refulgent-that treasure wonderful bestow thou on us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Give us not up to those who, foes in ambuscade, are greedy for the wealth of him who sits at ease, Who cherish in their heart abandonment of Gods. Brhaspati, no further rest shall they obtain.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: For Tvastar, he who knows each sacred song, brought thee to life, preeminent o'er all the things that be. Guilt-scourger, guilt-avenger is Brhaspati, who slays the spoiler and upholds the mighty Law.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The mountain, for thy glory, cleft itself apart when, Angiras! thou openedst the stall of kine. Thoul O Brhaspati, with Indra for ally didst hurl down water-floods which gloom had compassed round.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Brahmanaspati, be thou controller of this our hymn and prosper thou our children. All that the Gods regard with love is blessed. Loud may we speak, with heroes, in assembly.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: BE pleased with this our offering, thou who art the Lord; we will adore thee with this new and mighty song. As this thy friend, our liberal patron, praises thee, do thou, Brhaspati, fulfil our hearts' desire.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He who with might bowed down the things that should be bowed, and in his fury rent the holds of Sambara: Who overthrew what shook not, Brahmapaspati,-he made his way within the mountain stored with wealth.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: That was a great deed for the Godliest of the Gods: strong things were loosened and the firmly fixed gave way. He drave the kine forth and cleft Vala through by prayer, dispelled the darkness and displayed the light of heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The well with mouth of stone that poured a flood of meath, which Brahmapaspati hath opened with his might- All they who see the light have drunk their fill thereat: together they have made the watery fount flow forth.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Ancient will be those creatures, whatsoe'er they be; with moons, with autumns, doors unclose themselves to you. Effortless they pass on to perfect this and that, appointed works which Brahmanaspati ordained.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: They who with much endeavour searching round obtained the Panis' noblest treasure hidden in the cave,- Those sages, having marked the falsehoods, turned them back whence they had come, and sought again to enter in.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The pious ones when they had seen the falsehoods turned them back, the sages stood again upon the lofty ways. Cast down with both their arms upon the rock they left the kindled fire, and said, No enemy is he.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With his swift bow, strung truly, Brahmanaspati reaches the mark whate'er it be that he desires. Excellent are the arrows wherewithal he shoots, keen-eyed to look on men and springing from his ear.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He brings together and he parts, the great High Priest; extolled is he, in battle Brahmapaspati. When, gracious, for the hymn he brings forth food and wealth, the glowing Sun untroubled sends forth fervent heat.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: First and preeminent, excelling all besides are the kind gifts of liberal Brhaspati. These are the boons of him the Strong who should be loved, whereby both classes and the people have delight.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou who in every way supreme in earthly power, rejoicing, by thy mighty strength hast waxen great,- He is the God spread forth in breadth against the Gods: he, Brahmanaspati, encompasseth this All.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: From you, twain Maghavans, all truth proceedeth: even the waters break not your commandment. Come to us, Brahmanaspati and Indra, to our oblation like yoked steeds to fodder.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The sacrificial flames most swiftly hear the call: the priest of the assembly gaineth wealth for hymns. Hating the stern, remitting at his will the debt, strong in the shock of fight is Brahmanaspati.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The wrath of Brahmanaspati according to his will had full effect when he would do a mighty deed. The kine he drave forth and distributed to heaven, even as a copious flood with strength flows sundry ways.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Brahmanaspati, may we be evermore masters of wealth well-guided, full of vital strength. Heroes on heroes send abundantly to us, when thou omnipotent through prayer seekest my call.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Brahmanaspati, be thou controller of this our hymn, and prosper thou our children. All that the Gods regard with love is blessed. Loud may we speak, with heroes, in assembly.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: HE lighting up the flame shall conquer enemies: strong shall he be who offers prayer and brings his gift. He with his seed spreads forth beyond another's seed, whomever Brahmanaspati takes for his friend.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With heroes he shall overcome his hero foes, and spread his wealth by kine wise by himself is be. His children and his children's children grow in strength, whomever Brahmanaspati takes for his friend.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He, mighty like a raving river's billowy flood, as a bull conquers oxen, overcomes with strength. Like Agni's blazing rush he may not be restrained, whomever Brahmanaspati takes for his friend.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: For him the floods of heaven flow never failing down: first with the heroes he goes forth to war for kine. He slays in unabated vigour with great might, whomever Brahmanaspati takes for his friend.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: All roaring rivers pour their waters down for him, and many a flawless shelter hath been granted him. Blest with the happiness of Gods he prospers well, whomever Brahmanaspati takes for his friend.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: THE righteous singer shall o'ercome his enemies, and he who serves the Gods subdue the godless man. The zealous man shall vanquish the invincible, the worshipper share the food of him who worships not.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Worship, thou hero, chase the arrogant afar: put on auspicious courage for the fight with foes. Prepare oblation so that thou mayst have success. we crave the favouring help of Brahmanaspati.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He with his folk, his house, his family, his sons, gains booty for himself, and, with the heroes, wealth,believing Who with oblation and a true heart serves Brahmanaspati the Father of the Gods.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Whoso hath honoured him with offerings rich in oil, him Brahmanaspati leads forward on his way, Saves him from sorrow, frees him from his enemy, and is his wonderful deliverer from woe.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: THESE hymns that drop down fatness, with the ladle I ever offer to the Kings Adityas. May Mitra, Aryaman, and Bhaga hear us, the mighty Varuna Daksa, and Amsa.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With one accord may Aryaman and Mitra and Varuna this day accept this praise-song- Adityas bright and pure as streams of water, free from all guile and falsehood, blameless, perfect.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: These Gods, Adityas, vast, profound, and faithful, with many eyes, fain to deceive the wicked, Looking within behold the good and evil near to the Kings is even the thing most distant.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Upholding that which moves and that which moves not, Adityas, Gods, protectors of all being, Provident, guarding well the world of spirits, true to eternal Law, the debt-exactors.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May I, Adityas, share me this your favour which, Aryaman, brings profit e'en in danger. Under your guidance, Varuna and Mitra, round troubles may I pass, like rugged places.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Smooth is your path, O Aryaman and Mitra; excellent is it, Varuna, and thornless. Thereon, Adityas, send us down your blessing: grant us a shelter hard to be demolished.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Mother of Kings, may Aditi transport us, by fair paths Aryaman, beyond all hatred. May we uninjured, girt by many heroes, win Varuna's and Mitra's high protection.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With their support they stay three earths, three heavens; three are their functions in the Gods' assembly. Mighty through Law, Adityas, is your greatness; fair is it, Aryaman, Varuna, and Mitra.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Golden and splendid, pure like streams of water, they hold aloft the three bright heavenly regions. Ne'er do they slumber, never close their eyelids, faithful, far-ruling for the righteous mortal.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou over all, O Varuna, art Sovran, be they Gods, Asura! or be they mortals. Grant unto us to see a hundred autumns ours be the blest long lives of our forefathers.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Neither the right nor left do I distinguish, neither the east nor yet the west, Adityas. Simple and guided by your wisdom, Vasus! may I attain the light that brings no danger.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He who bears gifts unto the Kings, true Leaders, he whom their everlasting blessings prosper, Moves with his chariot first in rank and wealthy, munificent and lauded in assemblies.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Pure, faithful, very strong, with heroes round him, he dwells beside the waters rich with pasture. None slays, from near at hand or from a distance, him who is under the Adityas' guidance.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Aditi, Mitra, Varuna, forgive us however we have erred and sinned against you. May I obtain the broad light free from peril: O Indra, let not during darkness seize us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: For him the Twain united pour their fulness, the rain from heaven: he thrives most highly favoured. He goes to war mastering both the mansions: to him both portions of the world are gracious.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Your guiles, ye Holy Ones, to quell oppressors, your snares spread out against the foe, Adityas, May I car-borne pass like a skillful horseman: uninjured may we dwell in spacious shelter.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May not live, O Varuna, to witness my wealthy, liberal, dear friend's destitution. King, may never lack well-ordered riches. Loud may we speak, with heroes, in assembly.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: THIS laud of the self-radiant wise Aditya shall be supreme o'er all that is in greatness. Beg renown of Varuna the Mighty, the God exceeding kind to him who worships. 2, Having extolled thee. Varuna, with thoughtful care may we have high fortune in thy service, Sniffing thy praises like the fires at coming, day after day, of mornings rich in cattle.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May we be in thy keeping, O thou Leader wide-ruling Varuna, Lord of many heroes. O sons of Aditi, for ever faithful, pardon us, Gods, admit us to your friendship.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He made them flow, the Aditya, the Sustainer: the rivers run by Varuna's commandment. These feel no weariness, nor cease from flowing: swift have they flown like birds in air around us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Loose me from sin as from a bond that binds me: may we swell, Varuna, thy spring of Order. Let not my thread, while I weave song, be severed, nor my work's sum, before the time, be shattered.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Far from me, Varuna, remove all danger accept me graciously, thou Holy Sovran. Cast off, like cords that hold a calf, my troubles: I am not even mine eyelid's lord without thee.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Strike us not, Varuna, with those dread weapons which, Asura, at thy bidding wound the sinner. Let us not pass away from light to exile. Scatter, that we may live, the men who hate us
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O mighty Varuna, now and hereafter, even as of old, will we speak forth our worship. For in thyself, invincible God, thy statutes never to be moved are fixed as on a mountain.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Move far from me what sins I have committed: let me not suffer, King, for guilt of others. Full many a morn remains to dawn upon us: in these, O Varuna, while we live direct us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O King, whoever, be he friend or kinsman, hath threatened me affrighted in my slumber- If any wolf or robber fain would harm us, therefrom, O Varuna, give thou us protection.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May I not live O Varuna, to witness my wealthy, liberal dear friend's destitution. King, may I never lack well-ordered riches. Loud may we speak, with heroes, in assembly.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: UPHOLDERS of the Law, ye strong Adityas, remove my sin like her who bears in secret. You, Varuna, Mitra and all Gods who listen, I call to help me, I who know your goodness.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Ye, Gods, are providence and ye are power: remove ye utterly all those who hate us. As givers of good things deal with us kindly: this day be gracious to us and hereafter.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: What service may we do you with our future, what service, Vasus, with our ancient friendship? O Aditi, and VaruVa and Mitra, Indra and Maruts, make us well and happy.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Ye, O ye Gods, are verily our kinsmen as such be kind to me who now implore you. Let not your car come slowly to our worship: of kinsmen such as you ne'er let us weary.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I singly have sinned many a sin against you, and ye chastised me as a sire the gambler. Far be your nets, far, Gods, be mine offences: seize me not like a bird upon her offspring.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Turn yourselves hitherward this day, ye Holy, that fearing in my heart I may approach you. Protect us, God; let not the wolf destroy us. Save us, ye Holy, from the pit and falling.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May I not live, O Varuna, to witness my wealthy, liberal, dear friend's destitution. King, may I never lack well-ordered riches. Loud may we speak, with heroes, in assembly.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: THE streams unceasing flow to Indra, slayer of Ahi, Savitar, God, Law's fulfiller, Day after day goes on the sheen of waters. What time hath past since they were first set flowing?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: His Mother-for she knew-spake and proclaimed him who was about to cast his bolt at Vrtra. Cutting their paths according to his pleasure day after day flow to their goal the rivers.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Aloft he stood above the airy region, and against Vrtra shot his deadly missile. Enveloped in a cloud he rushed upon him. Indra subdued the foe with sharpened weapons.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: As with a bolt, Brhaspati, fiercely flaming, pierce thou Vrkadvaras', the Asura's, heroes. Even as in time of old with might thou slewest, so slay even now our enemy, O Indra.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Cast down from heaven on high thy bolt of thunder wherewith in joy thou smitest dead the foeman. For gain of children make us thine, O Indra, of many children's children and of cattle.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Whomso ye love, his power ye aid and strengthen; ye Twain are the rich worshipper's advancers. Graciously favour us, Indra and Soma; give us firm standing in this time of danger.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Let it not vex me, tire me, make me slothful, and never let us say, Press not the Soma; For him who cares for me, gives gifts, supports me, who comes with kine to me who pour libations.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Sarasvati, protect us: with the Maruts allied thou boldly conquerest our foemen, While Indra does to death the daring chieftain of Sandikas exulting in his prowess.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Him who waylays, yea, him who would destroy us,-aim at him, pierce him with thy sharpened weapon. Brhaspati, with arms thou slayest foemen O King, give up the spoiler to destruction.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Perform, O Hero, with our valiant heroes the deeds heroic which thou hast to finish. Long have they been inflated with presumption: slay them, and bring us hither their possessions.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I craving joy address with hymn and homage your heavenly host, the company of Maruts, That we may gain wealth with full store of heroes, each day more famous, and with troops of children.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: HELP, Varuna and Mitra, O ye Twain allied with Vasus, Rudras, and Adityas, help our car, That, as the wild birds of the forest from their home, our horses may fly forth, glad, eager for renown.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Yea, now ye Gods of one accord speed on our car what time among the folk it seeks an act of might; When, hasting through the region with the stamp of hoofs, our swift steeds trample on the ridges of the earth.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Or may our Indra here, the Friend of all mankind, coming from heaven, most wise, girt by the Marut host, Accompany, with aid untroubled by a foe, our car to mighty gain, to win the meed of strength.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Or may this Tvastar, God who rules the world with power, one-minded with the Goddesses speed forth our car; Ila and Bhaga the celestial, Earth and Heaven, Pusan, Purandhi, and the Asvins, ruling Lords.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Or, seen alternate, those two blessed Goddesses, Morning and Night who stir all living things to act: While with my newest song I praise you both, O Earth, that from what moves not ye may spread forth threefold food.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Your blessing as a boon for suppliants we desire: the Dragon of the Deep, and Aja-Ekapad, Trita, Rbhuksan, Savitar shall joy in us, and the Floods' swift Child in our worship and our prayer.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: These earnest prayers I pray to you, ye Holy: to pay you honour, living men have formed them, Men fain to win the prize and glory. May they win, as a car-horse might the goal, your notice.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: GRACIOUSLY further, O ye Heaven and Earth, this speech striving to win reward, of me your worshipper. First rank I give to you, Immortal, high extolled! I, fain to win me wealth, to you the migbty Pair.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Let not man's guile annoy us, secret or by day: give not us up a prey to these calamities. Sever not thou our friendship: think thereon for us. This, with a heart that longs for bliss, we seek from thee.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Bring hither with benignant mind the willing Cow teeming with plenteous milk, full, inexhaustible. O thou invoked by many, day by day I urge thee with my word, a charger rapid in his tread.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With eulogy I call on Raka swift to hear may she, auspicious, hear us, and herself observe. With never-breaking needle may she sew her work, and give a hero son most wealthy, meet for praise.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: All thy kind thoughts, O Raka, lovely in their form, wherewith thou grantest wealth to him who offers gifts- With these come thou to us this day benevolent, O Blessed One, bestowing food of thousand sorts.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O broad-tressed Sinivali, thou who art the Sister of the Gods, Accept the offered sacrifice, and, Goddess, grant us progeny.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With lovely fingers, lovely arms, prolific Mother of many sons- Present the sacred gifts to her, to Sinivali Queen of men.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Her, Sinivali, her, Gungu, her, Raka, her, Sarasvati, Indrani to mine aid I call, and Varunani for my weal.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: FATHER of Maruts, let thy bliss approach us: exclude us not from looking on the sunlight. Gracious to our fleet courser be the Hero may we transplant us, Rudra, in our children.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With the most saving medicines which thou givest, Rudra, may I attain a hundred winters. Far from us banish enmity and hatred, and to all quarters maladies and trouble.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Chief of all born art thou in glory, Rudra, armed with the thunder, mightiest of the mighty. Transport us over trouble to well-being repel thou from us all assaults of mischief.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Let us not anger thee with worship, Rudra, ill praise, Strong God! or mingled invocation. Do thou with strengthening balms incite our heroes: I hear thee famed as best of all physicians.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May I with praise-songs win that Rudra's favour who is adored with gifts and invocations. Ne'er may the tawny God, fair-checked, and gracious, swift hearing, yield us to this evil purpose.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Strong, begirt by Maruts, hath refreshed me, with most invigorating food, imploring. As he who finds a shade in fervent sunlight may I, uninjured, win the bliss of Rudra.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Where is that gracious hand of thine, O Rudra, the hand that giveth health and bringeth comfort, Remover of the woe that Gods have sent us? O Strong One, look thou on me with compassion.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To him the strong, great, tawny, fair-complexioned, I utter forth a mighty hymn of praises. We serve the brilliant God with adorations, we glorify, the splendid name of Rudra.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With firm limbs, multiform, the strong, the tawny adorns himself with bright gold decorations: The strength of Godhead ne'er departs from Rudra, him who is Sovran of this world, the mighty.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Worthy, thou carriest thy bow and arrows, worthy, thy manyhued and honoured necklace. Worthy, thou cuttest here each fiend to pieces: a mightier than thou there is not, Rudra.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Praise him the chariot-borne, the young, the famous, fierce, slaying like a dread beast of the forest. O Rudra, praised, be gracious to the singer. let thy hosts spare us and smite down another.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I bend to thee as thou approachest, Rudra, even as a boy before the sire who greets him. I praise thee Bounteous Giver, Lord of heroes: give medicines to us as thou art lauded.
