verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Of your pure medicines, O potent Martits, those that are wholesomest and health bestowing, Those which our father Manu hath selected, I crave from. Rudra for our gain and welfare.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May Rudra's missile turn aside and spare us, the great wrath of the impetuous One avoid us. Turn, Bounteous God, thy strong bow from our princes, and be thou gracious to our seed and offspring.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O tawny Bull, thus showing forth thy nature, as neither to be wroth, O God, nor slay us. Here, Rudra, listen to our invocation. Loud may we speak, with heroes, in assembly.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: THE Maruts of resistless might who love the rain, resplendent, terrible like wild beasts in their strength, Glowing like flames of fire, impetuous in career, blowing the wandering raincloud, have disclosed the kine.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: They gleam with armlets as the heavens are decked with stars, like cloud-born lightnings shine the torrents of their rain. Since the strong Rudra, O Maruts with brilliant chests, sprang into life for you in Prsni's radiant lap.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: They drip like horses in the racings of swift steeds; with the stream's rapid cars they hasten on their way. Maruts with helms of gold, ye who make all things shake, come with your spotted deer, one-minded, to our food.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: They have bestowed of Mitra all that live, to feed, they who for evermore cause their swift drops to flow; Whose steeds are spotted deer, whose riches never fail, like horses in full speed, bound to the pole in work.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With brightly-flaming kine whose udders swell with milk, with glittering lances on your unobstructed paths, O Maruts, of one mind, like swans who seek their nests, come to the rapturous enjoyment of the meath.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To these our prayers, O Maruts, come unanimous, come ye to our libations like the praise of men. Make it swell like a mare, in udder like a cow, and for the singer grace the song with plenteous strength.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Give us a steed, O Maruts mighty in the car; prevailing prayer that brings remembrance day by day; Food to your praisers, to your bard in deeds of might give winning wisdom, power uninjured, unsurpassed.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When the bright-chested Maruts, lavish of their gifts, bind at the time bliss their horses to the cars, Then, as the milch-cow feeds her calf within the stalls, they pour forth food for all oblation-bringing men.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Save us, O Maruts, Vasus, from the injurer, the mortal foe who makes us looked upon as wolves. With chariot all aflame compass him round about: O Rudras, cast away the foeman's deadly bolt.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Well-known, ye Maruts, is that wondrous course of yours, when they milked Prsni's udder, close akin to her. Or when to shame the bard who lauded, Rudra's Sons, ye O infallible brought Trita to decay.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: We call you such, great Maruts, following wonted ways, to the oblation paid to Visnu Speeder-on. With ladles lifted up, with prayer, we seek of them preeminent, golden-hued, the wealth which all extol.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: They, the Dasagvas, first of all brought sacrifice: they at the break of mornings shall inspirit us. Dawn with her purple beams uncovereth the nights, with great light glowing like a billowy sea of milk.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Rudras have rejoiced there in the gathered bands at seats of worship as in purple ornaments. They with impetuous vigour sending down the rain have taken to themselves a bright and lovely hue.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Soliciting their high protection for our help, with this our adoration we sing praise to them, Whom, for assistance, like the five terrestrial priests. Trita hath brought to aid us hither on his car.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: So may your favouring help be turned to us-ward, your kindness like a lowing cow approach us, Wherewith ye bear your servant over trouble, and free your worshipper from scoff and scorning.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: EAGER for spoil my flow of speech I utter: may the Floods' Child accept my songs with favour. Will not the rapid Son of Waters make them lovely, for he it is who shall enjoy them?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To him let us address the song well-fashioned, forth from the heart. Shall he not understand it' The friendly Son of Waters by the greatness of Godhead hath produced all things existing.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Some floods unite themselves and others join them: die sounding rivers fill one common storehouse. On every side the bright Floods have encompassed the bright resplendent Offspring of the Waters.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The never-sullen waters, youthful Maidens, carefully decking, wait on him the youthful. He with bright rays shines forth in splendid beauty, unfed with wood. in waters, oil-enveloped.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To him three Dames are offering food to feed him, Goddesses to the God whom none may injure. Within the waters hath he pressed, as hollows, and drinks their milk who now are first made mothers.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Here was the horse's birth; his was the sunlight. Save thou our princes from the oppressor's onslaught. Him, indestructible, dwelling at a distance in forts unwrought lies and ill spirits reach not.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He, in whose mansion is the teeming Milch-cow, swells the Gods' nectar and cats noble viands. He Son of Waters, gathering strength in waters, shines for his worshipper to give him treasures.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He who in waters with his own pure Godhead shines widely, law-abiding, everlasting- The other worlds are verily his branches, and plants are born of him with all their offspring.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Waters' Son hath risen, and clothed in lightning ascended up unto the curled cloud's bosom; And bearing with them his supremest glory the Youthful Ones, gold-coloured, move around him.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Golden in form is he, like gold to look on, his colour is like gold, the Son of Waters. When he is seated fresh from golden birthplace those who present their gold give food to feed him.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: This the fair name and this the lovely aspect of him the Waters' Son increase in secret. Whom here the youthful Maids together kindle, his food is sacred oil of golden colour.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Him, nearest Friend of many, will we worship with sacrifice. and reverence and oblation. I make his back to shine, with chips provide him; to offer food and with my songs exalt him.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Bull hath laid his own life-germ Within them. He sucks them as an infant, and they kiss him. He, Son of Waters, of unfading colour, had entered here as in another's body.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: While here he dwelleth in sublimest station, resplendent with the rays that never perish, The Waters, bearing oil to feed their offspring, flow, Youthful Ones, in wanderings about him.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Agni, I gave good shelter to the people, and to the princes goodly preparation. Blessed is all that Gods regard with favour. Loud may we speak, with heroes, in assembly.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: WATER and milk hath he endued, sent forth to thee: the men have drained him with the filters and the stones. Drink, Indra, from the Hotar's bowl first right is thine-Soma hallowed and poured with Vasat and Svaha.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Busied with sacrifice, with spotted deer and spears, gleaming upon your way with ornaments, yea, our Friends, Sitting on sacred grass, ye Sons of Bharata, drink Soma from the Potar's bowl, O Men of heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Come unto us, ye swift to listen: as at home upon the sacred grass sit and enjoy yourselves. And, Tvastar, well-content be joyful in the juice with Gods and Goddesses in gladsome company.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Bring the Gods hither, Sage, and offer sacrifice: at the three altars seat thee willingly, O Priest. Accept for thy delight the proffered Soma meath: drink from the Kindler's bowl and fill thee with thy share.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: This is the strengthener of thy body's manly might: strength, victory for all time are placed within thine arms. Pressed for thee, Maghavan, it is offered unto thee: drink from the chalice of this Brahman, drink thy fill.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Accept the sacrifice; mark both of you, my call: the Priest hath seated him after the ancient texts. My prayer that bids them come goes forth to both the Kings: drink ye the Soma meath from the Director's bowl.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Enjoy thy fill of meath out of the Hotar's cup: Adhvaryus he desires a full draught poured for him. Bring it him: seeking this he gives. Granter of Wealth, drink Soma with the Rtus from the Hotar's cup.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He whom of old I called on, him I call on now. He is to be invoked; his name is He who Gives, Here brought by priests is Soma meath. Granter of Wealth, drink Soma with the Rtus from the Potar's cup.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Fat may the horses be wherewith thou speedest on: Lord of the Wood, unharming, strengthen thou thyself. Drawing and seizing, Bold One, thou who grantest wealth, drink Soma with the Rtus from the Nestar's cup.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: From Hotar's cup and Potar's he hath drunk and joyed: the proffered food hath pleased him from the Nestar's bowl. The fourth cup undisturbed, immortal, let him drink who giveth wealth, the cup of the wealth-giving God.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Yoke, O ye Twain, to-day your hero-bearing car, swift-moving hitherward: your loosing-place is here. Mix the oblations, then come hither with the meath, and drink the Soma, ye rich in abundant strength.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Agni, accept the fuel and our offered gift: accept the prayer of man, accept our eulogy, Do thou with all, with Rtu, O thou Excellent, fain, make the great Gods all fain taste the gift we bring.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: UPRISEN is Savitar, this God, to quicken, Priest who neglects not this most constant duty. To the Gods, verily, he gives rich treasure, and blesses him who calls them to the banquet.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Having gone up on high, the God broadhanded spreads his arms widely forth that all may mark him. Even the waters bend them to his service: even this wind rests in the circling region.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Though borne by swift steeds he will yet unyoke them: e'en the fleet chariot hath he stayed from going. He hath checked e'en their haste who glide like serpents. Night closely followed Savitar's dominion.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: What was spread out she weaves afresh, re-weaving: the skillful leaves his labour half-completed. He hath arisen from rest, and parted seasons: Savitar hath approached, God, holy-minded.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Through various dwellings, through entire existence, spreads, manifest, the household light of Agni. The Mother gives her Son the goodliest portion, and Savitar hath sped to meet his summons.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He comes again, unfolded, fain for conquest: at home was he, the love of all things moving. Each man hath come leaving his evil doings, after the Godlike Savitar's commandment.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The wild beasts spread through desert places seeking their watery share which thou hast set in waters. The woods are given to the birds. These statutes of the God Savitar none disobeyeth.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With utmost speed, in restless haste at sunset Varuna seeks his watery habitation. Then seeks each bird his nest, each beast his lodging. In due place Savitar hath set each creature.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Him whose high law not Varuna nor Indra, not Mitra, Aryaman, nor Rudra breaketh, Nor evil-hearted fiends, here for my welfare him I invoke, God Savitar, with worship.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May they who strengthen bliss, and thought and wisdom, and the Dames' Lord and Narasamsa aid us. That good may come to us and wealth be gathered, may we be Savitar the God's beloved.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: So come to us our hearts' desire, the bounty bestowed by thee, from heaven and earth and waters, That it be well with friends and those who praise thee, and, Savitar, with the loud-lauding singer.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: SING like the two press-stones for this same purpose; come like two misers to the tree of treasure; Like two laud-singing Brahmans in the assembly, like the folk's envoys called in many places.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Moving at morning like two chr-borne heroes, like to a pair of goats ye come electing; Like two fair dames embellishing their bodies, like a wise married pair among the people.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Like to a pair of horns come first to usward, like to a pair of hoofs with rapid motion; Come like two Cakavas in the grey of morning, come like two chariot wheels at dawn, ye Mighty.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Bear us across the rivers like two vessels, save us as ye were yokes, naves, spokes and fellies. Be like two dogs that injure not our bodies; preserve us, like two crutches, that we fall not.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Like two winds ageing not, two confluent rivers, come with quick vision like two eyes before us. Come like two hands most helpful to the body, and guide us like two feet to what is precious.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Even as two lips that with the mouth speak honey, even as two breasts that nourish our existence, Like the two nostrils that protect our being, be to us as our ears that hear distinctly.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Like two hands give ye us increasing vigour; like heaven and earth constrain the airy regions. Asvins, these hymns that struggle to approach you, sharpen ye like an axe upon a whetstone.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: These prayers of ours exalting you, O Asvins, have the GrtSamadas, for a laud, made ready. Welcome them, O ye Heroes, and come bither. Loud may we speak. with brave men, in assembly.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: SOMA and Pusan, Parents of all riches, Parents of earth and Parents of high heaven, You Twain, brought forth as the whole world's protectors, the Gods have made centre of life eternal.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: At birth of these two Gods all Gods are joyful: they have caused darkness, which we hate, to vanish. With these, with Soma and with Pusan, India generates ripe warm milk in the raw milch-cows.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Soma and Pusan, urge your chariot hither, the seven-wheeled car that measures out the region, That stirs not all, that moves to every quarter, five-reined and harnessed by the thought, ye Mighty.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: One in the heaven on high hath made his dwelling, on earth and in the firmament the other. May they disclose to us great store of treasure, much-longed for, rich in food, source of enjoyment.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: One of you Twain is Parent of all creatures, the other journeys onward all-beholding. Soma and Pusan, aid my thought with favour: with you may we o'ercome in all encounters.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May Pusan stir our thought, the all-impelling, may Soma Lord of riches grant us riches. May Aditi the perfect Goddess aid us. Loud may we speak, with heroes, in assembly.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O VAYU, come to us with all the thousand chariots that are thine, Team-borne, to drink the Soma juice.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Drawn by thy team, O Vayu, come; to thee is offered this, the pure. Thou visitest the presser's house.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Indra and Vayu, drawn by teams, ye Heroes, come today and drink. Of the bright juice when blent with milk.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: This Soma hath been shed for you, Lawstrengtheners, Mitra-Varuna! Listen ye here to this my call.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Both Kings who never injure aught seat them in their supremest home, The thousand-pillared, firmly-based.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Fed with oblation, Sovran Kings, Adityas, Lords of liberal gifts. They wait on him whose life is true.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With kine, Nasatyas, and with steeds, come, Asvins, Rudras, to the house That will protect its heroes well;
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Such, wealthy Gods! as none afar nor standing nigh to us may harm, Yea, no malicious mortal foe.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: As such, O longed-far Asvins, lead us on to wealth of varied sort, Wealth that shall bring us room and rest.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Verily Indra, conquering all, driveth e'en mighty fear away, For firm is he and swift to act.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Indra be gracious unto us: sin shall not reach us afterward, And good shall be before us still.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: From all the regions of the world let Indra send security, The foe-subduer, swift to act.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O all ye Gods, come hitherward: hear this mine invocation, seat Yourselves upon this sacred grass.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Among the gunahotras strong for you is this sweet gladdening draught. Drink ye of this delightsome juice.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Ye Martus led by Indra, Gods with Pusan for your bounteousest, Hear all of you this call of mine.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Best Mother, best of Rivers, best of Goddesses, Sarasvati, We are, as 'twere, of no repute and dear Mother, give thou us renown.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: In thee, Sarasvati, divine, all generations have their stay. Be, glad with Sunahotra's sons: O Goddess grant us progeny.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Enriched with sacrifice, accept Sarasvati, these prayers of ours, Thoughts which GrtSamadas beloved of Gods bring, Holy One to thee.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Ye who bless sacrifice, go forth, for verily we choose you both, And Agni who conveys our gifts.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: This our effectual sacrifice, reaching the sky, shall Heaven and Earth Present unto the Gods to-day.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: In both your laps, ye guileless Ones, the Holy Gods shall sit them down To-day to drink the Soma here.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: TELLING his race aloud with cries repeated, he sends his voice out as his boat a steersman. O Bird, be ominous of happy fortune from no side may calamity befall thee.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Let not the falcon kill thee, nor the eagle let not the arrow-bearing archer reach thee. Still crying in the region of the Fathers, speak here auspicious, bearing joyful tidings.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Bringing good tidings, Bird of happy omen, call thou out loudly southward of our dwellings, So that no thief, no sinner may oppress us. Loud may we speak, with heroes, in assembly.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: HERE on the right sing forth chanters of hymns of praise, even the winged birds that in due season speak. He, like: a Sama-chanter utters both the notes, skilled in the mode of Trstup and of Gayatri.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou like the chanter-priest chantest the Sama, Bird; thou singest at libations like a Brahman's son. Even as a vigorous horse when he comes near the mare, announce to us good fortune, Bird, on every side, proclaim in all directions happy luck, O Bird.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When singing here, O Bird. announce good luck to us, and when thou sittest still think on us with kind thoughts.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: THOU, Agni, who wilt have the strong, hast made me the Soma's priest, to worship in assembly. Thou shinest to the Gods, I set the press stones. I toil; be joyful in thyself, O Agni.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: East have we turned the rite; may the hymn aid it. With wood and worship shall they honour Agni. From heaven the synods of the wise have learnt it: c'en for the quick and strong they seek advancement.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Prudent, he whose will is pure, brought welfare, allied by birth to Heaven and Earth in kinship. The Gods discovered in the midst of waters beautiful Agni with the Sisters' labour.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Him, Blessed One, the Seven strong Floods augmented, him white at birth and red when waxen mighty. As mother mares run to their new-born you ling, so at his birth the Gods wondered at Agni.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Spreading with radiant limbs throughout the region, purging his power with wise purifications, Robing himself in light, the life of waters, lie spreads abroad his high and perfect glories.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He sought heaven's Mighty Ones, the unconsuming, the unimpaired, not clothed and yet not naked. Then they, ancient and young, who dwell together, Seven sounding Rivers, as one germ received him.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: His piles, assuming every form, are scattered where flow sweet waters, at the spring of fatness; There stood the milch-kine with full-laden udders, and both paired Mighty Mothers of the Wondrous.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Carefully cherished, Son of Strength, thou showest assuming lasting and refulgent beauties. Full streams of fatness and sweet juice descended, there where the Mighty One grew strong by wisdom.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: From birth he knew even his Father's bosom, he set his voices and his streams in motion; Knew him who moved with blessed Friends in secret, with the young Dames of heaven. He stayed not hidden.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He nursed the Infant of the Sire and Maker: alone the Babe sucked many a teeming bosom. Guard, for the Bright and Strong, the fellow-spouses friendly to men and bound to him in kinship.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Mighty One increased in space unbounded; full many a glorious flood gave strength to Agni. Friend of the house, within the lap of Order lay Agni, in the Sister Rivers' service.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: As keen supporter where great waters gather, light-shedder whom the brood rejoice to look on; He who begat, and will beget, the dawnlights, most manly, Child of Floods, is youthful Agni.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Him, varied in his form, the lovely Infant of floods and plants the blessed wood hath gendered. Gods even, moved in spirit, came around him, and served him at his birth, the Strong, the Wondrous.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Like brilliant lightnings, mighty luminaries accompany the light-diffusing Agni, Waxen, as 'twere in secret, in his dwelling, while in the boundless stall they milk out Amrta.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I sacrificing serve thee with oblations and crave with longing thy good-will and friendship. Grant, with the Gods, thy grace to him who lauds thee, protect us with thy rays that guard the homestead.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May we, O Agni, thou who leadest wisely, thy followers and masters of all treasures, Strong in the glory of our noble offspring, subdue the godless when they seek the battle.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Ensign of Gods hast thou become, O Agni, joy-giver, knower of all secret wisdom. Friend of the homestead, thou hast lightened mortals: car borne thou goest to the Gods, fulfilling.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Within the house hath sate the King immortal of mortals, filling full their sacred synods. Bedewed with holy oil he shineth widely, Agni, the knower of all secret wisdom.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Come unto us with thine auspicious friendship, come speeding, Mighty, with thy mighty succours. Grant us abundant wealth that saves from danger, that brings a good repute, a glorious portion.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To thee who art of old these songs, O Agni, have I declared, the ancient and the later. These great libations to the Strong are offiered: in every birth is Jatavedas stablished.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Stablished in every birth is Jatavedas, kindled perpetual by the Visvamitras. May we rest ever in the loving-kindness, in the auspicious grace of him the Holy.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: This sacrifice of ours do thou, O Mighty, O truly Wise, bear to the Gods rejoicing. Grant us abundant food, thou priestly Herald, vouchsafe to give us ample wealth, O Agni.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: As holy food, Agni, to thine invoker give wealth in cattle, lasting, rich in marvels. To us he born a son, and spreading offspring. Agni, be this thy gracious will to us-ward.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To him, Vaisvanara, who strengthens Holy Law, to Agni we present our praise like oil made pure. With thoughtful insight human priests bring him anear, our Herald from of old, as an axe forms a car.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He made the heaven and earth resplendent by his birth: Child of two Mothers he was meet to be implored, Agni, oblation-bearer, gracious, ever-young, infallible, rich in radiant light, the guest of men.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Within the range of their surpassing power, by might, the Gods created Agni with inventive thought. I, eager to win strength, address him, like a steed, resplendent with his brilliance, with his ample light.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Eager to gain, we crave from him the friendly God strength confident, choice worthy meet to be extolled: The Bhrgus' bounty, willing, strong with sages' lore, even Agni shining forth with light that comes from heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: For happiness, men, having trimmed the sacred grass, set Agni glorious for his strength before them here; Yea, with raised ladles, him bright, dear to all the Gods, perfecting aims of works, Rudra of solemn rites.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Around thy dwelling-place, O brightly-shining Priest, are men at sacrifice, whose sacred grass is trimmed. Wishing to do thee service, Agni, they are there, desirous of thy friendship grant them store of wealth.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He hath filled heaven and earth and the great realm of light, when at his birth the skillful held him in their hold. He like a horse is led forth to the sacrifice Sage, graciously inclined, that he may win us strength.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Honour the oblation-bearer, him who knows fair rites, serve ye the Household Friend who knows all things that be. He drives the chariot of the lofty ordinance: Agni most active, is the great High Priest of Gods.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: They who are free from death, fain for him, purified three splendours of the mighty Agni, circling all. To man, for his enjoyment, one of these they gave: the other two have passed into the sister sphere.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Man's sacrificial food hath sharpened like an axe, for brightness, him the Sage of men, the people's Lord, Busied with sacred rites he mounts and he descends. He hath laid down his vital germ within these worlds.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He stirs with life in wombs dissimilar in kind, born as a Lion or a loudly-bellowing Bull: Vaisvanara immortal with wide-reaching might, bestowing goods and wealth on him who offers gifts.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Vaisvanara, as of old, mounted the cope of heaven, heaven's ridge, well greeted, by those skilled in noble songs. He, as of old, producing riches for the folk, still watchful, traverses the common way again.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: For new prosperity we seek to Agni, him whose course is splendid, gold-haired, excellently bright, Whom Matarisvan stablished, dweller in the heaven, meet for high praise and holy, sage and true to Law.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: As pure and swift of course, beholder of the light, who stands in heaven's bright sphere a sign, who wakes at dawn, Agni, the head of heaven, whom none may turn aside-to him the Powerful with mighty prayer we seek.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The cheerful Priest, the pure, in whom no guile is found, Friend of the House, praise-worthy, dear to all mankind, Fair to behold for beauty like a splendid car,- Agni the Friend of men we ever seek for wealth.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To him who shines afar, Vaisvanara, shall bards give precious things that he may go on certain paths: For Agni the Immortal serves the Deities, and therefore never breaks their everlasting laws.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He, wondrous envoy, goes between the earth and heaven, firm seated as the Herald, great High Priest of men. He compasseth with rays the lofty dwelling-place, Agni, sent forward by the Gods, enriched with piayer.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Sages shall glorify Agni with earnest thoughts, ensign of sacrifice, who fills the synod full: In whom the singers have stored up their holy acts to him the worshipper looks for joy and happiness.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Sire of sacrifice, great God of holy bards, Agni, the measure and the symbol of the priests, Hath entered heaven and earth that show in varied form: the Sage whom many love rejoiceth in his might.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Bright Agni with the bright car, Lord of green domains, Vaisvanara dweller in the floods, who finds the light, Pervading, swift and wild, encompassed round with powers, him very glorious have the Gods established here.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Agni, together with the Gods and Manu's folk by thought extending sacrifice in varied form, Goes, car-borne, to and fro with those who crown each rite, the fleet, the Household Friend, who turns the curse aside.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Sing, Agni, for long life to us and noble sons: teem thou with plenty, shine upon us store of food. Increase the great man's strength, thou ever-vigilant: thou, longing for the Gods, knowest their hymns full well.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Mighty One, Lord of the people and their guest, the leader of their thoughts, devoted Friend of priests, Our solemn rites' announcer, Jatavedas, men with worship ever praise, with urgings for their weal.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Agni the God resplendent, giver of great joy, hath on his lovely car compassed the lands with, might. Let us with pure laudations in his house approach the high laws of the nourisher of multitudes.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I celebrate thy glories, O Vaisvanara, wherewith thou, O farsighted God, has found the light. Thou filledst at thy birth both worlds, the earth and heaven: all this, O Agni, hast thou compassed of thyself.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: By his great skill the Sage alone hath brought to pass a great deed, mightier than Vaisvanara's wondrous acts. Agni sprang into being, magnifying both his Parents, Heaven and Earth, rich in prolific seed.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: BE friendly with each kindled log of fuel, with every flash bestow the boon of riches. Bring thou the Gods, O God, unto our worship: serve, well-inclined, as Friend thy friends, O Agni.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Agni whom daily Varuna and Mitra the Gods bring thrice a day to this our worship, Tanunapat, enrich with meath our service that dwells with holy oil, that offers honour.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The thought that bringeth every boon proceedeth to worship first the Priest of the libation, That we may greet the Strong One with our homage. Urged, may he bring the Gods, best Sacrificer.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: On high your way to sacrifice was made ready; the radiant flames went upward to the regions. Full in the midst of heaven the Priest is seated: strew we the sacred grass where Gods may rest them.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Claiming in mind the seven priests' burnt oblations, inciting all, they came in settled order. To this our sacrifice approach the many who show in hero beauty at assemblies.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Night and Dawn, lauded, hither come together, both smiling, different are their forms in colour, That Varuna and Mitra may accept us, and Indra, girt by Maruts, with his glories.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I crave the grace of heaven's two chief Invokers: the seven swift steeds joy in their wonted manner. These speak of truth, praising the truth eternal, thinking on Order as the guards of Order.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May Bharati with all her Sisters, Ila accordant with the Gods, with immortal Agni, Sarasvati with all her kindred Rivers, come to this grass, Three Goddesses, and seat them.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Well pleased with us do thou O God, O Tvastar, give ready issue to our procreant vigour, Whence springs the hero, powerful, skilled in action, lover of Gods, adjuster of the press-stones.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Send to the Gods the oblation, Lord of Forests; and let the Immolator, Agni, dress it. He as the truer Priest shall offer worship, for the Gods' generations well he knoweth.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Come thou to us, O Agni, duly kindled, together with the potent Gods and Indra. On this our grass sit Aditi, happy Mother, and let our Hail delight the Gods Immortal.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: AGNI who shines against the Dawns is wakened. The holy Singer who precedes the sages. With far-spread lustre, kindled by the pious, the Priest hath thrown both gates of darkness open.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Agni hath waxen mighty by laudations, to be adored with hymns of those who praise him. Loving the varied shows of holy Order at the first flush of dawn he shines as envoy.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Amid men's homes hath Agni been established, fulfilling with the Law, Friend, germ of waters. Loved and adored, the height he hath ascended, the Singer, object of our invocations.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Agni is Mitra when enkindled duly, Mitra as Priest, Varuna, Jatavedas; Mitra as active minister, and House-Friend, Mitra of flowing rivers and of mountains.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Earth's, the Bird's dear lofty place he guardeth, he guardeth in his might the course of Surya, Guardeth the Seven-headed in the centre, guardeth sublime the Deities enjoyment.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The skillful God who knows all forms of knowledge made for himself a fair form, meet for worship. This Agni guards with care that never ceases the Sonia's skin, the Bird's place rich in fatness.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Agni hath entered longingly the longing shrine rich with fatness, giving easy access. Resplendent, pure, sublime and purifying, again, again he renovates his Mothers.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Born suddenly, by plants he grew to greatness, when tender shoots with holy oil increased him, Like waters lovely when they hasten downward may Agni in his Parents' lap protect us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Extolled, the Strong shone forth with kindled fuel to the earth's centre, to the height of heaven. May Agni, Friend, adorable Matarisvan, as envoy bring the Gods unto our worship.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Best of all luminaries lofty Agni supported with his flame the height of heaven, When, far from Bhrgus, Matarisvan kindled the oblation-bearer where he lay in secret.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: As holy food, Agni to thine invoker give wealth in cattle, lasting, rich in marvels. To us be born a son and spreading offspring. Agni, be this thy gracious will to us-word.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: URGED on by deep devotion, O ye singers, bring, pious ones, the God-approaching ladle. Borne onward to the right it travels eastward, and, filled with oil, to Agni bears oblation.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou at thy birth didst fill both earth and heaven, yea, Most Adorable, thou didst exceed them. Even through the heaven's and through the earth's expanses let thy swift seven tongued flames roll on, O Agni.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Both Heaven and Earth and Gods who should be worshipped establish thee as Priest for every dwelling, Whenever human families, God-devoted, bringing oblations; laud thy splendid lustre.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Firm in the Gods' home is the Mighty seated, between vast Heaven and Earth the well-beloved- Those Cows who yield, unharmed, their nectar, Spouses of the Far-Strider, ever young, united.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Great are the deeds of thee, the Great, O Agni: thou by thy power hast spread out earth and heaven. As soon as thou wast born thou wast an envoy, thou, Mighty One, was Leader of the people.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Bind to the pole with cords of holy Order the long-maned ruddy steeds who sprinkle fatness. Bring hither, O thou God, all Gods together: provide them noble worship, Jatavedas.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Even from the sky thy brilliant lights shone hither: still hast thou beamed through many a radiant morning, That the Gods praised their joyous Herald's labour eagerly burning, Agni, in the forests.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Gods who take delight in air's wide region, or those the dwellers in heaven's realm of brightness, Or those, the Holy, prompt to hear, our helpers, who, car borne, turn their horses hither, Agni---
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With these, borne on one ear, Agni, approach us, or borne on many, for thy steeds are able. Bring, with their Dames, the Gods, the Three and-Thirty, after thy Godlike nature, and be joyful.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He is the Priest at whose repeated worship even wide Heaven and Earth sing out for increase. They fair and true and holy coming forward stand at his sacrifice who springs from Order.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: As holy food, Agni, to thine invoker give wealth in cattle, lasting, rich in marvels. To us be born a son and spreading offspring. Agni, be this thy gracious will to usward.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: THE seven tones risen from the whitebacked viand have made their way between the pair of Mothers. Both circumjacent Parents come together to yield us length of days they hasten forward.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Male who dwells in heaven hath Mares and Milch kine: he came to Goddesses who bring sweet treasure. To thee safe resting in the seat of Order the Cow alone upon her way proceedeth.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Wise Master, wealthy finder-out of riches, he mounted those who may with case be guided. He, dark-backed, manifold with varied aspect, hath made them burst forth from their food the brush-wood.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Strength-giving streams bear hither him eternal, fain to support the mighty work. of Tvastar. He, flashing in his home with all his members, hath entered both the worlds as they were single.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: They know the red Bull's blessing, and are joyful under the flaming-coloured Lord's dominion: They who give shine from heaven with fair effulgence, whose lofty song like Ila must be honoured.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Yea, by tradition from the ancient sages they brought great strength from the two mighty Parents, To where the singer's Bull, the night's dispeller, after his proper law hath waxen stronger.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Seven holy singers guard with five Adhvaryus the Bird's beloved firmly-settled station. The willing Bulls, untouched by old, rejoice them: as Gods themselves the ways of Gods they follow.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I crave the grace of heaven's two chief Invokers: the seven swift steeds joy in their wonted manner. These speak of truth, praising the Truth Eternal, thinking on Order as the guards of Order.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The many seek the great Steed as a stallion: the reins obey the Lord of varied colour. O heavenly Priest, most pleasant, full of wisdom, bring the great Gods to us, and Earth and Heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Rich Lord, the Mornings have gleamed forth in splendour, fair-rayed, fair-speaking, worshipped with all viands, Yea, with the glory of the earth, O Agni. Forgive us, for our weal, e'en sin committed.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: As holy food, Agni, to thine invoker, give wealth in cattle, lasting, rich in marvels. To us be born a son, and spreading offspring Agni, be this thy gracious will to usward.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: GOD-SERVING men, O Sovran of the Forest, with heavenly meath at sacrifice anoint thee. Grant wealth to us when thou art standing upright as when reposing on this Mother's bosom.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Set up to eastward of the fire enkindled, accepting prayer that wastes not, rich in hero. Driving far from us poverty and famine, lift thyself up to bring us great good fortune.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Lord of the Forest, raise. thyself up on the loftiest spot of earth. Give splendour, fixt and measured well, to him who brings the sacrifice.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Well-robed, enveloped he is come, the youthful: springing to life his glory waxeth greater. Contemplative in mind and God-adoring, sages of high intelligence upraise him.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Sprung up he rises in the days' fair weather, increasing in the men-frequented synod. With song the wise and skillful consecrate him: his voice the God-adoring singer utters. 6, Ye whom religious men have firmly planted; thou Forest Sovran whom the axe hath fashioned,- Let those the Stakes divine which here are standing be fain to grant us wealth with store of children.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O men who lift the ladles up, these hewn and planted in the ground, Bringing a blessing to the field, shall bear our precious gift to Gods.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Adityas, Rudras, Vasus, careful leaders, Earth, Heaven, and Prthivi and Air's mid-region, Accordant Deities shall bless our worship and make our sacrifice's ensign lofty.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Like swan's that flee in lengthened line, the Pillars have come to us arrayed in brilliant colour. They, lifted up on high, by sages, eastward, go forth as Gods to the God's dwelling-places.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Those Stakes upon the earth with rings that deck them seem to the eye like horns of horned creatures; Or, as upraised by priests in invocation, let them assist us in the rush to battle.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Lord of the Wood, rise with a hundred branches. with thousand branches may we rise to greatness, Thou whom this hatchet, with an edge well whetted for great felicity, hath brought before us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: WE as thy friends have chosen thee, mortals a God, to be our help, The Waters' Child, the blessed, the resplendent One, victorious and beyond compare.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Since thou delighting in the woods hast gone unto thy mother streams, Not to be scorned, Agni, is that return of thine when from afar thou now art here.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O'er pungent smoke host thou prevailed, and thus art thou benevolent. Some go before, and others round about thee sit, they in whose friendship thou hast place.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Him who had passed beyond his foes, beyond continual pursuits, Him the unerring Ones, observant, found in floods, couched like a lion in his lair.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Him wandering at his own free will, Agni here hidden from our view, Him Matarisvan brought to us from far away produced by friction, from the Gods.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Bearer of Oblations, thus mortals received thee from the Gods, Whilst thou, the Friend of man, guardest each sacrifice with thine own power, Most Youthful One.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Amid thy wonders this is good, yea, to the simple is it clear, When gathered round about thee, Agni, lie the herds where thou art kindled in the morn.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Offer to him who knows fair rites, who burns with purifying glow, Swift envoy, active, ancient, and adorable: serve ye the God attentively.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Three times a hundred Gods and thrice a thousand, and three times ten and nine have worshipped Agni, For him spread sacred grass, with oil bedewed him, and stablished him as Priest and Sacrificer.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: THEE Agni, God, Imperial Lord of all mankind, do mortal men With understanding kindle at the sacrifice.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: They laud thee in their solemn rites, Agni, as Minister and Priest, Shine forth in thine own home as guardian of the Law.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He, verily, who honours thee with fuel, Knower of all life, He, Agni! wins heroic might, he prospers well.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Ensign of sacrifices, he, Agni, with Gods is come to us, Decked by the seven priests, to him who bringeth gifts.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To Agni, the Invoking Priest, offer your best, your lofty speech, To him Ordainer-like who brings the light of songs.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Let these our hymns make Agni grow, whence, meet for laud, he springs to life, To mighty strength and great possession, fair to see.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Best Sacrificer, bring the Gods, O Agni, to the pious man: A joyful Priest, thy splendour drive our foes afar
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: As such, O Purifier, shine on us heroic glorious might: Be nearest Friend to those who laud thee, for their weal.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: So, wakeful, versed in sacred hymns, the holy singers kindly thee. Oblation-bearer, deathless, cherisher of strength.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: AGNI is Priest, the great High Priest of sacrifice, most swift in act: He knows the rite in constant course.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Oblation-bearer, deathless, well inclined, an eager messenger, Agni comes nigh us with the thought.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Ensign of sacrifice from of old, Agni well knoweth with his thought To prosper this man's aim and hope.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Agni, illustrious from old time, the Son of Strength who knows all life, The Gods have made to their Priest.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Infallible is Agni, he who goes before the tribes of men, A chariot swift and ever new.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Strength of the Gods which none may harm, subduing all his enemies, Agni is mightiest in fame.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: By offering sacred food to him the mortal worshipper obtains. A home from him whose light makes pure.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: From Agni, by our hymns, may we gain all things that bring happiness, Singers of him who knows all life.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Agni, in our deeds of might may we obtain all precious things: The Gods are centred all in thee.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: MOVED, Indra-Agni, by our hymn, come to the juice, the precious dew: Drink ye thereof, impelled by song.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Indra-Agni, with the man who lauds you comes the wakening rite: So drink ye both this juice assured.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Through force of sacrifice I choose Indra-Agni who love the wise: With Sorna let these sate them here.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Indra and Agni I invoke, joint-victors, bounteous, unsubdued, Foe-slayers, best to win the spoil.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Indra and Agni, singers skilled in melody hymn you, bringing lauds: I choose you for the sacred food.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Indra and Agni, ye cast down the ninety forts which DAsas held, Together, with one mighty deed.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To Indra-Agni reverent thoughts go forward from the holy task Along the path of sacred Law.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Indra-Agni, powers are yours, and dwellings and delightful food Good is your readiness to act.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Indra and Agni, in your deeds of might ye deck heaven's lucid realms: Famed is that hero strength of yours.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To Agni, to this God of yours I sing aloud with utmost power. May he come to us with the Gods, and sit, best Offerer, on the grass.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Holy, whose are earth and heaven, and succour waits upon his strength; Him men who bring oblations laud, and they who wish to gain, for grace.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He is the Sage who guides these men, Leader of sacred rites is he. Him your own Agni, serve ye well, who winneth and bestoweth wealth.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: So may the gracious Agni grant most goodly shelter for our use; Whence in the heavens or in the floods he shall pour wealth upon our lands.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The singers kindle him, the Priest, Agni the Lord of tribes of men, Resplendent and without a peer through his own excellent designs.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Help us, thou Brahman, best of all invokers of the Gods in song. Beam, Friend of Maruts, bliss on us, O Agni, a most liberal God.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Yea, grant us treasure thousandfold with children and with nourishment, And, Agni, splendid hero strength, exalted, wasting not away.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: THE pleasant Priest is come into the synod, true, skilled in sacrifice, most wise, Ordainer. Agni, the Son of Strength, whose car is lightning, whose hair is flame, hath shown on earth his lustre.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To thee I offer reverent speech: accept it: to thee who markest it, victorious, faithful! Bring, thou who knowest, those who know, and seat thee amid the sacred grass, for help, O Holy.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Two who show their vigour, Night and Morning, by the wind's paths shall haste to thee O Agni. When men adorn the Ancient with oblations, these seek, as on two chariot-seats, the dwelling.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To thee, strong Agni! Varuna and Mitra and all the Maruts sang a song of triumph, What time unto the people's lands thou camest, spreading them as the Sun of men, with lustre.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Approaching with raised hands and adoration, we have this day fulfilled for thee thy longing. Worship the Gods with most devoted spirit, a Priest with no unfriendly thought, O Agni.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: For, Son of Strength, from thee come many succours, and powers abundant that a God possesses. Agni, to us with speech that hath no falsehood grant riches, real, to be told in thousands.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Whatever, God, in sacrifice we mortals have wrought is all for thee, strong, wise of purpose! Be thou the Friend of each good chariot's master. All this enjoy thou here, immortal Agni.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: RESPLENDENT with thy wide-extending lustre, dispel the terrors of the fiends who hate us May lofty Agni be my guide and shelter, the easily-invoked, the good Protector.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Be thou To us, while now the morn is breaking, be thou a guardian when the Sun hath mounted.. Accept, as men accept a true-born infant, my laud, O Agni nobly born in body.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Bull, who beholdest men, through many mornings, among the dark ones shine forth red, O Agni. Lead us, good Lord, and bear us over trouble: Help us who long, Most Youthful God, to riches.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Shine forth, a Bull invincible, O Agni, winning by conquest all the forts and treasures, Thou Jatavedas who art skilled in guiding, the chief high saving sacrifice's Leader.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Lighting Gods hither, Agni, wisest Singer, bring thou to us many and flawless shelters. Bring vigour, like a car that gathers booty: bring us, O Agni, beauteous Earth and Heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Swell, O thou Bull and give those powers an impulse, e'en Earth and Heaven who yield their milk in plenty, Shining, O God, with Gods in clear effulgence. Let not a mortal's evil will obstruct us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Agni, as holy food to thine invoker, give wealth in cattle, lasting, rich in marvels. To us be born a son and spreading offspring. Agni, be this thy gracious will to us-ward.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: THIS Agni is the Lord of great felicity and hero Strength; Lord of wealth in herds of kine; Lord of the battles with the foe.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Wait, Maruts, Heroes, upon him the Prosperer in whom is bliss-increasing wealth; Who in fights ever conquer evil-hearted men, who overcome the enemy.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: As such, O Agni, deal us wealth and hero might, O Bounteous One! Most lofty, very glorious, rich in progeny, free from disease and full of power.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He who made all that lives, who passes all in might, who orders service to the Gods, He works among the Gods, he works in hero strength, yea, also in the praise of men.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Give us not up to indigence, Agni, nor want of hero sons, Nor, Son of Strength, to lack of cattle, nor to blame. Drive. thou our enemies away.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Help us to strength, blest Agni! rich in progeny, abundant, in our sacrifice. Flood us with riches yet more plenteous, bringing weal, with high renown, most Glorious One!
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: DULY enkindled after ancient customs, bringing all treasures, he is balmed with unguents,- Flame-haired, oil-clad, the purifying Agni, skilled in fair rites, to bring the Gods for worship.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: As thou, O Agni, skillful Jatavedas, hast sacrificed as Priest of Earth, of Heaven, So with this offering bring the Gods, and prosper this sacrifice today as erst for Manu.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Three are thy times of life, O Jatavedas, and the three mornings are thy births, O Agni. With these, well-knowing, grant the Gods' kind favour, and help in stir aid stress the man who worships.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Agni most bright and fair with song we honour, yea, the adorable, O Jatavedas. Thee, envoy, messenger, oblation-bearer, the Gods have made centre of life eternal.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: That Priest before thee, yet more skilled in worship, stablished of old, healthgiver by his nature,- After his custom offer, thou who knowest, and lay our sacrifice where Gods may taste it.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: AGNI, be kind to us when we approach thee good as a friend to friend, as sire and mother. The races of mankind are great oppressors burn up malignity that strives against us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Agni, burn up the unfriendly who are near us, burn thou the foeman's curse who pays no worship. Burn, Vasu, thou who markest well, the foolish: let thine eternal nimble beams surround thee.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With fuel, Agni, and with oil, desirous, mine offering I present for strength and conquest, With prayer, so far as I have power, adoring-this hymn divine to gain a hundred treasures.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Give with thy glow, thou Son of Strength, when lauded, great vital power to those who toil to serve thee. Give richly, Agni, to the Visvamitras in rest and stir. Oft have we decked thy body.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Give us, O liberal Lord, great store of riches, for, Agni, such art thou when duly kindled. Thou in the happy singer's home bestowest, amply with arms extended, things of beauty.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: How, quick, sage, infallible, all-knowing, I choose to be our Priest at this oblation. In our Gods' service he, best skilled, shall worship: may he obtain us boons for strength and riches.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Agni, to thee I lift the oil-fed ladle, bright, with an offering, bearing our oblation. From the right hand, choosing the Gods' attendance, he with rich presents hath arranged the worship.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Of keenest spirit is the man thou aidest give us good offspring, thou who givest freely. In power of wealth most rich in men. O Agni, of thee, the Good, may we sing forth fair praises.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Men as they worship thee the God, O Agni, have set on thee full many a brilliant, aspect. So bring Most Youthful One, the Gods' asserrigly, the Heavenly Host which thou to-day shalt honour.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When Gods anoint thee Priest at their oblation, and seat thee for thy task as Sacrificer, O Agni, be thou here our kind defender, and to ourselves vouchsafe the gift of glory.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: WITH lauds at break of morn the priest invoketh Agni, Dawn, Dadhikras, and both the Asvins. With one consent the Gods whose light is splendid, longing to taste our sacrifice, shall hear us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Three are thy powers, O Agni, three thy stations, three are thy tongues, yea, many, Child of Order! Three bodies hast thou which the Gods delight in: with these protect our hymns with care unceasing.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Agni, many are the names thou bearest, immortal, God, Divine, and Jatavedas. And many charms of charmers, All-Inspirer! have they laid in thee, Lord of true attendants!
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Agni, like Bhaga, leads the godly people, he who is true to Law and guards the seasons. Ancient, all-knowing, he the Vrtra-slayer shall bear the singer safe through every trouble.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I call on Savitar the God, on Morning, Brhaspati, and Dadhikras, and Agni, On Varuna and Mitra, on the Asvins, Bhaga, the Vasus, Rudras and Adityas.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: SET this our sacrifice among the Immortals: be pleased with these our presents, Jatavedas. O Priest, O Agni, sit thee down before us, and first enjoy the drops of oil and fatness.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: For thee, O Purifier, flow the drops of fatness rich in oil. After thy wont vouchsafe to us the choicest boon that Gods may feast.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Agni, Most Excellent! for thee the Sage are drops that drip with oil. Thou art enkindled as the best of Seers. Help thou the sacrifice.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To thee, O Agni, mighty and resistless, to thee stream forth the drops of oil and fatness. With great light art thou come, O praised by poets! Accept our offering, O thou Sage.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Fatness exceeding rich, extracted from the midst,-this as our gift we offer thee. Excellent God, the drops run down upon thy skin. Deal them to each among the Gods.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: THIS is that Agni whence the longing Indra took the pressed Soma deep within his body. Winner of spoils in thousands, like a courser, with praise art thou exalted, Jatavedas.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: That light of thine in heaven and earth, O Agni, in plants, O Holy One, and in the waters, Wherewith thou hast spread wide the air's mid-region-bright is that splendour, wavy, man-beholding.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Agni, to the sea of heaven thou goest: thou hast called hither Gods beheld in spirit. The waters, too, come hither, those up yonder in the Sun's realm of light, and those beneath it.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Let fires that dwell in mist, combined with those that have their home in floods, Guileless accept our sacrifice, great viands free from all disease.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Agni, as holy food to thine invoker give wealth in cattle, lasting, rich in marvels. To us be born a son and spreading offspring. Agni, be this thy gracious will to us-ward.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: RUBBED into life, well stablished in the dwelling, Leader of sacrifice, the Sage, the youthful, Here in the wasting fuel Jatavedas, eternal, hath assumed immortal being.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Both Bharatas, Devasravas, Devavata, have strongly rubbed to life effectual Agni. O Agni, look thou forth with ample riches: be, every day, bearer of food to feed us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Him nobly born of old the fingers ten produced, him whom his Mothers counted dear. Praise Devavata's Agni, thou Devasravas, him who shall be the people's Lord.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He set thee in the earth's most lovely station, in Ila's place, in days of fair bright weather. On man, on Apaya, Agni! on the rivers Drsadvati, Sarasvati, shine richly.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Agni, as holy food to thine invoker give wealth in cattle, lasting, rich in marvels. To us be born a son and spreading offspring Agni, be this thy gracious will to us-ward
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary
